repair_triage.estimate_boundary: Potentially exceeds one-hour audit diversion; policy-sensitive repair left explicit.

findings.status: source-confirmed; not repaired
findings.title: Unix endpoint startup cleanup can unlink an ordinary file

findings.scope: Current-source branch analysis plus native Linux primitive experiment in WSL Ubuntu. The Python policy probe does not execute Rust/Tokio or launch Djinn. Effect is deletion at a configured endpoint path accessible to the process; no remote attacker or cross-user privilege claim.

repair_triage.reason: Installer already checks socket type, uid and inode, whereas resident agent and shared door helper duplicate weaker policies. findings.status: source-confirmed; not repaired
findings.title: Resident emits listening and ready before polling the app and browser brokers that bind their doors
findings.evidence: Async broker futures are constructed and pinned, status.ready is set and a ready event emitted, then the first select polls them. Binding occurs inside the async serve path. findings.status: source-confirmed; not repaired
findings.title: Identity resource read-through bypasses the disclosed and released resource boundary
findings.evidence: bytes_for checks staged and released maps, then calls reader for any requested hash and caches the result. The resident composer supplies host.blobs().get_bytes(hash) without checking a disclosed card/media set or release authorization. Correct session membership is checked separately. The existing read-through test requests an unstaged hash before any snapshot; the release-boundary test installs no reader.
findings.scope: Source-confirmed current product composition when personal sync supplies a reader. An admitted local client must know a blob hash. No unauthenticated remote access, guessing capability or vault-secret exposure is established. The transport blob store's full contents and other consumers remain under review.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; resource authorization owner must be explicit
repair_triage.reason: Define one allowed set covering disclosed card/media dependencies and accepted transfers, enforce it before read-through/cache access, and qualify grant retirement across cached and newly opened sessions. Simply disabling the reader would break real receipt captures.
repair_triage.estimate_boundary: Potentially exceeds one-hour audit diversion because projection dependencies, blob custody and transfer grants cross owners.

findings.status: source-confirmed; not repaired
findings.title: Read cache admits a single resource larger than its advertised 64 MiB budget
findings.evidence: admit_fetched evicts while fetched_bytes + size exceeds READ_CACHE_BUDGET, but breaks when the order queue is empty and then inserts the oversized blob anyway. The existing bound test uses five quarter-budget blobs and does not cover one over-budget blob.
findings.scope: Source-confirmed retention-budget violation after a reader returns an oversized Vec. Peak whole-blob allocation already happens in the reader; a cache fix alone cannot make the complete path streaming or bounded. No actual oversized product-store read was run in this pass.

repair_triage.disposition: bounded candidate repair documented
repair_triage.reason: Choose uncached serving versus explicit oversized-resource refusal, preserve chunk reads and add a single-oversized-blob control. This is independent of Q045 authorization.

findings.status: source-confirmed; not repaired
findings.title: Accepted transfer decisions are volatile despite the immediate-durability claim
findings.evidence: Accepted is returned after pushing into Arc<Mutex<Vec<TransferDecision>>>. The watcher drains it with mem::take, attempts work later, and logs/drops failures. No durable write precedes the reply. The offer remains available for another explicit acceptance, as the watcher documentation states.
findings.scope: Source-confirmed false persistence claim about the decision. Accepted need not mean completed transfer, and the code explicitly separates decision from fetch. Crash-loss between reply and work follows from volatile ownership; no fresh-process fault injection was run.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; select promised acceptance contract
repair_triage.reason: If acceptance is durable, persist its state before reply and retire only under an explicit completion/failure policy. Otherwise correct the documentation and expose queued/failed states. Do not equate an in-memory decision queue with the durable source graph.

findings.status: repaired; source reviewed; non-Windows execution not performed

findings.status: source-confirmed; not repaired
findings.title: Daemon reservoir registration retains a catalog ownership cycle that embedded shutdown explicitly breaks
findings.evidence: Daemon creates MereRoutes holding an AppEndpointCatalog clone, then registers a reservoir factory in that same catalog capturing Some(routes). The catalog owns its factories, so dropping outer references leaves catalog -> factory -> MereRoutes -> catalog. The factory also retains the reservoir Shared and the catalog's other route factories. Main cancels/joins tasks before resident.shutdown, but does not clear this catalog. EmbeddedOwner explicitly clears its catalog after cancellation with a comment identifying this exact cycle.
findings.scope: Source-confirmed ownership cycle when the daemon's reservoir is open and routes are composed. ReservoirLane::close and published-site shutdown use Arc::try_unwrap and therefore can refuse while these factories remain retained; shutting down the OS process ultimately releases its handles. No current-binary shutdown or public-API cycle reproduction was executed in this pass. Do not claim silent successful shutdown: main propagates shutdown errors. The fully read two-process library daemon fixture explicitly clears its catalog, so its clean-release assertion cannot qualify the full binary's omitted cleanup. That integration test was not executed in this pass.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; share the embedded cleanup boundary with daemon shutdown
repair_triage.reason: Retain an explicit catalog cleanup handle across the serving scope, stop borrowers, clear factory cycles, then perform owner release checks. Qualify normal stop, bind/startup failure and route-serving failure for both daemon and embedded modes before treating one cleanup implementation as complete.
repair_triage.estimate_boundary: Runtime lifecycle qualification across modes may exceed the requested one-hour audit diversion limit.

findings.status: source-confirmed; not repaired
findings.title: Failed initial pre-key publication is not retried on the next open despite the recovery claim
findings.evidence: GraphKeyGroup::open persists the new session and bundle before returning publish=Some, and returns publish=None for an existing session. PersonalSyncHost only publishes when that Option is Some, logs an initial author/encoding failure and continues, with a comment saying the next open tries again. Reopening the already-persisted session cannot enter that publication branch. The existing graph-key reopen test explicitly expects publish=None.
findings.scope: Source-confirmed missing automatic retry after encoding or pre-commit author failure, where the pre-key never reached durable lane storage; actual I/O/lane failure was not injected. author commits before joined.publish, so a later broadcast error can leave a stored event recoverable through sync and is not evidence of a missing durable pre-key. Manual relay of the retained public bundle is a separate recovery path, particularly for intentional receive-only devices. No claim that every ordinary startup or pairing fails.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; bind publication retry to retained lane evidence
repair_triage.reason: Preserve the same session/bundle, detect whether its exact pre-key reached the durable lane, and retry missing publication without minting another session or adding duplicate pre-key traffic on every restart. Cover publication failure, read-only pairing-facts startup and receive-only relay semantics.
repair_triage.estimate_boundary: Durable bootstrap/publication qualification may exceed the one-hour audit diversion limit.

findings.status: repaired-verified

findings.scope: Reproduced and repaired on this Windows checkout. The fixture still equals HEAD byte for byte. This corrects the checkout contract for an exact text fixture; it does not establish broader projection or custody safety.

repair_triage.disposition: contained repair implemented and verified

findings.status: classifier overclaim reproduced; not repaired
findings.title: Knot's no-copy residue success excludes intermittent and same-size additional copies
findings.evidence: The exact own_blocks source was compiled in a standalone native Rust harness. A persistent unique allocation size is reported as its positive control. A copy seen in only one of five host runs, a persistent copy matching one baseline observation, and additional same-size copies are all discarded. The sync-host gate only fails on the resulting set, then prints Knot leaves no copy beyond its bind/join baseline.
findings.scope: Exact classifier on synthetic already-observed allocation records, not execution of Knot, its allocator tracker or a real seed leak. Retain every observed hit, qualify baseline attribution and multiplicity, and state the heap/arming window and excluded upstream cases. findings.status: reproduced through public guard and Windows process environment; not repaired
findings.title: Windows environment case aliases bypass the testkit's root and forbidden-variable checks
findings.evidence: Guard checks BTreeMap names with exact-case lookup. The canonical LOCALAPPDATA outside-root and SSH_AUTH_SOCK standard-agent controls are refused. An environment-only child composed with the same env_clear/envs operations sees the outside-root value and the standard-agent name through uppercase Windows lookup.
findings.scope: Native Windows public Guard API plus actual Windows child environment semantics; Resident::env/env_map/guarded_env source confirms this composition path. The outside value was a generated decoy, and the child only read variables: no Djinn, SSH client or endpoint connection, and no real user state touched. Unix variable lookup is case-sensitive and was not tested as vulnerable.

Cover redirected roots, endpoint variables, forbidden names and permitted harness-role/askpass additions; the current guard is not an arbitrary-variable allowlist.

findings.status: reproduced through public Run finalization; not repaired

Retain failed-run diagnostic records rather than replacing them with a passed summary.

findings.status: reproduced through public Resident::start; not repaired

findings.status: reproduced; documented, not repaired

findings.status: reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.title: Idle notice pushes continue after grant expiry or revocation until a request arrives
findings.evidence: The shared loop polls and writes notices before its only authority check. Idle read timeouts repeat this path without checking authority. A public native notifying-loop diagnostic starts live, receives a first notice, then expires or revokes the real signed grant. After an independent lapse assertion, a newly queued notice still reaches the idle peer. The next valid Close request is refused and terminates with the correct Lapsed result. A live control receives notices and closes normally.
findings.scope: Current public native session loop over Tokio duplex with a constructed admitted session and real signed grant/revocation. No admission handshake, installed resident, remote link or DTLS test. Demonstrates session/epoch/revision notice disclosure and continued endpoint polling, not arbitrary snapshot/resource/intent authorization bypass; request gating still works.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production edits excluded by active audit objective
repair_triage.reason: Apply retained-authority checks to asynchronous output and idle polling as well as inbound requests; define how a quiet peer is told authority lapsed without inventing a request id. Qualify mid-session revocation and expiry across both notice and request lanes.

findings.status: reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.title: Refusing a second client request overwrites the first pending operation
findings.evidence: discover calls core.rediscover before send checks inflight. SessionCore::begin unconditionally replaces Pending. Public diagnostic starts a Close, attempts a second discover and gets the expected still-waiting refusal. The valid Closed response with the original id is then rejected because the core now expects a descriptor. Without the second call, the same close completes. The existing second-request unit test only asserts that the second send errors; it never answers the original request.
findings.scope: Current compiled public client API and encoded NDJSON response, no I/O, browser or product UI. This is local pending-operation corruption after an explicitly refused operation, not request-id spoofing or endpoint authorization bypass. Full core.rs and driver.rs source read; the rest of the client package remains ahead.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production edits excluded by active audit objective
repair_triage.reason: Make starting the core operation and claiming the driver request slot one coordinated transition. Checking only discover early fixes this entry but leaves public core_mut plus begin callers able to overwrite Pending before send refusal. Preserve the original operation after a refused start and exercise its legitimate answer.

findings.status: reproduced through current public client API; documented, not repaired
findings.title: Presentation resolution accepts a different advertised resource and keeps requesting the missing one
findings.evidence: Pending::Resolve remembers session/instance, not its resource request. on_response admits any response ClientState considers advertised and valid, then resolves again. A valid two-item fixture requests item 0; six replies containing the distinct advertised item 1 are accepted and cached, each producing another request for item 0 with the operation still pending. The requested-resource control resolves normally. The blocking adapter drive loop has no additional progress/retry bound. Pending::MediaResource does explicitly compare the requested session/hash.
findings.scope: Current compiled public SessionCore/ClientState on a validated generated snapshot and content-addressed bytes. No actual network or browser denial-of-service run. Hash and session advertisement checks still work; this is reply correlation/liveness failure, not serving an unadvertised resource or foreign endpoint secret.

repair_triage.disposition: open; prior read-only checkpoint, reassess under contained-repair policy
repair_triage.reason: Retain the outstanding ResourceRequest and reject a mismatching session/hash before caching or advancing. Distinguish successful additional resources from a repeated non-progressing answer, and test the same rejection through both adapters.

findings.status: reproduced through current public client API; documented, not repaired
findings.title: Frozen snapshot traversal ignores the explicit item order used by the remote reader
findings.evidence: freeze_snapshot_with_details enumerates sparse table slots directly, while the remote accessibility tree and blocking resolve_all use active_items_in_order. A validated snapshot with item_order [1,0] is read [1,0] remotely and [0,1] frozen; dense-order control agrees. Sparse identity preservation is real, but does not require ignoring the explicit order. Existing sparse test covers tombstones/repeated sources with unreordered slots.
findings.scope: Public native snapshot/freezing/accessibility data APIs. No live screen reader, browser DOM or OS accessibility bridge executed. Demonstrates reading-order divergence on valid source data, not renumbering of identities.

repair_triage.disposition: open; prior read-only checkpoint, reassess under contained-repair policy
repair_triage.reason: Share ordered active-item traversal while retaining InstanceId values, and verify reordered/tombstoned snapshots across interactive, frozen and accessible outputs.

findings.status: reproduced through current public client API; documented, not repaired
findings.title: Remote accessibility exposes items whose own visible flag is false

findings.scope: Current compiled public client functions, generated validated snapshot. No OS accessibility or product action execution. The item was already disclosed in the scene, so this is presentation/action-surface divergence, not a new secret-disclosure or endpoint authorization bypass.

repair_triage.disposition: open; prior read-only checkpoint, reassess under contained-repair policy

findings.status: reproduced through current public client API; documented, not repaired
findings.title: Unexpected remote closure leaves live mount status and a lost request can block rediscovery
findings.evidence: RemoteSession::disconnect clears pending wire state and marks mounted scenes disconnected, but channel_closed only updates strings/link_busy. Diagnostic of a mounted idle session shows outer closed status with MountedScene.status still Live. During initial discovery, channel_closed leaves driver awaiting and in_flight true; rejoined then fails with still waiting on request and queues no discovery. Intentional-disconnect control marks the mount disconnected and sends rediscovery. Existing unexpected-close test checks only the outer status string. Targeted port source routes stream termination to this method without the intentional disconnect step.
findings.scope: Public native RemoteSession plus encoded discovery/mount replies; targeted current port call-site excerpts inspected, full port review remains ahead. No actual browser channel teardown or DTLS rejoin executed. Reproduces lost-request recovery failure and contradictory client status, not a general claim that every reconnect fails.

repair_triage.disposition: open; prior read-only checkpoint, reassess under contained-repair policy
repair_triage.reason: Give all terminal link paths a common state transition that cancels lost operations, clears or qualifies old queued traffic and marks mounts disconnected, while preserving the cached scene for re-admission. Exercise unexpected close and link failure both idle and mid-request; preserve the intentional disconnect control.

findings.status: previously reproduced; bounded wording repair now package-tested
findings.title: Resume receipt calls a full replacement snapshot a diff
findings.evidence: ClientState distinguishes Current, Applied and Resynchronize but SessionCore reduces Current/Applied to Outcome::Changed(true), without preserving whether the reply carried diffs or a full snapshot. RemoteSession labels any true result diff. A public mounted-session diagnostic receives a revision notice and a real ResumeReply::Snapshot at revision 2, applies the replacement, and reports diff · 1 → 2. The scripted board test likewise answers resumes with Snapshot while its test name/assertion says by diff.
findings.scope: Current public RemoteSession driven by encoded NDJSON and validated generated snapshots; no browser or real network. Snapshot recovery itself succeeds correctly. This is false evidence about the recovery mode, not failure to apply a valid snapshot. The separate host real-endpoint test genuinely checks a diff; it was read in the preceding pass, not executed here.

repair_triage.reason: A generic truthful update label avoids introducing a new outcome/protocol API solely for UI wording.

findings.repair: RemoteSession reports updated rather than diff for Outcome::Changed(true). The two scripted board tests are named for the Snapshot replies they actually supply. No exact wire-mode claim is inferred from the boolean outcome.

findings.status: public capture/live-client admission mismatch reproduced; not repaired
findings.title: Validated captures retain presentation metadata the live client rejects
findings.evidence: CaptureWire validation checks the scene, version and optional score/authority generation, but not the presentation sidecar. With valid scene tables, absent-item bindings, duplicate bindings and codec/capability conflicts each pass V1 from_projection, validation, encoding, decoding and resource-availability checks, then V2 lifting/encoding/decoding/availability checks. findings.scope: Current public native APIs on generated fixtures. No persisted user artifact or renderer crash executed. Resource availability callback is a caller assertion, not a byte verifier; this diagnostic supplies the actually present resource hash.

findings.status: public frame/native codec divergence reproduced; not repaired
findings.title: Frame line assembly silently rewrites invalid UTF-8 that native readers reject
findings.evidence: LineAssembler uses String::from_utf8_lossy for complete lines and unterminated tails. A CarrierOutput descriptor containing an invalid byte in its label is rewritten with U+FFFD and successfully decoded as a typed protocol response. Public native LineReader returns InvalidData for those bytes. A valid multibyte UTF-8 value split between pushes is reconstructed correctly and agrees with the native reader. Targeted BrowserSession source passes frame bytes directly through this assembler.
findings.scope: Current public Chirograph assembler/decode and native graphshell-host LineReader over Tokio duplex. Browser path is source-traced, not run in wasm or a real channel. Demonstrates divergent malformed-byte admission and altered data, not a content-hash bypass, authority forgery or valid UTF-8 fragmentation defect.

repair_triage.disposition: open; prior read-only checkpoint, reassess under contained-repair policy
repair_triage.reason: Make complete-line and partial-tail UTF-8 decoding fallible, with the same rejection policy as native readers. Thread the error through browser frame callers and test both invalid-byte locations and split valid codepoints. API/error propagation needs a coordinated pass.

findings.status: public snapshot/diff/trace admission and non-reopenable output reproduced; not repaired
findings.title: Structurally validated scene geometry can serialize successfully into bytes that cannot reopen
findings.evidence: Snapshot validation checks slot/reference/fold/hold structure but no finite geometry. Public from_dense and validate accept NaN/Infinity in item position/scale, footprint width and scene bounds. SceneTrace::new accepts each; serde_json serialization succeeds, writing null for the nonfinite numeric value, but deserializing the emitted snapshot/trace fails. A finite trace control reopens identically. A nonfinite SetBounds diff also returns Applied and commits revision 2, and its accepted trace serializes into bytes that cannot reopen.
findings.scope: Current compiled public Sceno/Scenotime APIs on generated typed data. No product solver, renderer, user archive or remote peer was executed. Malformed numeric values arise before JSON encoding; this is not evidence that JSON decoding accepts NaN syntax. The existing structural validation claims are narrower than full wire round-trip validity; the diagnostic identifies that missing boundary rather than an authorization failure.

repair_triage.disposition: deferred broad repair; one-hour diversion limit
repair_triage.reason: Define and share finite-value admission for all serialized scene geometry, then apply it consistently at from_dense, diff commit, capture and trace boundaries. Preserve explicit zero/degenerate footprint semantics and separately decide permissible negative dimensions/scales. Test serialization/reopening as well as structural validity; do not silently normalize invalid geometry or change source coordinates.
repair_triage.scope_reason: A complete repair spans shared geometry, snapshot/diff admission, portable capture and trace reopening, and downstream solvers. Keep this larger consumer/serialization pass documented rather than fixing one NaN field and claiming all portable scenes valid. Finite admission can be separated from any new negative/degenerate-geometry policy.

findings.related_producer_evidence: Q074 now supplies a finite, JSON-round-trippable Score that produces NaN through public Timeline solve and reaches the same admitted/non-reopenable snapshot path; scenomise_solver_probe_receipt.json.

findings.status: reproduced before repair; repaired and package-tested

findings.title: Removing the last force source leaves its persistent Rapier force active
findings.status: reproduced through public Simulation API; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: After one Boundary tick, clear_forces reports force_count0 but the next velocity grows from-15.719008 to-30.809254; replacing Boundary with strength0 instead decays it to-15.090249. Removing the last AnchorSpring likewise grows velocity from-18.768496 to-36.78625, while a zero-stiffness anchor decays to-18.017756. Identical pre-removal state was checked for Boundary. tick resets persistent Rapier forces only when a built-in/coupling/affinity/anchor/scene-field source remains present, so removing the last source skips clearing its previous accumulator.
findings.scope: Two native CPU Simulation observations with zero-force replacement controls. Public direct API behavior; not evidence that Canvas Still fails, since its host law can install Hold or another force and thereby enter the reset branch. Removal through coupling/affinity/scene-field setters shares the inspected reset condition but was not independently executed.

findings.title: A zero-sized rounded collider panics instead of applying the advertised minimum clamp

findings.evidence: set_node_colliders accepts Ball radius0 and Square half0 via their positive minimum clamps. findings.scope: One native CPU test with direct public setter, two non-rounded controls and catch_unwind. No partial mutation rollback or hosted UI input path was tested. Canvas ordinary footprint admission clamps to a larger range, so this is not a claim its normal resize slider emits zero.

findings.title: The tidal gravity locus stops when the backend tick budget ends
findings.status: reproduced inline and on the actual actor; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: GravityLocus::tidal advances a private sinusoidal clock in apply but inherits wants_tick=false. Both actors were halted and dropped. The source test named a_tidal_locus_never_settles drives Simulation.tick manually and therefore never exercises backend demand.
findings.scope: Two generated native tests, one inline and one actual actor, with the identical force implementation behind a demand-only control. No hosted Canvas or GUI execution. An infinite manual tick loop is not evidence the normal runtime continues scheduling.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits

findings.title: The actor pool can strand queued actors by reusing the same unreserved idle count
findings.status: reproduced through unchanged public Pool.submit; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: submit checks idle==0 but does not reserve a waiting worker against the newly queued job. Two submissions can both see idle1, enqueue two jobs and wake only the same worker. The first native bounded attempt reproduced this: workers1, first actor started and blocked, second actor did not start during the150ms observation; releasing the first let the second run. Both were then released and finished. Busy-worker control waits for the first start before submitting the second and observes workers2 with both started before release. This contradicts the module assertion that growth is race-free and a job is never stranded with every worker busy.
findings.scope: One reproduction plus one control in a generated native harness compiling the original production pool module by path. Up to32 bounded attempts were allowed; first attempt sufficed. No private scheduling/state edits. Original package tests were filtered out. No hosted product actor workflow was executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: bounded queue/worker accounting correction; qualify concurrency before repair
repair_triage.reason: Account for queued reservations when deciding whether available workers can serve admitted long-lived jobs. Preserve a single idle-count transition owner, avoid over-spawn and stranded jobs, and cover multiple submissions against an idle worker. Broader pool shutdown/recovery work should not extend this audit beyond the user one-hour limit.

findings.title: Dropping the last Pool handle leaves its worker threads and state alive indefinitely
findings.status: source-confirmed lifecycle defect; no dedicated native drop probe; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Each spawned worker retains Arc<Inner>, loops forever and waits on Condvar when its queue empties. Pool has no Drop implementation, stop state or shutdown notification, and worker JoinHandles are discarded. Dropping all public Pool clones cannot drop Inner because waiting workers own it; no condition tells those workers to exit. Repeatedly constructing, using and discarding pools therefore retains workers beyond each pool owner lifetime. workers() counts cumulative spawns, not currently live workers after a job panic.
findings.scope: Complete source inspection of all six Armillary files. The pool native probe releases every job; its idle worker threads terminate only when the short-lived probe process exits. No production host drop sequence or dedicated leak/panic test was executed. Peak-concurrency bounds apply only to a deliberately retained single pool and do not establish reclamation of discarded pools.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: broader lifecycle policy; may exceed one-hour audit diversion limit
repair_triage.reason: Choose explicit owner shutdown/drain behavior, treatment of long-lived jobs and worker panic recovery. Keep public-handle lifetime distinct from worker-owned state; avoid a last-handle test based on raw Arc strong counts that also include workers. Do not block the read-only audit on a lifecycle redesign.

findings.title: Analytic field gradients ignore spatial variation of Gaussian centres and linear normals
findings.status: reproduced through current public Numen evaluator; documented, not repaired
findings.source: crates/conatus/numen/src/eval.rs:grad_scalar Gaussian and Linear; field_ast.rs:Gaussian.center and Linear.normal
findings.evidence: The portable AST allows arbitrary vector expressions for center and normal. Linear normal=Coord evaluates x*x+y*y, but grad_scalar at(3,4) returns(3,4), not(6,8). Registering that same scalar and differentiating Sample switches to finite differences and returns(5.9995646,8.000374). Gaussian center=Coord+(1,0), sigma10 has constant value0.99501246, yet the analytic gradient returns(0.009950125,0) while finite differences return(0,0). Constant-normal and fixed-center controls are correct. The analytic branches omit the derivative of their vector child; Burn restricts those branches to ConstVec and refuses unsupported dynamic forms.
findings.scope: Two generated native tests against a freshly built default Numen library; public AST/evaluation/registry APIs only. Seiche CouplingForce source calls this gradient for scalar physical responses, but no fresh Seiche/Canvas force or GPU execution was performed. Default Numen library suite65 tests passes and does not cover these dynamic-child cases.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained analytic eligibility correction; generalized derivatives broader
repair_triage.reason: Use the constant-child formula only when spatial constancy is established, otherwise use the existing finite-difference path or typed refusal consistent with the evaluator contract. A shared derivative/AST analysis across CPU, Burn, animation detection and budget accounting can exceed the user one-hour limit; document that larger work.

findings.title: Named registry allocation silently overwrites an explicit field identity
findings.status: reproduced through public FieldRegistry API; documented, not repaired

The new field returns the imported id, len remains1 and an existing Sample changes from7 to9. Fresh named entries get distinct ids, and same-name update deliberately reuses its id in controls. The bug is unrelated-name allocation colliding with the explicitly seeded identity domain.
findings.scope: One generated native test using unchanged public API and a valid nil UUID; no reserved-nil rule exists in the inspected type. Both paths are public but no single production host mixing them was executed. Graph-to-Seiche bridge source seeds explicit IDs; Canvas authoring helpers use named allocation on projections. Do not claim a reproduced production graph overwrite.

repair_triage.reason: Skip already occupied explicit IDs when allocating a fresh name, or separate/admit identity domains while retaining canonical graph IDs. Preserve intentional same-name updates and WASM-safe deterministic allocation; cover imported nonzero IDs and mixed insertion order when repaired.

findings.title: LightBlock validates positive-infinite intensities despite its finite-value contract
findings.status: source-confirmed public validation defect; no native Tenant probe; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The is_valid contract says every value is finite. Sun, ambient and point intensities are admitted with intensity>=0 only; positive infinity satisfies that predicate. Their colors/positions are checked with is_finite and point radius has a separate finite check, so the missing intensity guard is specific. set_lights trusts is_valid before forwarding intensities to lights and ambient. The source test rejects NaN ambient but does not test positive infinity.
findings.scope: All eight Tenant source files read. No Tenant build, value probe, adapter, GPU frame or consumer execution was performed. This is source-confirmed boolean admission, not evidence of a rendered artifact, device loss or observed shader failure.

repair_triage.size: contained shared intensity admission repair
repair_triage.reason: Require each intensity to be finite and non-negative before state mutation, retaining existing no-change refusal semantics. Include positive/negative infinity and finite controls for all three light kinds. Broader normalization, transform and renderer gates remain separately documented.

findings.title: Engine system failure consumes unexecuted time and discards applied-change publication
findings.status: reproduced through public CPU Engine; documented, not repaired
findings.source: crates/conatus/conatus/src/engine.rs:advance, run_steps, run_phase; clock.rs:FixedClock::advance; world.rs:step and drains
findings.evidence: An injected one-time AfterPhysics system error during advance50000us grants three60Hz steps up front. clock.steps_taken becomes3 but BodyWorld.tick is1; subsequent advance0 reports steps0/deferred0 and never executes the other two. A separate run applies a queued spawn and has a preexisting direct despawn, then errors after physics. The spawn exists in live state, but command result, changed-body and prior removal notification are absent from the error and the next successful zero-step frame. No-error controls execute all three steps and publish the spawn result/change/removal. run_steps drains notifications into locals and returns Err without a partial update or restoring them.
findings.scope: Two generated public CPU observations with a deterministic single failing system and no-error controls. No rollback is presumed: the demonstrated defect is lost admitted time and unobservable already-applied outcomes. A full state snapshot can rebuild current bodies, but cannot reconstruct discarded command results or interaction history. Resource/system side effects and product recovery were not exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: broader scheduler failure/publication policy; may exceed one-hour audit diversion
repair_triage.reason: Keep unexecuted granted steps pending and preserve or return partial publication for already-applied work. Choose exact phase retry/resume, command outcome and resource side-effect semantics before repair; do not invent transactional rollback. This larger design must not stall all-source reading.

findings.title: Finite component admission permits overflowing norms to corrupt rotations and ray answers
findings.status: reproduced through public CPU body and query APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.source: crates/conatus/conatus/src/world.rs:validate_transform, squared_length, raycast; world/rapier.rs:pose and ray direction normalization
findings.evidence: A fixed body with finite quaternion[f32::MAX,0,0,1] is accepted, then public state returns rotation[0,0,0,0], norm squared0, because squared norm overflowed before normalization. Moderate nonunit[2,0,0,0] correctly normalizes. A finite ray from(0,4,0) toward a present unit box hits at3 units for directions(0,-1,0) and(0,-10,0), but direction(0,-f32::MAX,0) is accepted as Ok(None). Finite component checks and the nonzero threshold do not reject an infinite derived norm; division turns the latter ray direction into zero.
findings.scope: Two generated native tests using freshly built default Conatus and actual Rapier-backed public APIs. Finite inputs and moderate controls only; no renderer, character movement, GPU or deliberate panic execution. Returned zero rotation is an admitted unusable state, not a demonstrated downstream crash.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained norm/admission repair with shared-helper review
repair_triage.reason: Compute stable scaled norms or reject unusable derived norms before mutation/query execution; preserve documented normalization of reasonable nonunit inputs. Character-up and Tenant normalization share the source-qualified numeric pattern but were not independently executed here.

findings.title: Public brick material lookup aliases distant world cells through a narrowing key cast
findings.status: reproduced through public Modulus CPU APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: For a map containing only key[0,0,0] filled with material7, material_at([524288,0,0]) and material_at([-524288,0,0]) both return7. Nearby outside x8 correctly returns0, and actual public trace at either distant coordinate is Clear. Public material_at divides world i32 coordinates by8 then casts to i16 without checking range, wrapping +/-65536 to key0. The pointer-volume reader used by traversal instead bounds local coordinates and treats outside volume as air.
findings.scope: One generated native test against a freshly built Modulus library, with selected/near-outside and actual trace controls. No GPU or product scene executed. The trace itself is bounded and does not inherit this distant-key alias; the defect is the separate public material lookup.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained lookup unification/admission repair
repair_triage.reason: Check key range before narrowing or route public lookup through the existing bounded pointer-volume reader. Keep negative coordinates, retained high slots and material byte order controls. This directly removes the divergent lookup authority rather than adding a third copy.

findings.title: The exact DDA parallel-threshold endpoint is classified differently by clipping and stepping
findings.status: reproduced through public Modulus CPU traversal; WGSL matching source inspected only
findings.evidence: A finite ray starting at(0.5,4.5,4.5), with solid voxels from x4, returns Clear for direction(1e-6,0,0). The next representable f32 direction above1e-6 and the unit-direction control both hit voxel[4,4,4]. Clipping treats only abs(d)<1e-6 as parallel, while crossings move only for d>1e-6 or d<-1e-6. Exact endpoints thus clip as moving but produce sentinel crossings. The CPU public contract explicitly permits nonunit directions. The WGSL contains the same predicate mismatch; it was not executed.
findings.scope: One generated native test with finite public inputs and neighbouring/unit controls. Bounded numeric endpoint finding, not a product-camera or general GPU parity failure. Below-threshold behaviour remains the explicitly approximate raw traversal policy; no global threshold redesign is inferred.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained boundary-predicate correction
repair_triage.reason: Choose one consistent endpoint classification across CPU clip/crossing, WGSL and exact test reference, then test both signed endpoints and adjacent floats. Do not silently retune the overall parallel threshold or replace the finite-precision traversal policy.

findings.title: Corrupt subgraph sidecars silently become fresh indexes that can replace saved definitions

Load itself leaves corrupt bytes intact; saving that returned index replaces them, and the next load contains only the default. Missing, unreadable and corrupt inputs share the same fallback in source; only truncation was exercised.

findings.title: Failed Forme saves stamp live timestamps and contaminate later successful creation time
findings.status: reproduced against current directly compiled Forme source; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: With session path blocked by an ordinary file, save_forme returns Err but changes a fresh document created/updated timestamps from0 to100. First successful save at200 then persists created100 and updated200. Timestamp mutation precedes directory creation, serialization and rename. Ordinary later roundtrip works.
findings.scope: Native store feature compiled from current source, deterministic directory-admission failure, followed by successful save/load. Owned fixture removed. Does not claim a successful save lost its JSON or prove automatic host success.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained candidate timestamp staging
repair_triage.reason: Stamp a candidate and publish the caller document only after the file replacement succeeds, or restore the prior stamps on every error. Preserve clock policy and do not inflate tmp+rename into a multi-file/crash-durability guarantee.

findings.title: Forme lookup accepts document identity different from requested file identity
findings.status: reproduced against current directly compiled Forme source; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Two valid saved documents A/B initially load by their IDs. Copying valid A JSON over B path makes load_forme(B) return Some(documentA) without error. Renaming the duplicate to not-a-uuid.json also admits two A documents from load_all_formes, despite its uuid-only filename comment. Only JSON syntax is checked.
findings.scope: Native valid-file mismatch and list duplication with ordinary matching-ID control; no host write-back, malicious remote input or graph-binding bypass executed. Caller still owns expected graph binding.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained filename/document-ID admission, with explicit list diagnostics policy
repair_triage.reason: Check the decoded ID against requested/path ID. Enumerated files need valid filenames and an explicit duplicate/refusal outcome. Keep graph binding policy host-owned; do not create a second catalog to conceal mismatches.

findings.title: Cold ancestors suppress active descendant pane geometry while accessibility still publishes it
findings.status: reproduced against current directly compiled Forme source; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Cold root1 with Active child2 returns active2 and a tab for2 but no pane rectangles in SplitPanes. emit_ux_tree nevertheless emits Pane2. Making parent1 Warm restores child geometry. Layout filters visible roots/immediate children before descent; accessibility independently includes all visible members in insertion order.
findings.scope: Parked but compiled/public GraphTree API; repository search found no production caller, only comments outside the package. Public API defect, not demonstrated current product UI impact. Native geometry and UX descriptors executed with lifecycle control. This is divergence between two projections, not proof of screen-reader/platform rendering failure.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: shared visible-frontier projection; policy/adoption may exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Resolve visible descendants through non-present ancestors and let geometry/accessibility consume the same admitted pane set. Preserve topology and host lifecycle policy; do not reactivate cold ancestors merely to hide the divergence.

findings.title: Nested split handles use a representative leaf edge instead of the sibling subtree edge
findings.status: reproduced against current directly compiled Forme source; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: For a horizontal subtree of members1/2 beside root3 in1000x600, actual subtree/root3 boundary is x500 but the outer handle is x375. It averages first leaf1 right edge x250 with root3 left edge x500. Vertical-subtree control puts the handle at the correct edge. The inner pane rectangles abut correctly.
findings.scope: Parked but compiled/public GraphTree API; repository search found no production caller, only comments outside the package. Public API defect, not demonstrated current product UI impact. Native finite geometry and direction control. No interactive drag or rendered host exercised; geometry defect is independent of current product adoption.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained container-bound geometry correction; nested resize intent mapping needs follow-up
repair_triage.reason: Compute outer handles from direct sibling container layouts, retaining representative members only as labels/intent references. Qualify whether drag acts on a container or only its first leaf before promising correct nested resizing.

findings.title: Fraction sanitizers retain negative shares and overflow finite positive shares into zero
findings.status: reproduced against current Cargo-built public library; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: sanitize([-1,2]) leaves[-1,2] despite detecting invalidity. Both sanitize and live set_weights([f32::MAX,f32::MAX]) produce[0,0] because their f32 sum overflows. Live canonical_roundtrips then becomes false and debug to_persisted_json panics before returning its advertised Result. Ordinary[3,1] becomes[0.75,0.25] and serializes.
findings.scope: Native no-default-feature Platen public data/API paths, caught debug assertion. No release panic claim: release skips debug assertion. Graphshell load validates finite positive shares/total; its live edit builds and validates a candidate, so those host paths reject the invalid result rather than proving a UI crash.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: shared stable normalization/admission; contained algorithm repair
repair_triage.reason: Use one finite positive normalization policy across geometry and live state, with overflow-safe accumulation/scaling and refusal or repair before publication. Keep valid fractions bit-exact as promised. Do not use a debug assertion as the only fallible persistence boundary.

findings.title: Opening into an unknown target removes the already-open member before reporting failure
findings.status: reproduced against current Cargo-built public library; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Starting with stack[1,2], active2, open_in_slot_of(2,99) returns false and leaves only1. It detaches2 before checking target99. move_to_slot_of with the same unknown target preserves both; a valid target control succeeds. The documented caller fallback can reopen the member but cannot recover its prior grouping/active state automatically.
findings.scope: Native ordinary public TileLayout API, with guarded move and valid-target controls. No current external production caller of open_in_slot_of was found by repository symbol search; the generic API failure is proven, current product trigger not.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained target admission before detach
repair_triage.reason: Resolve/check the target before mutating, or stage a candidate and publish only on success. Preserve full prior structure/active selection on refusal rather than reconstructing it with a fallback open.

findings.title: Tree projection ignores a stacking edge when a later tile connects two existing slots
findings.status: reproduced against current Cargo-built public library; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Root members inserted1,2,3 with StackedWith edges1-3 and2-3 project into two slots;2 and3 are not together even though their explicit stacking edge exists. All three tiles survive. Insertion-aligned chain1-2,2-3 projects one slot. The greedy first-known-slot lookup never merges previously placed components.
findings.scope: Native public Arrangement/project_tree with ordinary authored relations and chain control. No Group/nested projection support inferred; those remain explicitly deferred. No rendered host or grouping editor execution.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained equivalence-component grouping with stable order
repair_triage.reason: Resolve stacking groups independent of visit/edge order before emitting slots, preserving member occurrence identities and first-authored order. Do not merge separate appearances solely by graph member UUID.

findings.title: Geometry sidecar overrides semantic membership and tab grouping without a disagreement outcome
findings.status: reproduced against current Cargo-built public library; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Same arrangement with1 StackedWith2 yields one two-tab cell without geometry. Geometry containing only1 silently omits2; geometry splitting1/2 yields two cells despite the stacking relation. That split layout still returns canonical_roundtrips=true because it derives a new matching arrangement from itself rather than comparing with the supplied authority. Reconciliation only removes geometry members absent from the arrangement.
findings.scope: Native source/sidecar mismatch at public constructor. Graphshell validate enforces exact membership-set equality and therefore rejects the missing-member case before its load path; it does not compare stacking-edge semantics. No current product archive or live editor mismatch executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: authority reconciliation design and consumer migration may exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Specify and enforce which source owns membership/grouping versus geometry refinement. Reject/report mismatches or reconcile from the authored arrangement with explicit coverage. A self-roundtrip receipt only proves reconstruction of its own output, not agreement with an independent authority.

findings.title: Closing an inactive earlier tab changes the active member in both tiling reducers
findings.status: reproduced against current Cargo-built public library; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: For stack[1,2,3] with active2, closing inactive1 leaves index1 active, now selecting3, in both independent implementations. A last-active3 control remains3 through their clamp path. Both removal functions clamp only out-of-range indices instead of preserving the selected tile identity.
findings.scope: Two native public reducers exercised. Graphshell event Closed calls layout.close_tile, and missing-access masking/load also closes members, source-traced only; no hosted event or renderer execution.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained selected-identity preservation in each owner, then shared algorithm review
repair_triage.reason: Preserve the active tile by identity when removing another tab; choose documented neighbor only when the active tile itself closes. Align both reducer implementations or share the neutral operation with appropriate ID mapping.

findings.title: Loaded duplicate geometry passes the canonical check and produces duplicate accessibility IDs
findings.status: reproduced against current Cargo-built public library; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Arrangement containing1 plus geometry stack[1,1] loads as two tabs, passes canonical_roundtrips, and project_tile_layout emits duplicate AccessKit NodeIds because tab paths use the repeated member. One close removes only one copy. Normal open_stack([1,1]) deduplicates to one.
findings.scope: Native geometry admission and AccessKit DTO construction only, no AccessKit consumer/adapter panic executed. Graphshell host validate rejects duplicate access IDs before loading this state, so that existing boundary limits product impact.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained loaded-layout uniqueness admission; occurrence-aware generalization broader
repair_triage.reason: Enforce the same one-member-per-cell policy on import as ordinary mutators, with explicit refusal/diagnostics. If repeats are meant to be real appearances, introduce occurrence IDs consistently across geometry, editing and a11y rather than reusing member IDs.

findings.title: Self-edge drag deletes a tile while the shared Workbench reports Applied
findings.status: reproduced against current Cargo-built public library; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: From stack[1,2], dragging1 to its own Right edge returns WorkbenchOutcome::Applied and leaves only2. Target validation succeeds before removing1, then split_at_tile cannot find the removed target; its false return is ignored and drag returns true. Unknown-target control is Unchanged with both tiles; other-tile edge control succeeds preserving both.
findings.scope: Native shared public Workbench wrapper and reducer. No platform event producer or current host execution. Platen self-split APIs guard this case and Graphshell uses split_out for own-cell edges, so this is a separate shared reducer defect rather than a demonstrated Graphshell deletion.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained self-target policy and atomic move correction
repair_triage.reason: Resolve an alternate target within the original stack for an intended split-out, or refuse self-edge drops without mutation. Publish Applied only if insertion succeeded and tile custody is retained. Keep the explicit outside tear-out Effect boundary.

findings.title: Floating geometry promises nonfinite sanitization but host-area values can panic or leak NaN
findings.status: reproduced against current Cargo-built public library; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Finite400x400 area resolves normally. A NaN host x origin panics in f32::clamp; a NaN host width returns NaN x. Nonfinite relative x/width are sanitized as the existing policy promises. The host area bypasses the finite helper even though resolve documents nonfinite inputs reading as zero.
findings.scope: Native CPU geometry with explicit nonfinite host input and finite/relative-input controls. Does not prove ordinary host viewport is nonfinite or any GPU/renderer failure. No finite-range behavior regression claimed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained area precondition/finite admission clarification
repair_triage.reason: Apply the documented finite policy to the full area before bounds/clamp arithmetic, or expose/refuse an invalid area explicitly and document the precondition. Keep host size/layout policy outside this neutral contract.

findings.title: Distinct links in one shaping run share a hit rectangle and first-label clicks resolve the later URL
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default document-canvas APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Two ordinary same-style links FIRST/SECOND receive distinct retained IDs but exactly equal full-run rectangles. A point inside the first glyph resolves second URL. An intervening plain space still gives equal rectangles. Making the first link bold creates a shaping boundary and resolves first URL correctly. Geometry intersects annotation ranges with the underlying shaping run text_range, then includes the whole run advance.
findings.scope: Native Windows font environment, public layout/packet hit testing and bold-font control. No claim every font/script shapes identically. Smolweb uses the packet typed interaction_at and separately checks topmost retained pointer targets, source-traced only; no hosted pointer, OS accessibility or network navigation executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: per-cluster annotation geometry; shared hit/semantic ownership correction may exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Use actual cluster/positioned-item spans for each logical annotation and keep disjoint links disjoint, including style boundaries, bidi and wrapping controls. Distinct semantic IDs do not repair overlapping geometry. Do not add a second host-side link rectangle table.

findings.title: Nested rendered block source indices can name unrelated top-level content or exceed the source array
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default document-canvas APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A quote at top-level0 has second child source_block_index1. block_at correctly returns that child geometry, but EngineDocument.blocks[1] is unrelated outside text. A quote at top-level1 emits first child index1000 beyond the two-element source array. The public field says index into EngineDocument.blocks and block_at advertises point-to-source mapping. top_level_block correctly avoids the collision as control.
findings.scope: Native public nested layout and hit testing. Original fold test already pins child-index reuse and top-level helper protection; no regression claim for that helper. Smolweb accessibility carries a hierarchical path and independently repeats synthetic arithmetic, source-traced only; no current hosted citation/selection misattribution executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: typed source path plus compatibility/consumer migration may exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Separate original top-level source identity from an explicit nested path. Preserve host path resolution while retiring undocumented decimal packing; renaming an ambiguous integer alone cannot repair source attribution.

findings.title: Ordered lists lose their ordering marker distinction in the visual packet
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default document-canvas APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Changing only Block::List ordered=true to false yields an exactly equal complete DocumentRenderPacket. Paint-command Debug dumps are also equal. Changed item-text control differs. List dispatch ignores ordered and render_list emits indented child blocks without number/bullet commands or ordering metadata, so a packet consumer cannot recover that distinction.
findings.scope: Native layout and portable paint producer data. Packet equality is exact; paint comparison is Debug-dump equality, not serialized-wire proof. No visual screenshot or GPU render. Uxtree independently preserves an ordered description, so visual and semantic projections have different information.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained list-marker lowering, with nested/source identity controls
repair_triage.reason: Render appropriate markers or retain explicit visual list metadata through the packet, keeping decorative numbering out of authored link labels and source identity. Preserve multi-block item grouping and nested-list behavior.

findings.title: Body paragraph layout ignores the resolved role spacing-above setting
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default document-canvas APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Setting roles.body.spacing_above80 resolves to80 but leaves a one-paragraph packet exactly equal to baseline. Increasing body spacing_below changes geometry; code-role spacing_above80 moves its block by80. Paragraph dispatch passes only spacing_below and its wrapper hardcodes spacing_above0.
findings.scope: Native public style/layout with ordinary finite settings and sibling-role controls. No host settings UI or persistence executed. Default body spacing-above is0, so default appearance remains unaffected.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained resolved-role field threading
repair_triage.reason: Thread resolved spacing_above through paragraph layout consistently with other text roles. Existing default-value tests should not stand in for user-configurable role-field coverage.

findings.title: Changing adornment presentation renumbers later retained logical-link identities
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default document-canvas APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Same document with an empty-label link followed by a visible later link gives that later link different SemanticInteractionIds under SchemeArrow versus None. The first annotation exists only when its decoration creates nonempty painted text. Empty custom glyph repeats None; nonempty first-label control retains the later ID across the style change. Identity allocation counts flattened visible annotations, so presentation affects the logical ordinal.
findings.scope: Native default public layout and retained tokens, with empty-custom-glyph and nonempty-label controls. Smolweb set_style_sheet preserves document/focus state and invalidates geometry, source-traced only. No hosted stale-action retarget or security bypass is claimed; session revision guards require full review.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: shared source-owned link allocation; retained-consumer adoption may exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Allocate/reserve logical identities from authored link occurrences independently of decoration and visible rectangles. Keep removed/zero-width interactions noninteractive while retaining later IDs; preserve fold and reflow guarantees and review session revision/currentness rules.

consumer_followup.evidence: Native retained SmolwebDocument focuses Second with an earlier empty-label link. After link adornment None and a new frame, focused_interaction resolves Third. Nonempty first-label control retains Second. Current accessibility revision guards still reject old queued requests; the reproduced failure is live retained keyboard focus retargeting across presentation, not a stale-request bypass.

findings.title: Navigation currentness accepts unrelated same-length replacement blocks
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default Inker public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A real two-block heading/body table with an anchor and fold reports is_current=true for unrelated Rule/body blocks. resolve still returns the old anchor. A one-block replacement is rejected. is_current compares only block_count, despite claiming indices still describe the supplied blocks and copied targets stay inert.
findings.scope: Native public navigation table and replacement/control. No hosted copied-target action, fold UI or stale session bypass executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: source identity/revision and transform contract migration may exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Name the guard as a length check or bind navigation/targets to an explicit document identity/revision. A complete fix must cover same-count replacements, copies into another document and consumers, while preserving explicit clear/remap transforms.

findings.title: Markdown/Knot export conflates literal syntax with authored structure and raw frontmatter values with fields
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default Inker public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Literal Text("*x*") and Emphasis(Text("x")) are distinct source blocks but export exactly the same Markdown and Knot strings. HTML distinguishes them. Title "Alpha\nsource: Beta" without canonical URI exports exactly the same Knot as title "Alpha" with canonical URI "Beta". Two distinct inputs with identical bytes cannot both round-trip as the claimed equivalent document.
findings.scope: Native serializer non-injectivity proof with HTML control. No Nematic parser reparse, trust escalation, executable HTML/JS, or saved user note executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: literal escaping is contained; complete structural/frontmatter round-trip contract can exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Escape syntax according to each output context, choose safe code fences, and encode multiline frontmatter values unambiguously. Qualify the round-trip claim and test supported field equivalence through the actual Knot parser. Do not infer authentication from a serialized trust label.

parser_followup.evidence: Actual KnotEngine parse/export/reparse turns escaped literal *x* into an Emphasis span. This upgrades the prior exact-output collision proof to an executed parser example; no user persistence or trust escalation.

findings.title: Knot semantic round-trip silently drops stable feed-entry identity
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default Inker public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Changing only FeedEntry.guid from first to second produces exactly equal Knot output; a changed block-kind control differs. The serializer also omits published, updated, enclosures and content_address by source inspection. Public to_knot documentation promises equivalent document-level metadata and every structural/semantic block.
findings.scope: Native output collision for guid; other omitted fields source-qualified. No feed database identity collision or parser reparse executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: semantic fence schema and parser/consumer evolution may exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Define which semantic fields Knot preserves and extend producer/parser together, or explicitly describe a lossy projection. Keep stable feed identity and offline content address distinct from display date/article navigation. Presented semantic blocks also take ordinary Markdown rather than semantic-fence serialization and need a control in that repair.

parser_followup.evidence: A FeedEngine-parsed stable-id survives in its source FeedEntry.guid, then to_knot plus KnotEngine reparse produces a FeedEntry with guid=None. This upgrades the prior serializer collision proof; no live feed database was mutated.

findings.title: Independent authority splitters both misparse IPv6 hosts
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default Inker public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: gopher://[::1]:7070/1/notes exports host "[" and port70; a DNS host with7070 is correct. host_from_address independently returns "[" for https://[::1]:7070/, and a configured [::1] host override is missed while a DNS override works. Both split authority on the first colon.
findings.scope: Native string export and default policy with host overrides. No Gopher server/client, DNS, socket or live navigation executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained bracket-aware authority handling or shared URL parsing
repair_triage.reason: Use an existing typed URL/authority owner or a shared validated helper rather than fixing two ad hoc splitters independently. Specify bracket conventions at override/export boundaries and retain userinfo/port controls.

findings.title: Availability-filtered routing still returns an unavailable fallback engine
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default Inker public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A filter returning false for every ID still produces external.protocol; an empty EngineRegistry does not contain that decision. An available Genet control routes correctly. The fallback bypasses is_available, contrary to the API explanation that filtering avoids decisions pointing to unregistered engines. Existing test also expects an unavailable fallback without asserting availability.
findings.scope: Native policy and registry membership. No actual external protocol launch, application dispatch or host registration graph executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: explicit no-route result and host adoption may exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Validate fallback availability and expose explicit absence/refusal, or document a separate host-handled sentinel contract. Do not silently select another unavailable engine. EngineRegistry already refuses missing IDs, so this is a route-contract gap rather than proof of successful dispatch.

findings.title: The claimed type-enforced one-hop flip invariant is an unenforced implementor convention
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default Inker public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: An ordinary downstream Secondary type implements FlipBack, FlipDonor and FlipReceiver together, compiles, then forwards its state to B and B to C through flip_forward. Public traits contain no mutual exclusion, role token or constrained primary identity, although docs claim there is no type path for secondary chaining.
findings.scope: Native generated implementor and two forward calls. Built-in ScryForward itself does not implement FlipDonor. No real black-box state extraction or lossy browser chain executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: documentation correction is contained; enforced role/provenance API may exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: State the current convention accurately. If enforcement is required, make primary/source custody an explicit API input or constrained role and review downstream implementors. Merely naming separate open traits does not enforce negative trait membership.

findings.title: Scry loses host-observable cookie and restore failures while finishing the flip
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default Inker public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A mock set_cookie refusal still yields begin Ok and navigates. A run_script refusal then yields terminal is_done. Debug warnings appear in stderr, but neither error reaches a result/event/diagnostic accessor. In non-debug source configuration tracing_warn discards its argument. Docs say cookie failures are logged by/decided by the host, yet this seam never reports them to it.
findings.scope: Native mock surface with default/debug Cargo library. Release suppression is source-qualified; no release build, real WebView, authentication flow or user cookie store executed. is_done explicitly includes failure and is not itself misdocumented as success.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: typed degraded outcome and asynchronous host adoption may exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Preserve degrade-without-blocking while returning/retaining structured per-layer failures. Keep admission, load completion and restoration outcome separate. The host can then decide how to surface missing state without scraping debug stderr.

findings.title: An XML declaration prevents feed sniffing and defeats the default feed route
findings.source: crates/inker/inker/src/sniff.rs:sniff_structured and atom_feed_is_detected_inside_xml; routing.rs default MIME rules
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default Inker public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The same Atom root without an XML declaration sniffs application/atom+xml and routes to the feed engine; adding the ordinary XML declaration sniffs application/xml and routes to Genet for HTTPS. The default policy has no application/xml feed rule. The test permits either result and claims generic XML can still dispatch without checking the actual combined policy.
findings.scope: Native sniff plus default policy composition on two byte fixtures. No fetch host second-pass logic, parser, RSS endpoint or actual rendering executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained sniff precedence with generic XML controls
repair_triage.reason: Recognize a feed root before returning the generic XML label within the same bounded window. Test both generic XML and feed declarations through sniff plus routing; do not route all application/xml to feeds.

findings.title: SVG sniffing escapes the advertised small prefix window
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built default Inker public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Two inputs with exactly equal first1024 bytes and65536 leading spaces produce different MIME values when the later marker is SVG versus HTML. SVG is detected beyond the advertised window because sniff_image trims the entire input; HTML remains limited to head_window. Existing bound test exercises HTML only.
findings.scope: Native65536-byte whitespace fixtures and public sniff result; no denial-of-service, huge allocation or benchmark claim.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained prefix-bound consistency
repair_triage.reason: Apply the documented window before whitespace-dependent image sniffing, keeping fixed magic-byte checks and BOM policy explicit. Test every signature family at/after the bound, not only the structured-text branch.

findings.title: A registered Smolweb session engine ID does not select the parser that actually runs
findings.status: reproduced through current feature-enabled Cargo-built document-lanes public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: SmolwebSessionEngine registered as nematic.text accepts an HTTPS held-body request containing literal heading syntax. Its actual document source_kind is nematic.gemtext, with a Heading and derived title. spawn never uses self.engine_id in lowering; lower independently selects by scheme, then feed prefix, then Gemtext. An explicit text pin/registration can therefore describe a different parser from the one producing content.
findings.scope: Native SessionEngine spawn with a NoFetch fixture, downcast, inspect and portable source facts. No host route UI, web fetch or network session executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: registration/route/MIME/session lowerer consolidation may exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Pass the selected format/engine or shared registry decision into lowering and retain the actual response MIME/final identity. Avoid another independent scheme/body selector. Keep deliberate block-versus-session engine kinds while sharing parser selection.

findings.title: Nested document images never enter the host subresource request set
findings.status: reproduced through current feature-enabled Cargo-built document-lanes public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A top-level Image produces its URL in subresources. The identical Image inside a Quote or List produces no request. provide_subresource only accepts pending URLs from that top-level scan, and replace_document similarly retains cached images only if a top-level Image still names them. The portable model, reader lowering and document-canvas support nested blocks.
findings.scope: Native public source/resource discovery with top-level, quote and list fixtures. No decoder/network failure or actual reader page image download executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; active goal forbids production edits
repair_triage.size: contained recursive image visitor shared by discovery/admission/cache retention
repair_triage.reason: Traverse Presented, Quote and List source blocks consistently and deduplicate URLs. Reuse that visit for pending requests, response admission and cache retention so different shallow scans do not become separate resource authorities. Preserve host fetch/decode limits.

findings.title: Smolweb load drops redirect-final response identity before resolving relative content
findings.status: reproduced through current feature-enabled Cargo-built document-lanes public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A rich mock fetch response names final.test/actual/index.gmi but load_with_inline_media asks for alias.test/old/index.gmi through the byte-only fetch method. Its retained address and promoted relative image remain on alias.test/old/image.png. Parsing the same body at the final URL gives final.test/actual/image.png. RemoteFetcher already exposes ResourceResponse with final_url/content_type, then its legacy fetch strips them.
