findings.title: Smolweb page caps wait for full acquisition and rely on a nonexistent Gopher read bound
findings.source: crates/system/fetch/src/lib.rs:fetch_page_capped, fetch_page_interactive_capped and fetch_bytes; actual gopher-protocol0.2.0 client send_and_read
findings.status: observed through current all-feature Cargo-built Fetch APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A Gopher fixture flushes eight bytes under max_bytes4 and keeps the socket open. fetch_page_capped remains pending until EOF, then returns the cap error. The dependency reads into Vec with read_to_end and no byte bound. The function discloses post-hoc Smolweb checking but justifies it by saying errand bounds its own read; that assurance is false for this actual route. The global PAGE_BODY_CAP prose also claims a hard streaming/OOM ceiling.
findings.scope: Eight synthetic bytes, one owned loopback connection, observed pre-EOF pending and terminal cap refusal. No large transfer, allocation exhaustion or remote denial-of-service executed. Gopher dependency excerpt is source traced, not whole-file Mere coverage.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; preserve production and original test source
repair_triage.size: bounded transport API and progress/cancellation migration can exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Carry a byte budget to the actual protocol acquisition or stream into a bounded sink that cancels on overflow. Gate progress and terminal buffering under the same request budget. A final length check and suppression of excess progress do not bound upstream allocation or stop the transfer.

findings.title: Identity download silently decodes an unexpected encoded body and reports the encoded length
findings.status: observed through current all-feature Cargo-built Fetch APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The handle sends Accept-Encoding identity. A supplied gzip response contains38 encoded bytes; read_into succeeds with18 decoded bytes in its sink and Facts.content_length=38. The maintained crawler rejects the same response as UnsupportedEncoding. Netfetcher decodes before the handle sees the body, and the no-store response retains encoded Content-Length. The handle comment claims identity makes the declared length equal the length written.
findings.scope: Current real decode pipeline with a supplied one-hop transport and bounded gzip fixture, no live HTTP/TLS wire or user file. The observed mismatch is in successful custody metadata; no arbitrary server protocol compliance is assumed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; preserve production and original test source

repair_triage.reason: Choose whether downloads require identity/raw representation or expose explicit encoding and decoded-length facts. Refuse unexpected encodings before transformation for a raw-custody contract, or revise Facts and caller integrity/range assumptions. An outbound request header alone is not a response guarantee.

findings.title: The five-redirect Smolweb limit actually allows only four redirects before a final response
findings.status: observed through current all-feature Cargo-built Fetch APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A local Spartan chain with four redirects and a final success uses five requests and succeeds. With five redirects, the function performs five redirect requests and reports too many redirects before asking for the final target. The constant is documented as the most redirects it follows, but the loop counts total attempts.
findings.scope: Two actual loopback Spartan chains, no external origin or mutation. This is a bound-definition/off-by-one mismatch; no unbounded traversal claim.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; preserve production and original test source
repair_triage.size: contained redirect-versus-attempt counting correction
repair_triage.reason: Define redirects and initial request separately and test zero, boundary and overflow chains. Preserve per-hop timeout and identity scope checks when adding the terminal allowed attempt.

findings.title: A new same-address request inherits response metadata from the preceding request
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A retained response at time10 with an old redirect/MIME is followed by begin2 and a new nonstreaming body at time30. The new bytes receive time10 plus the preceding effective URL and MIME. Fresh progress at time40 updates its response URL but also retains time10. begin clears the stream but retains the document; metadata lookup keys only by address and does not distinguish the new request. Explicit forget_fetched is a working control.
findings.scope: Public PageLoad API with synthetic timestamps and bodies. Current Pelt explicit Reload source calls forget_fetched first, so that inspected path is a real mitigating control; no bad Pelt reload, live source-capture timestamp or remote redirect was reproduced. A direct new request at the same address still violates the LoadedDocument admission-time meaning.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; preserve production and original test source

Retain old content for failure/Stop presentation while associating admission time, effective URL and MIME fallback with the current request epoch. Do not erase useful old content merely to make response identity current.

findings.title: Scene transfer reuses a per-frame image key as permanent asset identity and restores old image data
findings.source: crates/system/content-contract/src/lib.rs:SceneTransferEncoder::encode_scene and SceneTransferDecoder::decode_scene; document-canvas paint-list image allocation; actual paint_list_render register_images
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built public APIs; documented, not repaired

findings.scope: Real packet-to-paint-list-to-Scene-to-transfer/replay chain and exact resource bytes/dimensions, CPU only. No GPU upload/raster screenshot, browser worker or current product image corruption claim. Account for size, content revision and worker/cache reset together. Never use a per-list slot alone as proof the receiver already has this image.

findings.title: Out-of-order unique witness entries are falsely reported as duplicate labels
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built public APIs; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Witness::try_from accepts an owned list with distinct site:10 and site:9 labels and refuses it as DuplicateLabel(site:9), although that label occurs once. The Error documentation says DuplicateLabel means the witness already holds that label.
findings.scope: Public list admission and current strict-framed roundtrip control. Invalid entries remain refused, so this is a misleading diagnostic rather than invalid-state admission, false equality or data loss.

findings.title: Mesh ambient blob presence and reads ignore the typed algorithm and declared length
findings.status: reproduced through current Cargo-built public APIs; documented, not repaired

JobSpec validation also admits each reference through its width-only check. The actual JobNamespaceView then returns DigestMismatch before the resource sees either input. Stickleback's separate get_blob implementation explicitly checks BLAKE3 and reference.verifies.
findings.scope: Current real Mesh/Proofs/Muniment in-memory APIs with valid, wrong-algorithm and wrong-length references. The namespace file is fully read; broader Mesh/spec and Stickleback/courier excerpts are not whole-file coverage. The resource-facing guard was executed and works: no permission bypass, unverified adapter input, peer exchange or durable user blob was demonstrated.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; preserve production and original test source

repair_triage.reason: Apply BlobRef semantics consistently at host readiness/lookup boundaries, distinguishing mere raw-key residency from a held valid typed reference. Preserve the existing resource-view verification. Reuse BlobRef::verifies and explicit supported-algorithm admission rather than treating as_32 as a verifier or creating another weaker store-specific hash rule.

findings.title: Unleased completion overwrite violates the order-independent board contract
findings.status: reproduced against unchanged public APIs and current Cargo artifacts; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Two correctly signed sequential JobDone operations by the same valid claim winner carry A and B. Folding the identical set as post/claim/A/B returns Done(B); post/claim/B/A returns Done(A). Results are gathered by author and overwritten in input order, unlike claims keyed by operation hash. The board/module overview promises order independence.
findings.scope: Native direct public fold reproduced. Both operations form an ordinary signed author chain. Actual MeshStore iterates indexed author logs in sequence order, so this does not establish live store peer divergence or an accepted author-log fork.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; preserve production and original test source
repair_triage.size: semantic result arbitration decision; broader than a mechanical overwrite fix
repair_triage.reason: Name a deterministic rule for multiple winner outputs and mixed generations, retain the selected operation identity, and qualify permutations and checkpoint replay. Do not silently choose first/last by timestamp or hash as an unruled protocol change.

findings.title: Parsed addressing and cached signed extensions disagree across verification and storage
findings.status: reproduced against unchanged public APIs and current Cargo artifacts; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: An operation signed for foreign mesh F is initially refused by accept(M). Mutating public header.extensions.mesh_id to M leaves encoded signed bytes and cached operation hash unchanged, yet mesh::verify succeeds, direct fold(M) admits it, and real MeshStore::accept(M) reports insertion. Reading the retained header decodes F; ops(M) contains one record while board(M) is empty. The application policy indexes parsed extensions while durable bytes use the supplier cached CBOR extensions.
findings.scope: Native public API and real MemoryBackend store reproduction with synthetic valid signatures. No forged signature, corrupted wire acceptance, remote network ingress exploit or durable user store is claimed. Exact compiled p2panda supplier is 0.7.1 from 1f69c9b, not historical upstream API recollection.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; preserve production and original test source
repair_triage.size: shared supplier/admission consistency repair, potentially over one hour
repair_triage.reason: Establish one immutable or canonical decoded header boundary across p2panda typed extensions, Mere preflight, policy selection and persistence. Re-check all consumers and test features; a one-off mesh-id check would leave the shared representation problem in place.

findings.title: Accepted checkpoint reconstruction loses completed leased output
findings.status: reproduced against unchanged public APIs and current Cargo artifacts; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A valid leased job reaches Committed. A non-live completed snapshot passes retention policy. Empty-tail reconstruction yields Claimed while lease_at still says Done. The actual store build_checkpoint/accept/board sequence reproduces the loss before any pruning, while the original completion operation remains retained. The snapshot output is seeded into the unleased results map; leased completion lookup only searches newly gathered completion facts.
findings.scope: Direct snapshot API and actual MemoryBackend store checkpoint path. This is a completed lease, outside the explicitly rejected live-Held checkpoint case. No network, redb reopen or physical persistence claim.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; preserve production and original test source
repair_triage.size: contained restoration symptom with checkpoint contract implications
repair_triage.reason: Preserve the accepted completion/output identity through snapshot reconstruction and later tails. Verify checkpoint migrations, already terminal jobs and missing completion bodies before promoting a local state fallback as a complete retention repair.

findings.title: Leased result lookup publishes an output rejected by grant admission
findings.status: reproduced against unchanged public APIs and current Cargo artifacts; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The lease resolver validates output against the signed spec before forming a Completed end. A subsequent completed_output lookup independently chooses the first operation-hash-ordered completion matching holder/lease, without validation or matching the selected closing fact. A valid 5-byte completion closes at time400; an otherwise well-formed 17-byte output against a16-byte grant is ignored alone but published as Committed when paired with that valid completion and a lower hash. The real store accepts both structurally valid records and its board exposes the invalid output. Bounded search found the lower hash in7 attempts.
findings.scope: Native direct fold and actual MemoryBackend admission/board. Invalid output remains self-valid; job-specific admission is intentionally delegated to the fold. Existing single-invalid-result tests pass and do not cover coexistence with an accepted completion. No worker, blob transfer or peer execution was needed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; preserve production and original test source
repair_triage.size: bounded accepted-fact/output binding repair; retain exact resolver identity
repair_triage.reason: Return or retain the selected accepted completion identity/output from lease resolution instead of performing a second weaker selection. Validate competing valid/invalid outputs, outside-window facts, equal-time tiebreaks and snapshot restoration under that one selection owner.

findings.title: Checkpoint frontier removes device attestations from replay without snapshotting the directory
findings.status: reproduced against unchanged public APIs and current Cargo artifacts; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: JobBoardSnapshot clones only jobs; fold_from_snapshot initializes an empty DeviceDirectory. A real store with one valid master-signed self-attestation reports one device. build_checkpoint includes that event in its frontier; accepting the checkpoint changes board.devices to empty even though the attestation operation remains retained. All events below the frontier are filtered out before the fold, and no snapshot directory is available to restore them.
findings.scope: Both snapshot-only API and actual MemoryBackend checkpoint acceptance reproduced. Device cryptographic admission remains correct; the observed loss is replay state coverage, before pruning. Consumer scheduling/UX effects and remote catch-up were not executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; preserve production and original test source
repair_triage.size: snapshot version and replay-coverage repair, potentially over one hour
repair_triage.reason: Choose whether the governed snapshot includes authenticated device facts or retention separately preserves/replays attestations outside the job frontier. Coordinate encoded checkpoint version/commitment compatibility and catch-up export; avoid adding a second private directory owner.

findings.title: Legacy worker selection bypasses the configured resource allowlist
findings.status: native public-API observation against unchanged source; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: With allowed_resources containing only mesh.echo/v1, an M1 Blake3 post is still considered runnable, selected for Claim and then Execute. The equivalent V2 Blake3 spec correctly returns Idle. The legacy branch checks only payload presence, registration and adapter hardware requirements; V2 calls DevicePolicy::accepts.
findings.scope: Pure worker/board public APIs, valid synthetic signed operations and built-in registry. No actual excluded workload, host daemon or remote peer executed. This is a concrete configuration bypass, not a claim of untrusted remote GPU execution.

repair_triage.disposition: documented during read-only full-source continuation
repair_triage.size: bounded common legacy/V2 policy admission correction
repair_triage.reason: Apply the configured resource rule after mapping the legacy kind to its resource. Keep any implied legacy checkpoint-class rule explicit. Verify both generations under the same policy, preserving the single actual run_legacy -> run_job executor.

findings.title: The worker starts held work before checking owner withholding or capacity
findings.status: native public-API observation against unchanged source; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A valid live lease held by this author but absent from HostOffer.running yields Execute while conservative policy reports ForegroundActivity and accepting=false. The same held-but-unstarted job yields Execute when max_concurrent_jobs=0. When the job is placed in running, the owner-withholding control correctly yields Reclaim. Reclaim only checks running jobs and the start gate occurs after the Execute loop.
findings.scope: Pure public decision function with an actual folded lease. The probe establishes a start decision contrary to current settings; no native OS supervision, physical workload continuation or broader host race was executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented during read-only full-source continuation
repair_triage.size: bounded scheduling gate correction with a held-versus-running distinction
repair_triage.reason: Separate keeping an already running job from starting a held reservation. Owner withholding must prevent a start; capacity should prevent an additional run without reclaiming work already active. Keep heartbeats and reservation release policy deliberate rather than suppressing all lease maintenance.

findings.title: Cancellation during the final real-adapter await still commits output
findings.status: native public-API observation against unchanged source; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The real DelayedResource(1,100) is manually polled to its first Pending after reporting done=1. The host cancels before the next poll, and JobControl confirms Cancel. Awaiting the run nevertheless succeeds and stores the expected output. The adapter has no cooperative point after its final sleep; the runner has no final control check before commit. Existing cancelled-run tests only cancel before execution.
findings.scope: Deterministic cancellation ordering through the real built-in adapter and public runner, synthetic memory blobs. No malformed adapter or timing race is required: cancellation precedes execute returning. A stronger atomic cancellation-versus-sink-commit guarantee remains a separate design question.

repair_triage.disposition: documented during read-only full-source continuation
repair_triage.size: bounded final cooperative check; full commit linearization can exceed one-hour diversion
repair_triage.reason: Check control at the final cooperative boundary and before handing returned bytes to the sink. Define cancellation arriving during an in-flight sink write separately; do not promise rollback of a committed blob merely by adding one flag read.

findings.title: Exact verification verdicts ignore the rerunning adapter weaker class
findings.status: native public-API observation against unchanged source; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: An Observed spec legitimately runs a ProducerOnly local adapter. Its ordinary output is NotCheckable, but an ExactBytes producer output for that same resource causes this local adapter to emit Reproduced for matching bytes and Diverged for different bytes. verify_output inspects only the producing output class; run_job only requires the local adapter to satisfy the weaker posted spec. The identifier contract explicitly gives weaker implementations no cross-implementation exactness promise.
findings.scope: Public registry APIs with a small legal ProducerOnly test adapter and memory blobs. Hash comparison itself is accurate; the unsupported part is treating its mismatch as the exact conformance verdict described by Diverged. No malicious producer, GPU or remote execution is claimed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented during read-only full-source continuation
repair_triage.size: bounded rerunner-class qualification or clearer verdict taxonomy
repair_triage.reason: Require an appropriately qualified local class before attributing exact divergence, or distinguish an observed byte comparison from a conformance check. Preserve Unavailable for absent adapters and NotCheckable for unsupported verification semantics; do not infer a stronger rerun class from the producer declaration.

findings.title: Delayed resource configuration changes exact output without changing either identity
findings.status: native public-API observation against unchanged source; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Two legal registrations of DelayedResource with units1 and2 carry identical resource id mesh.delayed/v1, implementation id mesh.delayed.blake3-chain/v1 and ExactBytes class. The identical signed job spec and input produce different outputs. Verifying one with the other returns Diverged attributed to the same implementation id. Unit count is host constructor state and never bound into the job input/spec or either identity.
findings.scope: Actual shipped adapter through public run_job/verify_output; no copied hash-chain implementation. Default registries both use16 units and are not alleged to diverge. Delay-only configuration does not affect bytes; the unit count does.

repair_triage.disposition: documented during read-only full-source continuation
repair_triage.size: resource/input identity decision, potentially over one hour across rehearsal consumers
repair_triage.reason: Bind semantic unit count into canonical input or a resource generation contract; scheduling delay can remain host policy. A different implementation id alone would not repair the promised ResourceId algorithm equivalence. Keep the rehearsal configurable without claiming one exact algorithm for distinct computations.

findings.title: Checkpoint-plus-tail catch-up selection omits predecessors still required by owner admission
findings.status: native public-API observation against unchanged source; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A real source store holds post seq0, an owner-built accepted checkpoint covering it, and a later post seq1 linked to seq0. The catch-up selector omits seq0 and selects checkpoint plus tail. An empty receiver accepts the checkpoint and reconstructs its snapshot, but rejects the selected tail as MissingPredecessor. Supplying the omitted seq0 lets that same tail enter. Checkpoint state/frontier does not initialize the shared per-author log continuity anchor.
findings.scope: Actual source/receiver MemoryBackend MeshStores, real checkpoint policy and public selector. No file serialization/import transport or live catch-up campaign executed. The selected set is incompatible with this unchanged authoritative owner admission path; a future authorized prune anchor is a different scenario.

repair_triage.disposition: documented during read-only full-source continuation
repair_triage.size: retained-frontier/bootstrap contract repair, potentially over one hour
repair_triage.reason: Define an authenticated continuity anchor or require the needed signed boundary/prune operation in catch-up selection. Coordinate domain checkpoint authority with the shared processor instead of weakening MissingPredecessor for arbitrary non-root operations or bypassing MeshStore.

findings.title: Derived suggestion creation and attention admission use inconsistent candidate sets and budgets
findings.status: three public native Canvas counterexamples reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Two existing offers from an excluded source subtract the entire two-link minting budget, although shared SuggestionSettings::admit admits the two allowed links. Removing those excluded offers restores the links. Conversely, replacing existing offers after two links are minted removes both links from admitted Suggestion attention but leaves both derived graph nodes resident. A60x60 plate mints one link under the pre-mint fill, then immediately gives it no Suggestion attention under the post-mint fill. Minting and attention admission both call budget but use different sets/counts and different plate snapshots.
findings.scope: Current public Canvas API, synthetic graphs and actual shared SuggestionSettings. No rasterized screenshot, live browser or persisted owner write. The observed contract failure is a split admission decision; counts are not evidence of arbitrary unbounded allocation.

repair_triage.disposition: documented during read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded admission reconciliation; viewport-driven pacing may expand scope
repair_triage.reason: Compute one admitted set after source filtering and use it for both derived membership and attention. Reconcile on every relevant offer/settings/fill change, and define which content counts toward plate occupancy so creation does not invalidate its own admission. Avoid a second private pacing implementation.

findings.title: A shared suggested URL retains a page that withdrew it as its origin
findings.status: public native Canvas edge and kept-link provenance mismatch reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Pages A and B both offer the same URL, deduplicated into one derived member. When A replaces its offer with empty, B is the only remaining source. Refresh keeps the existing member by URL, skips its origin tuple and edge update, and leaves its hyperlink from A with none from B. Selecting that member emits KeptLink.origin=A even though only B still offers it.
findings.scope: Actual graph projected relations and public take_kept_links after CPU Canvas frame. No browser commit or wrong durable relation was executed. Stable URL-derived identity is not itself the defect; origin/edge state is stale.

repair_triage.disposition: documented during read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded derived origin/edge reconciliation
repair_triage.reason: Refresh source provenance and the owned ephemeral relation when the selected offer origin changes, preserving the stable member id. Retain enough relation identity to remove only the derived assertion; do not blanket-delete independent user relations.

findings.title: Sitemap scanning sends XML entity spelling as a page URL and omits CDATA locations
findings.evidence: A supplied XML sitemap loc ending search?a=1&b=2 reaches the public run_crawl fetch callback literally with amp;b=2. The intended a=1&b=2 URL is never requested. Equivalent CDATA text produces no search request. Both runs finish FrontierExhausted; the entity case reports two successful page fetches through the synthetic adapter. Frontier URL validation cannot decode XML syntax.
findings.scope: Native public acquisition driver with a supplied in-memory fetch callback, no real HTTP request or server behavior. The scanner explicitly disclaims a full XML parser, but ordinary XML text representation still changes or drops the declared acquisition target.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only continuation
repair_triage.size: bounded XML location decoding
repair_triage.reason: Use a bounded XML text reader or explicit supported location decoder before URL admission. Preserve request/byte/fanout/scope budgets and refusal evidence; do not expand sitemap-index recursion as part of this fix.

findings.status: public native counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired

findings.title: Visual clipping reports success for an empty intersection and includes pixels outside a partial selection
findings.evidence: On a 100x100 PNG, an inside rectangle yields the correct 20x20 control. Rect(-50,10,100,20) attaches 100x20 although its visible intersection is 50x20. Rect(200,10,30,20) attaches a 1x20 border strip and returns true despite having no intersection. Clamping origin and length independently substitutes visible pixels for an off-image rectangle.
findings.scope: Native public helper, synthetic image and caller-supplied ClipRect. Repository call search found the helper definition and its original unit test, not an active product call; no browser capture, user screenshot or end-to-end selection leak executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only continuation
repair_triage.size: bounded rectangle-intersection correction
repair_triage.reason: Transform both rectangle edges, intersect with image bounds, and return false for an empty/non-finite result before encoding. Keep existing resize limits and test inside, partial, outside and scaled controls.

findings.status: public native counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired

findings.title: Distinct valid canonical annotation targets alias to one exported annotation identity
findings.evidence: Two valid rendered DOM records for the same caller-owned acquired representation, selecting characters 0..5 in Alpha and Bravo, have different canonical-text resource IRIs but the same annotation.id. A third record with a different source scope also has that id. All pass validate_integrity and annotation_json_ld; changing capture hash changes the id as a control. Saving/loading the first two through Eidetic yields distinct content-addressed records, so the alias is specifically the exported annotation identity.
findings.scope: Native caller-supplied DOM and in-memory storage. Actual JSON-LD envelopes share id while their targets differ; no downstream RDF merge, peer overwrite, durable-store corruption or product annotation adoption executed.

repair_triage.disposition: document larger compatibility decision
repair_triage.size: potentially over one hour with exported-ID compatibility
repair_triage.reason: Choose whether identity names an immutable annotation or a logical family and state update semantics. If immutable, bind canonical-text resource, source/capture evidence and selector identity. Preserve or migrate existing exported IDs explicitly; a string-format patch alone leaves historical aliases unresolved.

findings.status: public native counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired

findings.title: Resident hint persistence can overwrite successful pair and unpair changes despite single-writer and atomic-update claims
findings.status: two native public read/write interleavings reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: pairing.rs says the resident never writes settings and that management pair/unpair are the only writers. refresh_dial_hint also loads, changes and saves the whole OwnerSettings file, claiming its atomic path avoids clobbering concurrent pair/unpair. The save and load sequence has no cross-process lock or revision check. A public unpair_device call returns Removed and removes the device; saving an earlier hint snapshot then restores both the paired device and its roster root. A public pair_device call returns Added; saving an earlier hint snapshot then removes that new device and root. Fresh-read controls preserve both management changes.
findings.scope: Explicitly ordered public API operations reproduce the possible read/write interleaving and final file contents. The fixture follows the resident hint load/record_endpoint/save critical section and uses real pair/unpair APIs. No timed race between resident processes, live roster reconciliation, key re-admission, peer connection or user settings mutation was executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded shared settings transaction seam
repair_triage.reason: Make all management and hint writers use the same cross-process load-modify-commit owner, or move live management through the resident. Locking only the final rename does not protect an earlier snapshot. Preserve independent concurrent fields and separately address crash-safe replacement; do not claim a rename is an atomic read-modify-write transaction.

findings.title: Personal sync host installs its transfer rule by discarding caller-supplied synthetic-address policy
findings.status: native public selector/replica counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Startup installs the receipt synthetic-address rule, warning that the setter replaces rather than appends. The host subsequently calls with_synthetic_addresses([transfer_offer_rule()]) on that supplied selection, which clears the entire rule vector. An in-memory public replica refuses an unselected synthetic carrier under the supplied custom rule; composing the exact host builder chain admits and projects that carrier. A plain-address control is admitted/projected in both cases.
findings.scope: Native public SyncSelection and PersonalGraphReplica over memory backends, using the same builder chain as the host. No full host opening or network run. Current desktop startup always selects receipt facets, masking a visible receipt-filter difference there; the caller-policy overwrite is real, but no current receipt disappearance or confidentiality breach is claimed. Synthetic carrier selection is presentation, not confidentiality.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded additive policy composition
repair_triage.reason: Preserve caller rules when adding the host-owned transfer rule. Keep an intentional replacement API for callers that replace settings; define duplicate-prefix precedence rather than changing every setter into append. One shared composition seam should own the effective selector list.

findings.title: The resident route lifecycle acceptance test still requires assertion-family rows after the host moved to pair-link projection
findings.status: current Cargo test failure reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The current offline default-feature resident_mere test run reports 22 passed and 1 failed. The lifecycle test inserts two semantic assertions and one containment assertion on one pair, then requires [containment, semantic, semantic]. The host deliberately emits link.surface/link.resource keyed by the link stratum; the route model forwards that disclosed kind. The assertion instead observes [link.surface] and aborts before the rest of that test body. A separately retained earlier-binary execution produced the same failure; it is not counted as a second independent test suite.
findings.scope: A stale acceptance assertion under the current source and shared WIP, not evidence that underlying assertion records were deleted. The link-model plan explicitly derives pair links while preserving separately attributed assertions. Other lifecycle, grant, archive and tamper tests passed; this failure does not invalidate their named checks or prove a headed rendering regression.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded test-contract refresh
repair_triage.reason: Align the route test with the current pair-link contract, and check independently addressable assertion preservation through the shared reading/material owner. Do not restore obsolete per-family scene rows or weaken the design merely to make this assertion pass. Keep the later lifecycle checks reachable.

later_source_qualification.note: Upstream now expects one link.surface and separately asserts the three retained source relation kinds, including after fork. This source correction addresses the historical stale assertion; no new execution of that resident test ran in this pass.

findings.title: Inference actor disconnection is not folded into run failure and later control operations falsely report success
findings.status: two native public lane counterexamples reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A gated provider-construction panic disconnects the actor after an admitted ask has been journaled. A later ask returns Closed, proving disconnection, but has already inserted and journaled another Queued run. The earlier run remains Queued with no load_error. Cancel and pause return success after their command delivery fails, and close returns success while both table and in-memory journal retain queued work. A second public lane opened on a retained user pause returns success from resume, appends a continuation and commits Queued even though the actor is already disconnected. The bridge simply exits on update-channel closure, and ActorHandle::join discards the actor panic result.
findings.scope: Synthetic, intentionally gated construction panics and a public in-memory RunJournal. No GPU, real model, disk journal, resident process, broker or network was used. An ordinary returned InvalidConfig load error is the passing control: that actor remains alive, reports load_error and makes its ask Failed. Some GPU/stage generation wrappers already catch panics; this finding does not claim that every backend failure crashes the actor.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only audit
repair_triage.size: shared actor-disconnect and durable run-transition handling
repair_triage.reason: Fold unexpected update-channel closure into a visible failure for unfinished runs, reject dead actor commands, and reconcile committed queued/resume state when delivery fails. Preserve valid retained checkpoints. A checked join result or explicit actor completion channel is needed to distinguish panic from clean shutdown; do not change every actor consumer or choose durable recovery semantics speculatively.

findings.title: Locally reused job inputs bypass the consuming mesh custody claim and can be collected beneath it
findings.status: native public delivery/custody/GC counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Two mesh-scoped TransportBlobSpace values share one collecting BlobStore. Mesh A stores an input under its own tag. deliver_inputs for mesh B reads that already-present input and continues without invoking the courier or installing B's tag. After delivery returns with the input readable, A releases its one claim; actual collection removes the input from B as well. B has zero custody tags to release. The positive control explicitly pins the same bytes through B.put before releasing A, and retains the bytes across repeated collection intervals.
findings.scope: Synthetic in-memory bytes, actual public deliver_inputs and collecting transport BlobStore APIs. The probe does not post the delivery fixture as a scheduler job or exercise full checkpoint maintenance/concurrent processes. It proves local presence is not mesh-scoped retention, and the production host calls this same delivery path before run_job_for. No user data or real remote peer was involved.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded local-hit custody adoption
repair_triage.reason: Acquire the consuming mesh's named custody claim on the local-hit path, just as the mesh-scoped fetch path does. Reuse the existing content-addressed store and its owner claim API; do not introduce a second blob store or treat a successful read as a pin.

findings.title: Supervisor emits Completed for an expired lease even though its authoritative mesh board discards that completion
findings.status: native public supervisor/board disagreement reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A public MeshHost starts a tiny leased BLAKE3 job, the task finishes between supervisor ticks, and a ManualClock advances beyond the lease window before the next tick. tick reaps finished tasks before abandon_lost_leases and emits Step::Completed after authoring the late completion. The current authoritative board remains nonterminal (Claimed), and the same tick claims the job again. The live-window control makes both the receipt and board terminal. The pure fold correctly rejects the late completion; the product receipt contradicts it.
findings.scope: One local P2panda/SyncedMesh endpoint, memory-backed synthetic job inputs and a manually advanced clock. The Step::Completed observation confirms reaping saw the finished task. No multi-device race, real compute workload, late result accepted by the fold, or broad checkpoint/data corruption is claimed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded finished-run lease validation
repair_triage.reason: Recheck the held lease against the current authoritative board/time before publishing completion or owner-reclaim facts from a finished task. Use the existing lost-lease result when ownership has ended. Keep the pure fold's refusal intact rather than making it accept late output to match an inaccurate receipt.

findings.title: Successful mesh host shutdown can leave a real CPU trainer blocking worker alive
findings.status: native real-resource shutdown counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A real CPU TrainerResource runs through a local MeshHost. The probe holds the shared artifact-store mutex, observing the actual spawn_blocking closure acquire a third store Arc. Host shutdown returns Ok while that worker still owns the Arc and remains gated before model loading. Releasing only the audit gate makes the absent synthetic model end the worker. The control drains the worker before shutdown and retains only the two expected probe/trainer owners.
findings.scope: Two native checks; one local endpoint and synthetic memory storage. No model training, GPU work, installed authority, user store or physical remote peer. All audit-owned worker/network work drains before probe exit. The successful build was at the premerge basis recorded in the prior checkpoint; runtime source hashes remain unchanged through the authorized merge.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in active read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.size: shared blocking-resource drain ownership
repair_triage.reason: Host shutdown must own a truthful drain contract for CPU work as well as the existing GPU occupancy guard. Retain/join actual blocking work or introduce a shared resource-lifetime drain seam. Aborting the awaiting async task does not abort its started spawn_blocking closure. Do not add a second scheduler or a false idle flag.

findings.title: Payload-only manifest identity aliases schemas and allows replacement metadata beneath one stable id
findings.status: native public typed-store alias and metadata replacement reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Two distinct TypedPayload schemas serialize the same valid JSON. Both saves succeed and return one id. After B saves, loading A by its previously successful id fails schema mismatch, while B loads. A separate same-schema second save replaces LocalOnly with explicitly supplied PublicPortable plus replacement timestamps/provenance under that same id. A different-byte control preserves both schema reads. save_typed hashes payload bytes only, then save_manifest unconditionally replaces manifest:<payload hash>.
findings.scope: Three native checks against exact retained Cargo-built Eidetic artifacts and synthetic in-memory records. The second save explicitly requests the changed privacy: no unauthorized publication, cryptographic bypass, remote disclosure or real data loss is claimed. Metadata replacement itself contradicts blanket immutable-manifest/no-op claims. Current reviewed Eidetic source is unchanged through merge; unrelated postmerge dependencies have a separately pending gate.

repair_triage.disposition: document architectural repair; do not divert full audit beyond one hour
repair_triage.size: storage identity and compatibility decision
repair_triage.reason: Distinguish shared blob identity from schema-bearing artifact/manifest identity and decide how metadata history or conflicting writes are admitted. Preserve blob deduplication. Hashing or rejecting metadata differently affects existing ids, readers, provenance, privacy/seal handling and migrations; a local patch cannot establish the full contract.

findings.title: Age-based retirement deletes unexpired tombstones sharing an expired tombstone node id
findings.status: native exact production-module retirement counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: An expired tombstone and a fresh tombstone have the same node_id. propose_retirement selects the expired record but reduces its selection to that node id. apply_retirement calls purge_deleted, whose correct per-item permanent-delete contract removes all records for the id. It reports two removed and leaves the bin empty. The different-node control removes one expired record and retains the fresh record.
findings.scope: Exact Athanor production module compiled into a native probe against retained Cargo-built dependencies, with actual public proposal/apply and Eidetic record/list APIs. This is not a new Cargo package test or resident scheduler/UI/disk/network gate. Synthetic memory-backed records only.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in active read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.size: bounded retention selection contract
repair_triage.reason: Carry exact tombstone/manifest identities or an explicit accepted cutoff through retirement and delete only that accepted aged subset. Keep purge_deleted for its deliberate all-history per-node command. Include same-node old/fresh and post-proposal re-deletion controls before claiming selective retention.

findings.title: Model fetch directory guard accepts dot paths outside its intended model leaf
findings.status: exact production PowerShell guard AST counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The three actual production directory assignment/guard/join statements accept /models/.. and resolve it to the Mere repository root. /models/. aliases the model root itself. The normal MiniLM child control stays strictly below models. The guard forbids separators and punctuation but does not exclude dot and dot-dot path components.
findings.scope: Three native PowerShell guard observations only. No curl, network, directory creation, model download, file move or overwrite is executed. Caller-supplied malformed matrix paths, not an externally reachable attack or damage from the current committed matrix.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in active read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.size: bounded leaf-path validation
repair_triage.reason: Reject dot components and verify the normalized absolute destination is strictly below the intended models root before creating directories or replacing files. Keep the single directory derivation instead of introducing another independently interpreted path.

findings.title: Remote inference timing includes the deliberate telemetry stage hold
findings.status: source-confirmed measurement defect; no new GPU execution
findings.evidence: Both first_execution_ms and recovery_execution_ms are sampled after report_stage for their completed remote execution. report_stage sleeps for DISTILLERY_REMOTE_STAGE_HOLD_MS. The driver telemetry wrapper sets that variable from StageHoldMs, default3000. The resulting remote_execution values therefore include the deliberate three-second hold rather than ending at inference completion.
findings.scope: Complete fixture and wrapper source read. The default direct fixture has zero hold; positive holds through the telemetry wrapper contaminate its execution durations. No actual GPU or wall-clock performance figure was measured here, and the allocator/driver release predicates are not invalidated by this timing observation.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in active read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.size: bounded timer boundary correction
repair_triage.reason: Capture inference elapsed time immediately when inference returns, then emit/hold the telemetry stage. Keep stage sampling and its configured hold separate from the reported inference duration.

findings.title: Session fixture max-error helper silently ignores non-finite coordinate differences
findings.status: exact extracted native numeric helper divergence reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The session helper maps differences and folds with f32::max without a finite check. NaN-minus-NaN and infinity-minus-the-same-infinity are NaN and disappear during that reduction: a paired non-finite coordinate plus a finite2 difference returns Ok(2). The remote fixture helper rejects these inputs. Finite and unequal-length controls show where both agree.
findings.scope: Three native checks using the two verbatim pure std-only functions, synthetic float values only. The full session fixture separately checks adapted and independent logits for finiteness, so this is not proof a complete model receipt passes NaNs. Its base-logit comparison and published-checkpoint audit reuse the weaker helper; actual non-finite model execution was not performed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in active read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.size: bounded shared numeric validation
repair_triage.reason: Reject non-finite operands before difference reduction and share the comparison contract across fixtures. Keep the independent PEFT merge arithmetic independent; duplicating a weaker validation helper does not strengthen that numerical control.

findings.title: Manual browser-probe termination leaves its UI submission unresolved and controls disabled
findings.status: actual page orchestration reproduced in controlled native Node VM; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The UI submission disables run controls and awaits runSuite/runWorker. terminateActive returns true, calls terminate and clears global worker state, but never calls the runWorker promise resolver/rejector. In the bounded VM observation the fake worker is terminated and page state is terminated, while submission remains pending and run controls stay disabled. A worker-error control settles the same flow and reenables controls.
findings.scope: Complete actual page JavaScript, synthetic DOM/fetch/worker messages. The pending observation is30ms plus the source proof that manual termination calls neither finish nor a timeout. No real browser, worker, GPU, model or storage was exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in active read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded cancellation settlement
repair_triage.reason: Route manual termination through the same owned finish/rejection boundary as normal result/error and state-driven cancellation; clear the active owner once and allow finally to reenable controls. Do not create a second independent cancellation state machine.

findings.title: Embedding row success ignores reported within-worker and across-worker repeatability failures
findings.status: actual page receipt gate counterexample reproduced in controlled native Node VM; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Synthetic worker-contract reports have valid dimensions/norm/reference/integrity but false cold/warm repeat_outputs_match and false matches_prior_worker. The actual embedding row concludes row_passed=true and output_repeated_across_workers=false. The decoder counterpart explicitly gates on these repeatability facts. Integrity-failure and ordinary-consistent controls show the embedding gate is selective, not universally passing.
findings.scope: Native execution of complete page code with controlled worker reports. No claim that an actual GPU produced nondeterministic values or a real model receipt was generated.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in active read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded shared row predicate
repair_triage.reason: Make row success require the repeatability facts the row purports to qualify, and share common cold/warm checks between embedding and decoder while keeping workload-specific numeric/stream/cancel checks separate.

findings.title: Browser matrix can claim pinned model size and success despite contradictory observed component sizes
findings.status: actual page matrix gate accepts contradictory controlled worker reports; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The page accepts cold/warm reports whose observed weights size is1 byte while the configured artifact advertises90000000 bytes. all_configured_rows_passed is true and largest_successful_weight_bytes is90000000. The gate never compares component_sizes with expected_artifacts, and ProbeConfig does not carry the pinned artifact sizes/SHA256 values into acquisition. Cold/warm hashes prove storage round-trip identity, not agreement with the configured external pin.
findings.scope: Actual full page source in native Node VM, synthetic worker-contract messages only. A one-byte real model was not loaded and no GPU success with a wrong model is claimed. This proves the receipt predicate/size conclusion gap and the missing pin comparison in reviewed source.

repair_triage.disposition: document artifact identity repair rather than widen audit beyond one hour
repair_triage.size: shared pin and observed-artifact contract
repair_triage.reason: Carry the producer-owned artifact pin to acquisition/validation, compare actual source bytes and sizes before claiming that row, and derive measured size conclusions from observed evidence. Reuse the same pin semantics across fetch/reference/browser readers; cold-to-warm equality alone cannot establish publisher/model identity.

findings.title: Legacy training-corpus reader bypasses the current corpus invariants
findings.status: public native legacy/current reader divergence reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The v1 path deserializes a legacy shape and directly maps fields into TrainingCorpus without validate. Public load returns empty, overlapping, duplicated and reverse-ordered partitions that fail the shared current validator. Current v2 serialization refuses all equivalent cases; valid v1/v2 records agree and validate.
findings.scope: Synthetic memory-backed artifacts and retained exact Cargo-built libraries; reviewed sources unchanged through merge. Distillery calls corpus.validate before loading cases, so actual training/evaluation leakage is not claimed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in active read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded legacy conversion validation
repair_triage.reason: Run the shared corpus validator after legacy conversion, preserving valid historical vocabulary and refusing malformed legacy partitions at the same artifact boundary. Keep the trainer recheck as defense at its consuming boundary.

findings.title: Successful URL-cache replacement with no MIME retains the preceding response content type
findings.status: public native cache replacement counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: After saving HTML, a successful replacement with new body bytes and content_type=None returns the new bytes plus old text/html. save_content overwrites body but only writes MIME for Some and never deletes the old MIME key. Fresh None and explicit text/plain replacement controls behave correctly. This contradicts the documented None round-trip on replacement.
findings.scope: Synthetic URL/body/MIME in MemoryBackend only. This durable-cache defect is distinct from Q192 in PageLoad request observation; no browser rendering, live network, credential or installed cache was exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in active read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded body/metadata replacement
repair_triage.reason: Replace body and MIME as one shared backend batch, deleting the MIME key when the new response has none. Muniment apply already supplies the common batch seam; do not retain metadata from a different body or add another cache layer.

findings.title: Pack verification verdict changes when the same valid and malformed signatures are reordered
findings.status: native public signature-order counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The same signature multiset is Trusted with a valid binding first and Broken with a malformed binding first. verify_pack returns on the first personae binding despite its documentation describing whether some binding verifies. Single valid, malformed, unsigned and tampered-manifest controls retain their expected distinctions.
findings.scope: Synthetic Ed25519 key/manifest and actual sign_pack/verify_pack. No signature forgery, installed pack, executable payload, grant or visible-review bypass is claimed. The replacement mixed-signature policy is not chosen by this audit.

repair_triage.disposition: document mixed-signature policy decision
repair_triage.size: trust verdict semantics and compatibility
repair_triage.reason: Choose and document whether one valid author binding suffices or any claimed invalid author binding rejects the envelope, then evaluate the complete set consistently. Keep signature verification distinct from local installation review and grants.

findings.title: Manifest resolution writes a canonical cache it cannot reuse for remote-only or differently keyed sources
findings.status: native actual acquisition/cache/reopen counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A synthetic fetcher supplies valid bytes through actual resolve_blob, which caches them under blob:<hash>. Taking that fetcher offline makes the next resolution fail despite those valid cached bytes remaining present, for remote-only and nonmatching-Local manifests. Adding the canonical Local source makes the warm read work without another fetch. Corrupt declared cache bytes are still rejected.
findings.scope: Actual resolver and MemoryBackend with an in-process canned fetcher, no network. Normal save_typed manifests already declare the canonical Local key and are the working control. The original cache test only checks that a cache key was written, not that it can be read on a subsequent offline resolve.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in active read-only audit
repair_triage.size: bounded shared cache lookup/source normalization
repair_triage.reason: Make canonical cached identity usable on later resolution or explicitly require/adopt a canonical Local source when populating that cache. Preserve hash verification and the sealed-blob boundary; a successful cache write is not proof of a reusable cache.

findings.title: Built-in adapter and opaque payload schemas do not conform to the shared declared validator
findings.status: native exact built-in schema versus real typed binding counterexamples reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Each extracted canonical definition hashes to the runtime public schema reference. A valid ModelAdapterManifest cannot validate because its mere-native body uses unsupported number/integer and nullable-union type forms; the observed failure is unknown variant number. OpaqueBlob serializes raw bytes, but its definition requires a JSON object with a bytes-string field and rejects those bytes. Current TrainingCorpus validates against its own exact definition. Meta bootstrap leaves the adapter definition absent, and the documented tolerant unknown-schema path skips rather than proving validity.
findings.scope: Public actual typed bindings and common validator, exact schema constants, synthetic payloads and a fresh memory-store control. Retained Cargo-built libraries; reviewed sources unchanged. Actual ESP loader domain checks are separate, so failed real model loading, GPU execution or installed artifact migration is not claimed.

repair_triage.disposition: document schema compatibility repair; do not widen audit beyond one hour
repair_triage.size: shared schema/encoding authority and legacy identities
repair_triage.reason: Make declared schema format/encoding and Rust binding agree through one supported contract. Preserve old immutable schema references via explicit revisions/legacy readers or deliberate validator compatibility. Merely relabeling a format or patching canonical constants without migration can invalidate retained artifacts or silently weaken validation.

findings.title: Failed browsing-memory flush removes unsaved events before persistence succeeds
findings.status: public native counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: The actual public API loses an open segment when a synthetic backend rejects its first write. The error propagates, the store remains empty, but recent_corridor is empty and a later successful flush returns no ids. A successful-flush control retains the same event in memory and on reopen.
findings.scope: Synthetic memory stores/fault injection or bookmark JSON, actual public APIs and exact retained Cargo-built libraries. Reviewed source unchanged through authorized merges. No installed history, real disk failure, user profile, browser, rendering or live network exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: bounded repair candidate; production edits excluded by active audit objective
repair_triage.reason: Keep pending events owned by BrowsingMemory until save_trace succeeds; commit the in-memory transition after durable success. A partial content-addressed blob write may be orphaned, but must not consume the sole pending event copy.

findings.title: Failed forget drops unrelated loaded traces while the stored history survives
findings.status: public native counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: With three persisted traces and deletion refused for the middle target, forget_url returns the backend error but mem::take has emptied the entire loaded corpus, including the unrelated earlier/later traces. The store is unchanged. After allowing deletion, retry reports Ok(0), while reopening still yields all three traces. The ordinary forget control removes only its target and keeps the other two.
findings.scope: Synthetic memory stores/fault injection or bookmark JSON, actual public APIs and exact retained Cargo-built libraries. Reviewed source unchanged through authorized merges. No installed history, real disk failure, user profile, browser, rendering or live network exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: bounded repair candidate; production edits excluded by active audit objective
repair_triage.reason: Remove a loaded trace only after its required deletion succeeds, and preserve the unprocessed and unrelated rows on failure. Make partial-progress and retry behavior explicit; do not take the whole corpus before fallible awaits without restoring it.

findings.title: Chronological browsing reads concatenate owner segments and can select the wrong recent events
findings.status: public native counterexample reproduced; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: Two open owners named a and z with times20 and10 yield corridor[20,10] and recent(1)=[10]. findings.title: Finite native community proof can exit successfully before qualification completes
findings.status: source-only control-flow defect
findings.evidence: The 35-second finite deadline only sets ctx.close. Normal run return is checked for host errors, but no completion flag/result-file assertion survives after run. A deadline or user close before the final stage can therefore return normally without writing a new qualification.json. create_dir_all also permits reuse of an existing receipt directory, so a previous qualification may survive an incomplete new run. This does not invalidate the recorded historical successful run.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged while shared build remains active
repair_triage.reason: Contained: require explicit final-stage completion for finite success, refuse receipt-directory reuse and preserve incomplete-run evidence. A fresh headed positive/timeout/early-close control is still required.

findings.title: Closed applet host handles still own review and close operations on later mounts
findings.status: current JS adapter counterexamples with synthetic callbacks
findings.evidence: disposed gates only pump. Three current-module counterexamples show review after close calls the Rust review interface, a pending fetch/review installs after close, and repeated close on an old handle calls global applet_close and removes the WeakSet guard for a live remount. The duplicate-live-root control still refuses before the stale close. Rust review/close entry points are host operations without a prior-handle ownership token; generation checks on guest output do not qualify stale host lifecycle ownership. No forged signature or guest authorization bypass is claimed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged while shared build remains active
repair_triage.reason: Contained lifecycle correction: make close idempotent, validate live registration ownership before mutations and again after asynchronous preparation, and reject closed-handle review/turn. Bind current host registration rather than using a shared-root boolean alone.

findings.title: Auto renderer fallback drops the visible refusal when its second artifact fails to load
findings.status: current element-module counterexample with synthetic observer and route supplier
findings.evidence: The async observer disposes WebGPU and removes data-mount-error before awaiting source(webgl2), outside connectedCallback error handling. A rejected second load leaves data-mount-error absent and data-mounted true; another connectedCallback returns immediately. The focused diagnostic proves this DOM/latch state. Receipt pages can still catch the resulting unhandled rejection through loader.js; this is not proof that the full scenario gate passes. Original presentation-mount checks all pass.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged while shared build remains active
repair_triage.reason: Contained: handle second-route load/attach failure in the observer with the same epoch checks and visible failure/reset semantics as initial mounting. Preserve disposal ownership across disconnect/remount.

findings.title: Scenario receipt delivery reports HTTP rejection as delivered
findings.status: exact current listener counterexample and controls
findings.evidence: The listener awaits fetch but never checks response.ok before setting scenarioSink=delivered. Its exact unchanged handler reports delivered for a synthetic HTTP 500. A 204 control reports delivered, a transport rejection reports failed, and an existing planted page-gate failure still forces the scenario verdict to fail. External drivers waiting for a new scenario.done file do not thereby accept a missing receipt; the defect is the browser delivery claim.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged while shared build remains active
repair_triage.reason: Contained: distinguish successful HTTP acknowledgement from HTTP refusal and transport failure. Do not weaken the existing scenario error gate.

findings.title: Headed receipt driver records a failed scenario but returns normally
findings.status: unchanged current main exercised with synthetic dependencies
findings.evidence: After scenario.done appears, main copies scenario.result.result into environment.json, captures the page and prints the file, without raising or returning a failing exit status for fail. Running actual unchanged main against synthetic failed and successful receipts returns normally for both, while preserving the correct metadata verdict. This is a status propagation defect; no browser or headed acceptance ran. The adjacent run-presentation-webgl.py explicitly asserts its final pass verdict.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged while shared build remains active
repair_triage.reason: Contained: finish evidence capture and process cleanup, then make failed or missing scenario verdicts fail the command. Keep successful receipt control and infrastructure failures distinct.

findings.title: One receipt sink writes capture names outside its output directory
findings.status: exact current Handler counterexample with in-memory write interception
findings.evidence: For an allowed-origin JSON receipt, capture.name is interpolated directly into out/name.png. The exact Handler accepts ../escaped, attempts a write outside --out, then returns 204. An ordinary-name control stays inside; a wrong-origin control returns 403 without writes. The diagnostic intercepts all writes in memory. This is a local receipt-server containment defect, not an internet-exposed service claim. scenario_qualification_server sanitizes names and co_op_gateway rejects invalid names, so those separate implementations have different protections.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged while shared build remains active
repair_triage.reason: Contained: validate a bounded capture name and resolved containment before writes, reject duplicate/colliding names, and preserve receipt evidence. Share a small receipt-path policy without merging application owners.

findings.title: Component stylesheet positions navigation buttons outside the component
findings.status: source-only selector containment defect
findings.evidence: The stylesheet that embed.html loads has bare nav button:nth-child selectors, including width/height and left/top/bottom declarations and narrower-viewport overrides. They match navigation buttons belonging to the embedding document as well as Graphshell. The existing embed fixture tests a host input and button inside a paragraph, not host navigation, so those cases do not cover this selector leak. Broad [hidden], .button-row and .file-picker rules also remain page-global; the definite finding here is the nav geometry selectors, not a claim that every generic rule causes a demonstrated visual regression.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Contained selector scoping repair with a host navigation fixture at wide/narrow widths. No browser CSS/layout reproduction was run in this pass.

findings.title: Browser source advertises one shared workspace and a root gate that do not include it
findings.status: verified current Cargo metadata and source contradiction
findings.evidence: web.rs says graphshell-web remains a root workspace member sharing its lock and patch table, and recommends cargo check -p graphshell-web. The actual web manifest explicitly creates a standalone workspace and restates dependencies and patches. Locked/offline/no-deps Cargo metadata finds 104 root members with no graphshell-web, then one separate web-workspace member. A root workspace check therefore does not establish this browser crate was checked. No Wasm compilation or failure diagnostic for the recommended check command ran here.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Contained source-document correction: identify the standalone workspace and run its target gate from its own directory so the committed Wasm configuration is discovered. Retain the separate dependency/patch maintenance obligation; do not claim one lockfile or root-only coverage.

findings.title: A failed browser rejoin consumes the credentials needed for another reconnect
findings.status: source-only failed-reconnect ownership defect
findings.evidence: reconnect pops the only RetiredSession before starting asynchronous signaling, parks only its frames, then moves its ephemeral identity and delegation into rejoin. Any early error, such as a failed POST /offer, reaches the error callback without restoring the retired credentials. A second reconnect sees no retired session and refuses locally. Successful-reconnect scenarios exercise the one successful attempt, not transient failure followed by retry. This is loss of local retry capability, not proof that admission accepts invalid credentials.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Preserve logical reconnect identity/delegation through a failed attempt and retire channel objects separately. Add failure-then-success and revocation/expiry controls. Actual browser/transport reproduction remains open.

findings.title: Remote callbacks and retirement slots are not bound to the connection they update
findings.status: source-only connection-generation and ownership defect
findings.evidence: connect can start another join against the same TreeRemote, and adopt replaces its live session. Existing read pumps capture that shared host and call received/stream_closed without checking that their original connection is still current; the real TreeRemote implementation applies those callbacks to its current reservoir/live. A displaced join completion can likewise adopt later. Separately, RETIRED is one thread-local LIFO stack with no logical-host/session key, and reconnect pops whichever session retired last. This source path can misroute old callbacks or select unrelated reconnect state; no live cross-peer disclosure or authorization bypass was demonstrated.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Hairy issue deferred: bind joins, pumps, closure notifications and retired credentials to explicit logical-host/connection identity, fence stale completion, and specify bounded callback retirement. This crosses carrier closure lifetime, reservoir state and browser-host adoption; document it rather than prolong this source review with a broad lifecycle redesign.

findings.title: Five historical packagers manufacture fixed passing-test totals from successful command records
findings.status: verified exact unchanged scripts with in-memory counterexamples and refusal controls
findings.evidence: The scripts assert the expected record count and zero exit codes, then assign CPU test totals of 68, 72, 72, 83 or 88 and true continuation flags. They do not derive those totals from successful, nonempty named tests. Executing each exact unchanged script with in-memory filesystem/process substitutes and the expected number of zero-test successful records returns normally and emits those positive claims. Ten controls with a failed exit or missing record correctly refuse before writes. These are rerun verification weaknesses; the probe does not establish that the dated original test totals were false.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; historical evidence preserved; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Keep immutable historical scripts and original receipts. A maintained future packaging gate should validate named gate identity and actual test results against its declared required cases before generating acceptance totals.

findings.title: Historical packagers relabel existing artifacts with current source without proving their build basis
findings.status: verified exact unchanged scripts with in-memory counterexamples and refusal controls
findings.evidence: All five scripts consume existing Wasm artifacts, run bindgen/copy, then overwrite candidate source HEAD and source-byte hashes from the current checkout while setting packaging_complete and CPU/Wasm-qualified status. No checked build-basis record connects those artifact bytes with that source. The same five in-memory executions retain an earlier-A binary while successfully emitting newer-B HEAD/source labels. Bundle hashes describe the supplied bytes accurately; they do not establish which source built them. This demonstrates an attribution gap on rerun, not a proved mismatch in the original dated packages.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; historical evidence preserved; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Retain historical evidence. Future maintained packaging should require an immutable successful build record binding exact source, feature/target/toolchain configuration and produced artifact digests; reject a mismatch rather than refreshing source labels over existing binaries.

findings.title: Receipt dry run writes its database and artifacts before saying nothing was written
findings.status: source-only complete CLI and owner trace
findings.evidence: run creates the store parent, opens RedbBackend, and awaits ingest_directory before inspecting args.dry_run. RedbBackend::open creates/materializes/commits a database table, and each artifact goes through BlobStore::put to a committed backend write. Only graph-events.json and inbox deposit are skipped when the CLI prints dry run: nothing written. This is a definite mutation/reporting contradiction from the current source; no actual user database or CLI invocation was used.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Contained repair: choose an ephemeral store or validation-only ingest path before any durable open/write, or explicitly define and disclose a staging-only mode rather than promising nothing written.

findings.title: Unknown receipt provenance survives parsing but is discarded from the replicated facts
findings.status: source-only complete parser-to-events trace
findings.evidence: ReceiptManifest flattens unknown fields into extra and promises they are preserved untouched so newer-lane provenance is not lost on ingest. run_facet serializes a fixed list and omits extra; the other emitted facet contains artifacts only, and the source manifest itself is not a stored blob. The test unknown_manifest_fields_survive only parses and checks extra, so it never crosses the lossy conversion. For example a gpu field is retained in the temporary Rust value and then absent from graph events.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Contained repair: preserve a versioned/namespaced extra-provenance object in the run facet, with collision rules, and test the events after actual ingest rather than only the parser.

findings.title: An empty producer digest silently disables receipt artifact verification
findings.status: source-only artifact-integrity contract contradiction
findings.evidence: The manifest parser accepts an empty sha256 string. ingest_manifest checks a mismatch only when the string is nonempty, then stores the received bytes and writes their newly computed digest into receipt.artifacts. The module claims it verifies the producing machine digest rather than trusting arrived bytes, but this path has no producer digest to compare. The declared artifact.bytes is also unused for verification. Host BLAKE3 restaging checks bytes against the locally produced event hash, so it cannot recover the missing original producer check.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Contained repair: validate a producer SHA-256 format and required size, or explicitly distinguish an unverified legacy import in the graph/card. A computed local hash is not a successful producer-digest comparison.

findings.title: Receipt timestamp parsing is neither total nor faithful to the claimed RFC3339 format
findings.status: six native observations of verbatim current function; full importer not executed
findings.evidence: The exact current parse_rfc3339_ms function panics on a non-ASCII fractional string because [..3] can split UTF-8. A huge i64 year also panics in checked native arithmetic. A +05:30 offset is silently ignored; a fractional -05:30 offset is likewise ignored while an integral-second negative offset returns None. 2026-02-30 is accepted. Thus ran_at_ms does not always turn unsupported input into the promised unknown=0 and can emit a wrong observation time. The original UTC/invalid-text control passes. Initial probe expected all negative offsets to refuse; that expectation failed on the fractional case and is preserved, with a distinct corrected six-case probe.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
