repair_triage.reason: Contained repair: use a validated shared date parser or a strict checked UTC-only grammar, reject unsupported offsets explicitly, validate calendar/time ranges and avoid byte slicing or unchecked arithmetic. Preserve original timestamp text alongside explicit parse status.

findings.title: Unknown receipt results receive a Failed badge
findings.status: source-only card result inconsistency
findings.evidence: Missing or invalid exit_code produces Result=unknown but passed=false, so the badge branch adds Failed. The sparse-run test checks the Result value and never checks badges. A reader skimming the badge receives a failure claim that the run facet does not establish. Normal zero/nonzero results are rendered separately and correctly.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Contained repair: derive Result and badge from one three-state outcome, with an Unknown badge or an omitted outcome badge for unknown.

findings.title: A non-UTF8 inbox file aborts intake for all healthy pending receipts
findings.status: source-only library-to-live-host intake trace
findings.evidence: pending skips JSON syntax errors but std::fs::read_to_string uses ?, so one .json file containing invalid UTF-8, an unreadable file or a directory named *.json aborts the entire scan. The host logs the scan failure and retries the same batch ten seconds later, never receiving the healthy pending entries. This contradicts the documented isolation of malformed handoffs. Even valid-UTF8 malformed JSON is silently skipped without a per-file diagnostic returned to the caller, despite the comment saying the caller logs it. No host or filesystem fault injection ran.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Contained repair: isolate and report each unreadable/unparseable entry, continue scanning valid files, and leave or quarantine failed handoffs without an endless whole-inbox failure.

findings.title: Receipt artifact names can resolve outside their selected source directory
findings.status: source-only manifest-path confinement defect
findings.evidence: Artifact name is an arbitrary deserialized string and ingest reads dir.join(name) without rejecting rooted paths, parent traversal or escaping links. The host later repeats receipt.source.join(name). An absolute path replaces the joined base on the current platform; ../ paths escape it. Consequently a supplied remote receipt can cause import of a local file outside the chosen receipt directory, especially when Q276 allows an empty producer digest. The host checks that later staged bytes match the graph hash, which binds content but does not confine the chosen source path. No sensitive files were accessed and no peer disclosure was executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Validate confined relative artifact names and resolve symlink/reparse escape under the selected directory before read. Keep local privileged inbox editing distinct from accepting untrusted producer paths. This needs a deliberate path policy, not a blanket claim that content hashing provides source confinement.

findings.title: G5 returns success after a peer closes before completing its request script
findings.status: source-only premature-success exit path
findings.evidence: run_session prints that the endpoint closed without answering, breaks the script and returns Ok with whatever responses arrived. An immediate EOF after first admission yields an empty vector; connect returns Ok before the interruption and remaining sessions. An EOF later likewise does not require the expected response count, ids or outcomes. Therefore exit zero alone does not establish the rehearsal was completed. A deliberate grant refusal is also an expected observation in this tool, so this finding concerns unexpected EOF and incomplete scripts, not the mere existence of a normal reported refusal.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Separate observation mode from a qualification mode that asserts expected request ids, complete response sequences and declared granted/revoked outcomes. Reuse the existing SessionDriver or checked H6 request loop rather than another loosely checked wire loop.

findings.title: C4 concurrency coverage is claimed by a test that closes each visitor before opening the next
findings.status: source-only acceptance-scope mismatch; no product serialization proved
findings.evidence: The test module says it proves a second visitor is served rather than queued behind the first. join_and_count sends Close, drops its line stream, awaits the pump and closes the carrier before returning. The test awaits that entire first call before beginning the second. Both visitors passing therefore proves repeat sequential admission, not overlapping live sessions; a host that serialized visitors until close could also satisfy this ordering. The host itself spawns service tasks, and this review does not establish that actual concurrency is broken.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Keep the first mounted session open, mount/use a second concurrently within a bounded deadline, then verify both still serve independent requests before closing them.

findings.title: Native Mere viewer duplicates the shared route state machine and silently accepts absent scoped material
findings.status: source-only live duplicated policy and demonstrated branch divergence
findings.evidence: The browser uses MereRouteSession with SessionDriver, and the shared type already implements the native LineDriven seam. The native binary independently sequences snapshots, resources, merge choices, application/session/epoch checks, saved view, archive state and intents through Connection and a worker. If an explicit session card lacks its scoped media, the shared route rejects it. The native session_graph_request helper returns None and Connection::read skips the entire validation block, retaining previous saved_view/read_only and returning a Reading. Thus sharing rendering and pure route helpers does not make validation or lifecycle single-owned. This is a source-path counterexample, not a live peer exploit or wrong-file-store mutation.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Hairy seam documented: make the native transport drive the shared route state machine, retaining native wake/UI adaptation; specify current application/session/material identity and purge semantics. Do not extend the audit with a broad worker/connection rewrite. A bounded refusal for explicit missing material can be repaired separately.

findings.title: Chronicle receipt fields commit rejected snapshot and resume attempts as though applied
findings.status: verified fresh current module over hash-bound retained dependency libraries
findings.evidence: mount sets snapshot_revision before ClientState accepts the snapshot; resume sets resumed_by_diff from the reply variant before apply_resume succeeds or reports Resynchronize. The public receipt then mixes those attempted values with the unchanged acknowledged scene. Three native counterexamples show wrong-session resume returning Err while resumed_by_diff=true at revision 1, a missing-base diff returning Resynchronize with the same false flag, and a rejected revision-999 snapshot stamped over acknowledged revision 1. A normal applied diff reaches revision 2 as its positive control. The shared ClientState correctly preserves the old acknowledged scene; the adapter bookkeeping creates the misleading report.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Commit receipt metadata after successful application, distinguish resynchronization from applied replay, and retain attempt/error observations separately from acknowledged state.

findings.title: Chronicle accepts a self-validating resource different from the one it requested
findings.status: verified fresh current module over hash-bound retained dependency libraries
findings.evidence: refresh_details checks response.has_valid_address but does not compare response.resource or response.session with its requested pair. A supplied endpoint can therefore return another correctly hashed PortableCard, and its values enter the requested instance frozen details. A native synthetic endpoint advertising PortableCard and returning a different self-validating card produces the substituted text in frozen_html. This parallels the previously reported shared presentation-resolution request-binding gap Q062; it is a separate direct endpoint adapter path, while Pending::MediaResource already checks scope, requested address and content hash. No actual remote admission or authorization bypass was exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Check both response scope and the exact requested hash before decoding, preferably through the shared checked resource path. A self-consistent content hash does not prove it is the requested content.

findings.title: Arbitrary facet fields shadow the canonical address used by saved-view actions
findings.status: verified exact current facet functions over real retained types; saved-view consumer path source-traced
findings.evidence: add_node_facets prepends flattened arbitrary facet fields to PortableCard display values. Both shared view_invocation and native Connection::take select the first value labelled Address for ViewIntent.focus; shared view_saved uses the same label. The exact current functions over real Chartulary facet storage produce a supplied facet Address before the still-present canonical owner address. No-facet and lowercase-address controls keep the canonical first match. This verifies ambiguous data selection and traces its use in saved-view payload construction; it does not claim a completed owner SetView action, durable wrong focus, GUI exploit or authorization bypass.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Carry canonical identity/address separately from arbitrary human-labelled display values, and have actions use that typed owner material. Both native and shared route consumers need the same rule.

findings.title: Mere-view assigns focus after folding, bypassing its stand-in remapping
findings.status: verified original current Mere-view crate over hash-bound retained dependency libraries
findings.evidence: MereView::swatch applies folds::project while the new Swatch focus is still None, then assigns state.focused afterward. The fold projector remaps focus only when it receives a member focus, so its intended focus_request path is unreachable from this caller. A public-method probe builds a valid summary fold over a,b: a disappears, the summary exists, focus remains a, and focus_request is None. Unfolded a and visible nonmember c remain valid controls. Rendered DOM focus movement, native keyboard input and GPU paint were not exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Provide hover/focus inputs before the final fold transform and avoid overwriting transformed focus. Verify both summary and member stand-ins through the actual component host before claiming UI acceptance.

findings.title: Hand drafts survive replacement by a different merge with the same conflict key
findings.status: verified original current Mere-view crate over hash-bound retained dependency libraries
findings.evidence: MereViewState retains merge_drafts solely by conflict key, without the pending MergeModel source or generation. Replacing Some(merge from branch 1) directly with Some(merge from branch 2), sharing a title conflict key but different values, preserves the old hand draft. The renderer prefers that draft over the new target/chosen-hand seed and uses it in the Edit by hand request. Public state/event methods reproduce retention; same-merge continuity, a different key, and None cleanup pass as controls. Actual rendered button invocation and durable owner merge application were not executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Bind drafts to a pending merge identity and conflict evidence; clear or explicitly rebase them when that identity changes. Preserve ordinary same-plan editing continuity.

findings.title: Context menus accept recursive command trees but cannot disclose grandchildren
findings.status: verified original current modules over hash-bound retained dependencies
findings.evidence: The recursive CommandItem tree is shared, but interaction is not: CommandState stores one submenu parent while CommandMenuBarState stores a recursive path. For File -> Export -> HTML, the actual current context-menu module renders Export but never HTML. Enter emits Activate([0,0]) for the non-leaf Export; pointer activation merely reopens the first submenu. The same tree through the actual current menubar reaches HTML and emits Activate([0,0,0]). CommandEvent documentation does acknowledge depth-one submenus, so this finding concerns accepted unsupported tree structure and misleading non-leaf activation, not an undocumented promise of recursive context-menu support. No application command backend was executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Either reject/explicitly lower deeper trees at the shared boundary or use a shared recursive traversal policy. Keep presentation-specific focus behavior separate while giving the same command tree a declared supported shape.

findings.title: Open submenus still activate children after the parent group becomes disabled
findings.status: verified original current modules over hash-bound retained dependencies
findings.evidence: Both engines retain open submenu paths across a model refresh that disables the ancestor group. Their activation checks examine the selected child only. A live headless runner opens File, refreshes File as disabled because Disconnected while its Open child is still individually enabled, and Enter emits Activate([0,0]) in both context-menu and menubar modules. An individually disabled child remains inert as its control. This is inconsistent UI availability/invalidation, not evidence of backend authorization bypass; command executors were not invoked.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Validate every ancestor when normalizing an open path and before emitting activation. Close/refuse stale open paths through one shared command availability rule.

findings.title: Inserting a combining mark corrupts the grapheme caret and moves subsequent text past the suffix
findings.status: verified original current modules over hash-bound retained dependencies
findings.evidence: insert_str increments its grapheme caret by the inserted fragment grapheme count without resegmenting the splice. A combining mark joins the preceding grapheme, so inserting U+0301 after a produces one grapheme with caret=2; the first Backspace removes no text. In ab, insertion at byte 1 produces a+acute+b but caret_position jumps after b, and the next x produces a+acute+bx instead of a+acute+xb. Current original TextInput/editor modules reproduce both paths through TextCommand::Insert. Constructing the same combined buffer initially and ordinary x insertion behave correctly as controls. No native IME, host field or persisted document was exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Track the splice endpoint in byte space and derive a valid caret from segmentation of the resulting buffer, with explicit boundary affinity. Cover combining, ZWJ and regional-indicator joins across the insertion boundary.

findings.title: TextCommand reports no change when a boundary caret move cancels visible composition
findings.status: verified original current modules over hash-bound retained dependencies
findings.evidence: TextInput::apply documents whether logical or composition state changed, but Move, SelectAll and SetSelection compare only caret_selection after clearing preedit. The native module probe puts a composition at the start of a, applies GraphemeLeft without extension, and receives false even though the composition vanishes and rendered text changes from candidate+a to a. Explicit CancelComposition returns true as its control. Only the Move counterexample was executed; the other two branches are source-traced. No audited caller was established to gate redraw/persistence on this false result, so user-visible missed redraw is not claimed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Include composition changes in the declared changed result, or narrow the API contract and return separate committed/selection/composition change flags.

findings.title: Retained click listeners ignore changes to capture mode while key listeners update correctly
findings.status: verified original current Cambium crate over hash-bound retained dependency artifacts
findings.evidence: OnClick::rebuild refreshes its registration only when the node or routing path changes, omitting self.capture != prev.capture. With the same live nodes, changing an ancestor from bubble to capture leaves child,parent click order. A freshly built capture listener produces parent,child, and the parallel OnKey::rebuild correctly updates capture mode in place. The original current toolkit runner/wrappers reproduce all three cases. The registration logic was copied between sibling wrappers and has drifted; no native platform input or application action was exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Reconcile capture as part of click listener registration identity, using the same changed-field discipline already implemented by OnKey. Keep ordinary node/path retention and multi-listener removal intact.

findings.title: Frisket promises pane-state preservation that only holds in one tree-order direction
findings.status: verified original current Cambium crate over hash-bound retained dependency artifacts
findings.evidence: PortableKeyed explicitly documents source-before-target preservation; target-before-source builds fresh and later tears down the parked original. Frisket advertises cross-stack DOM/view-state preservation without that caveat, and its test explicitly chooses earlier source then later target. A fresh current toolkit probe moves an active tile with component-local count=1 between two non-collapsing stacks. Left-to-right preserves the same node/count; right-to-left retires the old node and initializes count=0. This verifies local presentation-state loss, not loss of a persisted source document. Multi-window behavior and layout rendering were not exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Document the actual bound at the Frisket contract now. Order-independent preservation needs a coordinated pre-park/adoption or retained-mount design; keep that larger repair separate from a one-direction passing receipt. Broad lifetime/ownership repair is deferred under the user audit-diversion limit.

findings.title: Composed focus observers silently replace the inner handler on the same element
findings.status: verified original current Cambium crate over hash-bound retained dependency artifacts
findings.evidence: OnFocus is an ElementView and accepts another OnFocus as its child, but both register the same node in a single HashMap<NodeId,path>. Building the outer observer overwrites the inner route. A current toolkit runner focus/blur cycle delivers only the outer handler twice, while both typed observers remain in the view tree. The module describes one handler per child, so the verified issue is accepted silent wrapper composition with a lost inner observer, not a documented multi-listener guarantee. No existing product consumer requiring nested focus observers was established.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Either support a per-node observer list with path-specific teardown, as click/key already do, or make the single-observer composition limit explicit and enforce it rather than silently overwriting.

findings.title: stop_propagation suppresses same-node listeners despite the shared cancellation contract
findings.status: verified original current Cambium crate over hash-bound retained dependency artifacts
findings.evidence: Propagation says ordinary stop allows the current node other listeners, while immediate stop also suppresses them. RunnerTree flattens node/phase groups to paths, then breaks on stopped() after each listener in both click and key dispatch. The immediate flag has no distinct dispatcher consumption. Current toolkit probes with two same-node listeners plus an ancestor show all three without cancellation, but only the first with either ordinary or immediate stop. The stale comment claiming at most one listener per node contradicts the current vector registries. Only native toolkit synthetic dispatch was executed; no JavaScript dispatcher parity run was made.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Retain node/phase grouping through dispatch and distinguish ordinary stop from immediate stop when deciding whether to continue same-node listeners. Test both event types against the declared contract before claiming convergence.

findings.title: View-requested focus updates the focus seat without notifying focus observers
findings.status: verified original current Cambium crate over hash-bound retained dependency artifacts
findings.evidence: Direct set_focus and click focus call route_focus_transition, but build/rebuild consumption of FocusRequest assigns self.focus directly. With a current request_focus/on_focus widget initially unfocused, changing requested to true seats focus on the live root and leaves the observer log empty. Direct set_focus(None) and set_focus(root) then emit Lost and Gained as a control. This contradicts on_focus saying programmatic focus changes emit transitions and leaves observer-maintained state distinct from the actual focus seat. The rebuild counterexample was executed; initial-build notification absence is source-traced. No headed focus or accessibility adapter was run.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Commit all focus-seat changes through one transition/publication path, including deferred view requests, with a bounded reconciliation rule for handlers that request another focus change. Broader event/rebuild ordering needs care; record rather than introduce a second local workaround.

findings.title: Collapsed disclosure actions remain in Tab traversal and can activate while hidden
findings.status: verified original current Cambium crate over hash-bound retained dependency artifacts
findings.evidence: Disclosure keeps its child controls mounted under a hidden=true panel. collect_focusables walks every descendant carrying a key/focusability registration without pruning authored hidden ancestors. In the current toolkit runner a closed disclosure trigger Tabs directly to its hidden action, and Space invokes that action while the panel remains closed. Opening the panel makes the same traversal an ordinary visible-control case. This is an actual component plus synthetic native-runner keyboard path, not a headed rendering, screen-reader or backend authorization receipt. Computed-style visibility is a separate host concern; the counterexample only relies on the authored hidden attribute.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Apply authored hidden/inert ancestry at the common focus eligibility boundary and keep computed-style visibility supplied by the host. Test collapsed/expanded controls through actual focus traversal, including transitions that hide a focused subtree.

findings.title: Reordering graph nodes separates the focused logical identity from the keyboard activation target
findings.status: verified original current Cambium crate over hash-bound retained dependencies
findings.evidence: Node targets are an unkeyed Vec retained by position, while focus emphasis is retained as a logical Id. Reordering two existing logical nodes reuses the focused DOM node for the other Id without a focus transition. A current-toolkit probe focuses node 1 then swaps the graph nodes: the same DOM seat now represents node 2, node 1 still carries the focused class, and Enter emits activation for node 2. The callback-owned and component-owned APIs both reproduce it. Initial focus and an explicit blur/refocus to logical node 1 work as controls. The optional data-key is correctly emitted, but only automation metadata; its presence does not preserve view identity. No paint leaf, native input or persisted owner action was executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Key retained node targets by logical identity, or explicitly reconcile the DOM focus seat when order/membership changes. Reconcile local emphasis against valid identities without silently transferring keyboard activation to a different node.

findings.title: Graph relation and Expand buttons are pointer actions missing from keyboard traversal
findings.status: verified original current Cambium crate over hash-bound retained dependencies
findings.evidence: Node buttons use focusable/on_focus, but relation targets and the Expand button use bare on_click. The current runner registers explicit focusability or key handlers rather than deriving Tab seats from HTML button tags. A current-toolkit probe finds both buttons and verifies their pointer callbacks, but neither is in focusables(); Tab cycles only between node buttons. This is absence from toolkit keyboard traversal, not a claim about every accessibility bridge or headed host. The existing graph-canvas source tests invoke these actions directly by pointer and do not test their Tab reachability.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Use the shared clickable/button focusability path for relation and Expand actions, preserving relation hover, endpoint stacking and consumer action ownership. Verify complete Tab traversal and Enter/Space activation through the runner.

findings.title: Forest projections replace moved view state despite claiming cross-window preservation
findings.status: verified original current default-feature toolkit over retained exact dependency artifacts
findings.evidence: push_forest_projection shares one ScriptedDom but creates a separate RunnerTree/GenetCtx for each window. Each rebuild drains its own portable nursery before the next projection runs. Sharing the document therefore does not make parked children claimable across contexts. In current original toolkit probes, moving the same stateful Frisket tile from projection 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0 updates shared owner truth, retires the original node and resets component-local count from 1 to 0. An unchanged-owner refresh preserves both, and the distinct RetainedMount path preserves its actual runner/node/count across a destination-first mount. The forest source tests only establish sibling roots and shared counter refresh, not the advertised cross-window preservation. No native windows, scroll or animation were exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Qualify the forest API documentation to its actual shared-document/single-state guarantee and route retained owner moves through the tested RetainedMount contract. General cross-context portable adoption would require coordinated custody and lifecycle changes; defer that broad repair under the audit-diversion limit. This is broader than Q294 single-tree ordering loss.

findings.title: The modal overlay flag advertises modal isolation while background controls remain keyboard-active
findings.status: verified original current default-feature toolkit over retained exact dependency artifacts
findings.evidence: OverlaySurface::modal(true) adds a modal class and, for Dialog, aria-modal=true; it does not establish a focus scope or make background controls inert. A current toolkit runner renders a background button and this modal dialog, focuses the inside button, Tabs to the background, and Space invokes its callback while aria-modal remains true. A nonmodal control keeps the same background reachability without that ARIA claim. No in-tree .modal(true) product call site was found in the searched Cambium/ports Rust source, so this is a verified public API/semantic gap rather than a demonstrated deployed modal bypass. No headed host or accessibility bridge was executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; no production changes
repair_triage.reason: Either implement modality through a shared focus/input scope owned by the host/runner, or expose this flag as semantics-only with an explicit required host contract. Avoid having each overlay invent another partial modal controller; broader focus-scope design stays documented.

findings.title: Sectioned-list keyboard activation discards the action it promises to bubble
findings.evidence: The click closure returns OptionalAction from the shared row handler. The key closure invokes the same handler but assigns its result to let _, then returns unit. Current original toolkit execution with a nonunit Navigate action proves pointer activation returns Navigate, whereas both Enter and Space mutate the same local hit counter but return no action. Existing source tests only check in-place state changes from clicks and never assert a keyboard action. Source commentary explicitly promises that the key action bubbles. Searches of current in-tree crates/ports Rust found only the module test call site; a deployed product navigation failure was not established.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Contained repair: return the OptionalAction from handled keyboard branches and use a compatible empty result for other keys; verify both direct and optional action outputs. No new command authority is needed.

findings.status: verified original current default-feature toolkit over retained exact dependency artifacts

findings.title: ContainedSession invokes the second leaf-registry call outside its panic boundary
findings.evidence: ContainedSession::leaves first calls session.leaves().is_some() inside catch_unwind, then calls session.leaves() again outside the catch to return the mutable reference. A deterministic valid trait implementation returning Some on its first call and panicking on its second proves the panic escapes to an outer harness catch, failure() remains None and availability still reports Available. A first-call panic control is caught and retires the guest as Unhealthy; a stable registry control succeeds. This contradicts the every-call-contained guarantee. The test uses current original toolkit code and synthetic trait implementations, not a demonstrated failing deployed guest or a native host crash.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Keep the actual mutable-reference-producing invocation inside the boundary. Refactor disjoint field borrowing or the registry access contract rather than using an unguarded second call; returned leaf measure/paint panics are a separate host boundary to inspect.

findings.status: verified original current default-feature toolkit over retained exact dependency artifacts

findings.title: Raising a floating pane transfers component-local state to another tile
findings.status: verified original current default-feature toolkit over retained exact dependency artifacts
findings.evidence: workspace_view_with_marks and the presented variant build the visible floating tiles as an unkeyed Vec<PaneView>. Workspace activation raises a float by changing its z order, so the positional child view state is rebuilt with a different tile prop. In the executed current workspace_view path, float 1 owns count 1 and float 2 owns count 0; an unchanged-order refresh preserves both. Raising float 1 reuses its node/count for float 2 and the original float-2 node/count for float 1. Another real button click increments the wrong-owner inherited count to 2. The host workspace and model identity change correctly; the view custody is positional. This is distinct from the documented tree/float or cross-projection rebuild boundary because neither tile changes station. The presented path shares the same unkeyed construction and renderer by source trace, but was not separately executed. No native floating windows, layout, persistence or product-local owner data were exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Key the floating view sequence by TileId in both rendering entry points and preserve the existing shared float renderer. Verify raise, close, hidden unpinned floats and presented variants with distinct component state and focus. Do not add a second persisted pane store.

findings.title: Hook-queued pointer events recursively overtake events already waiting in the host queue
findings.status: verified original current toolkit and Rootstock over retained exact suppliers
findings.evidence: drain_pointer takes the current pending queue, but each delivered event can call after_dispatch -> with_ctx -> apply_pending -> drain_pointer again. An after_dispatch hook that queues another event therefore recursively drains it before the next event in the already-taken batch. The original current Host probe queues zoom-in A and zoom-out B. Without hook-enqueued work the hook observes [1.1,1.0]. When A queues zoom-in C, one outer drain observes [1.1,1.25,1.1], demonstrating A,C,B ordering, with C already consumed instead of pending for a later drain. This contradicts the source promise that the queue is ordered and hook-enqueued work lands on the next drain rather than looping. The fixture bounds itself to one extra event; no unbounded loop, stack overflow, native event source or product failure was executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Track an active queue-drain turn and defer nested drains until that turn ends, preserving the chosen FIFO/next-turn contract. Exercise already-queued events plus hook-enqueued pointer and wheel work. Do not create another replay dispatcher or rely on every application hook to suppress recursion.

findings.title: Host visual-caret correction overwrites correct toolkit selection with a separate scalar editor
findings.status: verified original current toolkit and Rootstock over retained exact suppliers
findings.evidence: OwnedLayout::selection_visual_move does not consult shaped line/bidi geometry: it concatenates DOM text, walks Unicode scalar boundaries, treats LineStart/LineEnd as buffer ends and collapses from the selection focus instead of the correct selection edge. Host::move_focused_text_visual overwrites the logical result with this answer whenever layout exists and default is unprevented. Eight original-current checks compare otherwise-identical Hosts with/without layout: multiline Home from byte 4 in ab\ncd correctly goes to 3 without layout but 0 with it; End from byte 1 correctly goes to 2 but is overwritten to 5; Left on selection 1..3 in abcd correctly collapses to 1 but becomes 2; Right from the start of a-combining-acute+b correctly advances to byte 3 but the layout correction snaps it back to byte 0. These are actual Host/model observations, not native key injection or visual/bidi acceptance.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: A narrow repair can stop replacing valid toolkit movement with this nonvisual fallback. A real visual move must delegate to shaped layout/selection authority while preserving grapheme, selection-edge, multiline and modifier semantics; document broad bidi/soft-wrap restoration rather than inventing another editor.

findings.title: Optional embedding frame initialization omits the current required producer purpose
findings.status: compiler-confirmed exact current initializer against fresh current public type; full optional feature graph not built
findings.evidence: ProducerFrameInfo now requires purpose to distinguish Presentation from Export. embedding::View::frame still initializes logical/physical size, scale, needs_frame, timestamp and appearance without purpose. The exact initializer text extracted from current embedding.rs, in a minimal receiver fixture, compiles against freshly built original current Rootstock and produces only E0063 missing field purpose. The no-optional-feature original Rootstock builds first, demonstrating why those passing builds miss the inactive module. The first extraction harness could not resolve the fresh Cambium dependency (E0463); it is retained as a failed diagnostic and a distinct v2 explicitly loads that dependency. No whole embedding/egui/Iced feature build, GPU or runtime claim is made.

repair_triage.disposition: documented; production unchanged under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Supply the intended producer purpose at the actual embedding frame boundary and verify its presentation/export behavior. Include the optional embedding feature in its own gate; a default host build is not coverage for inactive modules.

findings.title: Browser key conversion calls Unicode scalars graphemes and discards multi-scalar text keys
findings.status: source-verified conversion counterexample; browser/OS key delivery not executed
findings.evidence: The exported key_press_from_dom contract and match comment promise exactly one grapheme, but the admission test is other.chars().count() == 1. A key string a followed by combining acute has two Unicode scalar values and is consequently Key::Named(Other) with text None; the same is true of a multi-scalar emoji grapheme. Dead and Unidentified are explicitly special-cased, so neither fallback restores that text. The installed canvas and mirror keydown listeners call this exact converter. This establishes loss for such an input value at the API boundary; it does not claim an observed physical keyboard, browser layout or IME reproducer.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Use the shared text/grapheme policy for deciding text keys, preserving named/dead-key handling. Verify real browser key and composition routes separately rather than treating scalar count as grapheme segmentation.

findings.title: Public browser file chooser permanently forgets callbacks that retain its removed input
findings.status: source-verified ownership leak in exported non-lifetime constructor; no browser heap measurement
findings.evidence: WebFileChooser::new delegates to new_inner with no MountLifetime. That branch installs change/cancel listeners and calls Closure::forget on both, with no stored callback or removal token. The change closure captures a clone of input and pending; Drop only takes pending and removes the element. Removing the DOM element cannot drop the deliberately forgotten Rust closure, so each such construction leaves callback/input state allocated for the remaining module lifetime. The normal mount.rs call uses new_with_lifetime and registers removable callbacks; repository search found no call to the public new path. The separate owned implementation thus has materially different cleanup semantics despite returning the same RAII-looking chooser.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Store and remove standalone callbacks on chooser drop, or make this constructor explicitly owned by a supplied lifetime. Do not change group-owned device or mount disposal authority.

findings.title: T4 receipt program exits successfully without enforcing its comparison or completeness conditions
findings.status: source-verified success-path defect; full GPU fixture not executed
findings.evidence: The capture path records matched and non_vacuous booleans, but after run returns main only formats those fields into results_raw.md, writes it and prints wrote receipt. It never rejects false matches, false non-vacuity, missing pairs/timing samples, absent lower counters or a changed Path-B counter. In particular control_lower_before == control_lower_after reports true for None == None. Closing before collecting all fixtures or collecting failed comparisons can therefore end normally and return process status 0, provided the event loop and file I/O themselves succeed. Raw report booleans may disclose failure to a human, but a successful process is not an acceptance gate for this receipt. No observed pixel pass/failure or actual fixture exit was run.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Add an explicit complete-case acceptance predicate and fail the process on missing/failed conditions. Require both counter readings to exist; record timing sample completeness separately from correctness.

findings.title: T4 unlayered reference is placed into the wrong column by its own later CSS
findings.status: verified original extracted pair/style functions with actual current runner/retained layout over exact retained suppliers
findings.evidence: pair_view constructs the bare control style with left:616px;top:16px and then appends plain_style(dx,dy,...), which declares left/top again. At the first fixture offset 4,4 the unchanged extracted original functions, real current Cambium Runner and Rootstock OwnedLayout report the bare control rect (4,4,64,48). It is consequently outside the intended third reference column and can cover the retained-path column instead. Comparing the third crop against the layered reference is not the claimed non-vacuity control. The full native/GPU T4 run was not executed; equal-width frame cropping versus fixed 300px panel spacing is a further source follow-up.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Place the unlayered content inside a separate positioned column, or compose the intended absolute coordinates once. Derive captures from actual panel bounds and require independent non-vacuity and matching gates.

findings.title: Native caption control lookup substitutes raw aria-label for the shared accessible-name authority
findings.status: verified exact extracted lookup against actual current neutral accessibility projection over retained exact suppliers; no OS hit-test run
findings.evidence: window_control_node says it reuses button semantics and the accessible label rather than adding a second native-only marker, but it recursively matches only button/role plus raw aria-label. Three real ScriptedDom/OwnedLayout/projection checks show text-only Maximize and aria-labelledby Maximize have the proper shared projected name but are not found by native lookup; a raw Maximize aria-label overridden by aria-labelledby Agrandir is still selected as Maximize by the native lookup, while the projection correctly announces Agrandir. WinitHost::refresh_snap_layout_rect calls this helper for the Win32 maximize region, making native target identity diverge from shared semantic identity. This proves lookup/projection disagreement, not observed Win32 Snap UI behavior.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Resolve control role/name through the shared accessible semantics and visibility authority, then map that same node to painted bounds. Do not grow another native-only naming algorithm.

findings.title: Native accessibility bypasses retained scroll correction and reports unscrolled control bounds
findings.status: verified actual current DOM/Host/layout with unchanged extracted native lowering over exact retained suppliers
findings.evidence: Rootstock document_projection rewrites bounds with OwnedLayout::painted_rect after generic semantic projection. The browser consumes that projection. Native project_tree_with_actions calls genet_render::accesskit_tree_with_style directly with raw fragments and neither scroll offsets nor the Rootstock correction, then scales only the tree root. Two real current Host checks, one viewport and one nested scroll, move a button from y=300 to painted y=150. Neutral bounds correctly report y=150; the exact original native lowering reports y=300 in both cases. A root DPI/zoom transform cannot repair an omitted scroll translation. No OS screen-reader or physical hit testing was executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Lower the already corrected shared projection, preserving platform-specific producer/leaf semantics and action custody. Add scroll-plane coverage at that shared boundary rather than another independent bounds algorithm.

findings.title: Native accessibility still maps and activates a node absent from the published tree
findings.status: verified unchanged native projection and request-mapper functions with real current Host dispatch; no OS action execution
findings.evidence: project_tree_with_actions walks the entire DOM and inserts every node into action_map before considering whether the style-aware accessibility tree contains it. map_parts checks that map, not current publication or supported actions. In a real current Host, a button is changed to display:none and relaid out: the exact native projection omits the node, but retains its action route. The unchanged original map_parts method, using fixture storage for its two actual maps, returns a Click request, and actual Host::apply_a11y_requests activates the hidden button, incrementing state. Thus the documented refusal for a target no longer in the tree is false. This can affect an action queued before hiding and drained against a later sync; the probe does not claim observed OS queue timing.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Build action routes from the current exposed projection and enforce current action eligibility at consumption. Keep textbox/producer pruning consistent; do not treat all retained DOM IDs as current accessibility authority.

findings.title: The same custom leaf receives different accessible names on native and browser hosts
findings.status: verified unchanged native/browser pure lowerings and real current DOM/layout; OS AT and browser DOM application not executed
findings.evidence: Native projection invokes a sprigging leaf accessibility hook on the existing AccessKit node, so the hook can overwrite an author aria-label. Browser lowering treats ordinary leaf semantics as names_itself=false and explicitly gives the author name precedence. The same custom-leaf with aria-label Author name and a leaf hook naming itself Leaf name projects Leaf name natively, while the exact browser mirror planner retains Author name. Producer-owned slot naming is deliberately distinct, so that exception does not account for this ordinary leaf disagreement. The test uses real current layout and unchanged pure adapters; it does not assert an OS/browser announcement.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Choose and publish one ordinary-leaf naming precedence in the shared semantic owner, preserving the separate producer slot policy. Derive both platform outputs from it.

findings.title: GPU producer refusal test checks a local image key that the live registry never stages
findings.status: source-verified blind assertion; ignored GPU test not executed
findings.evidence: The test claims a failed producer has already unregistered its previous staged image because unregister_external_image(external_image_key(KEY)) returns false. KEY is the local registry key 807. Current ProducerRegistry allocates an unrelated process-wide physical key in the upper half of the lower-62-bit domain and stages/retire by that allocated key; image_identity exposes it. For local 807, external_image_key(KEY) is consequently not the staged binding. This assertion returns false for an absent unrelated key even if the actual physical image were still live, so it cannot prove the claimed invalidation. The rest of the test has separate typed failure/authority checks, which are not invalidated by this one blind check.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Capture the actual pre-refusal ProducerImageIdentity::renderer_key, establish that binding exists in a positive control, and assert its retirement. Do not apply external_image_key again to the full returned renderer key.

findings.title: Headed device-reuse negative controls clear the cache while leaving the device authority intact
findings.status: source-verified stale control perturbation; headed tests not rerun
findings.evidence: The one-window control and the multi-window third-window control expect clearing shared.render_core to force a second device boot. Current native render_core first consults shared.render_recovery, reattaches that owner and returns owner.current; the owner is installed on first boot and is not cleared by either control. Resume also polls the same recovery owner. Both purported forget-the-device perturbations therefore leave the actual authority available and no longer exercise the old two-device behavior they claim to detect. The assertions expect a second boot, so this is an obsolete negative control, not a claim that those ignored tests currently pass.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Construct an explicit isolated negative-control ownership graph and verify its distinct device identity. Keep the ordinary shared-recovery path intact; a cached Arc is no longer the device owner.

findings.title: Windows multi-window idle policy can poll continuously for a minimized window it refuses to draw
findings.status: source-verified scheduling predicate mismatch; native minimize/CPU runtime not executed
findings.evidence: The Windows about_to_wait draw loop considers a window showing only when it is not app-hidden and its native window is not minimized. A minimized window therefore skips asked(), leaving its paced wanted flag set. The later owed predicate checks only !hidden and wanted.get(), omitting the minimized check, and selects ControlFlow::Poll when true. A minimized, otherwise nonhidden window with a pending redraw thus continuously requests idle turns while the same code declines to consume its request. The Minimize command changes native state without setting app-hidden, so those are distinct states in the shipping wrapper. This is the exact boolean counterexample, not an observed OS CPU measurement.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Use one eligible-to-draw predicate when drawing and deciding whether to poll, preserving the owed redraw for restoration and the normal monitor-paced path.

findings.title: Saving does not end the undo coalescing run, so another edit can stay falsely clean
findings.status: verified original History API with standard-library-only runtime counterexample; editor save caller source traced
findings.evidence: History::mark_saved records undo.len but leaves last_key/last_time live. Record initial 0 with a field key at t1000, edit to 1, mark_saved, then record 1 under the same key at t1100 and edit to 2: record coalesces without changing depth, is_dirty remains false, and undo(2) returns 0, skipping the saved content 1. Current Scenomise save/load/mark_saved paths call this API without break_run inside those paths. The actual editor UI and persistence were not run. Eight original Backstep tests plus two counterexamples pass.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: A save checkpoint must terminate the coalescing run or use a distinct content/history identity. Keep explicit save and undo semantics together; do not merely repaint the dirty indicator.

findings.title: Lowering an existing History cap does not enforce the advertised bound
findings.status: verified public API counterexample; no live product cap-resize consumer established
findings.evidence: with_cap accepts an already populated History and only changes cap. Starting with five undo entries, applying with_cap(1), then recording another edit leaves five undoable entries because record drops only one before pushing one. Thus the stated cap can remain exceeded indefinitely under ordinary one-entry records. This is an API/resource-bound defect; the current editor construction uses a cap before population and no runtime configuration consumer was proven.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Trim down to the chosen cap and update the saved checkpoint consistently, either at cap change or before record. Preserve the existing zero-cap meaning.

findings.title: Count::combine indexes past every nonempty array and breaks constant sequence metadata
findings.status: verified actual current Meristem runtime and expected E0080 constant consumer over two exact retained suppliers
findings.evidence: The combine loop increments idx before matching vals[idx]. It skips vals[0] and reaches vals[N] for every nonempty input. All four singleton Count variants panic, and Count::One.multiple inherits the panic. A separate consumer evaluating public ViewSequence::ELEMENTS_COUNT at compile time fails E0080 on this original source. The ordinary 37 integration and 9 core unit tests pass because they do not evaluate the affected metadata on these shapes. This is a real metadata implementation defect, not evidence that all normal view construction currently fails.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Evaluate the current index before incrementing and cover empty/single/mixed counts plus a real sequence constant. Do not interpret normal build success as evaluation of lazy associated constants.

findings.title: Vec partial regrowth discards generation tombstones, then revives a stale child route
findings.status: verified actual current generic sequence using its original test element/splice fixture over exact retained suppliers
findings.evidence: VecSeqState documents retaining generations for the longest-ever sequence. The grow branch unconditionally resize(n,0), which can truncate the generations vector when regrowing below its historical maximum. A real core 3->1->2->3 sequence shows the removed index-2 route correctly stale after shrinking, panicking during partial regrowth when message indexes the truncated vector, then matching generation 0 again after full regrowth. The old child-3 message returns Action(30) from the replacement child. Existing stale tests cover 1->0->1 and miss this path. These are core routing results, not native DOM/application activation or OS event timing.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Only extend generation storage beyond its historical maximum; retain removed-slot generations. Also refuse out-of-live-range paths before indexing state, without silently routing a stale payload to a replacement.

findings.title: Leaf replacement keeps a retired Path-B scene and discards the replacement paint
findings.status: verified original current Sprigging registry/cache API over three exact retained suppliers; no live product replacement or GPU execution
findings.evidence: LeafRegistry and RenderedLeaves independently retain state by the same numeric key, without a leaf incarnation. After a SceneSlot is painted, replacing it under the same key with a fresh Swatch repaints but cx.take_scene().or(prior_scene) selects the retired scene, discards the new rect commands, and continues publishing DrawExternalTexture. Removing and reinserting an empty SceneSlot of the same size instead skips paint entirely and retains retired content. Two actual registry/cache counterexamples pass. The carry is intended for a size-only repaint of the same scene leaf, but cannot distinguish a replacement. An in-tree live product replacement causing a physical wrong image was not established.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Qualify retained output by leaf incarnation/paint kind or explicitly invalidate both caches on replacement. Keep same-leaf SceneSlot size carry; changing .or alone would erase that valid behavior.

findings.title: Public graph styling changes current hit geometry without dirtying retained paint
findings.status: verified actual original GraphCanvas and cache APIs; live product style mutation/native hit dispatch not run
findings.evidence: GraphCanvas exposes node_radius and edge_width publicly but paint_dirty only reads its private flag; neither direct field assignment nor LeafRegistry::get_mut_as invalidates it. After the first render, adding 10 to node_radius moves node_local_position(0) by (10,10), yet render_into at unchanged size returns zero and retains byte-for-byte debug-equivalent old commands. Similar public colors and sizes exist on other stock leaves. This makes the advertised common paint/hit projection disagree across retention boundaries. The ordinary Cambium paint_leaf wrapper sets these fields on a newly constructed dirty leaf; that construction path is not shown failing.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Provide invalidating style setters or a revisioned paint-input snapshot. Avoid forcing every unchanged leaf to repaint merely because mutable access was requested.

findings.title: Mesquite wheel selectors bypass the requested surface family
findings.status: source-verified current Mere adapter path plus inspected cached Taproot selector/driver implementation; full Mesquite runtime not compiled
findings.evidence: The wheel grammar retains surface:NAME via Selector::on_surface. Its app_step directly calls self.selector_target, then queues Wheel at Hit.point, without checking Hit.surface against the requested family. That selector_target applies the DOM/projection matcher and unconditionally attributes a match to P::SURFACE. The inspected cached Taproot matchers ignore surface because they match within a supplied DOM; its public resolve/click driving methods enforce matches_surface at the host boundary. The wheel verb bypasses those methods. Given a matching local control and a foreign surface name, the current branch still queues input for the local control. Ordinary shared click is protected by Taproot before click_target, so that path is not accused. No full current supplier build, scenario or OS wheel execution is claimed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Route wheel targeting through the scope-enforcing resolver or explicitly check selector.matches_surface(hit.surface). Keep the honest miss behavior and held-click semantics.

findings.title: Standalone browser smoke keeps its PASS automation title after later errors
findings.status: verified unchanged JavaScript error hooks in Node VM fixture storage; actual browser/GPU error timing not executed
findings.evidence: The HTML says console/window error hooks surface panics and JS failures through the title for external automation. Both hooks refuse to change any title beginning SMOKE, including SMOKE PASS. The Rust smoke sets that title after render submission and queue.present, without a separate completion/error boundary. The exact unchanged JS hooks correctly change a stage title to ERR for an early console error; after SMOKE PASS both console.error and the window error handler leave PASS. Errors still log to console, so this is a misleading title sentinel, not suppression of all diagnostics. The probe does not establish an observed browser/GPU fault.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Let observed failures revoke the automation sentinel and qualify success at the intended completion boundary. A submitted smoke frame does not prove eventual GPU completion or visible pixels.

findings.title: Reopening the workshop library clears the embedding host export protections
findings.status: source-verified full current Workshop/Pelt caller chain; actual export overwrite and full Workshop runtime not executed
findings.evidence: set_protected_export_paths/directories installs transient host storage policy. A successful reopen calls Self::load and replaces the entire current state; from_registry initializes both protection vectors empty and reopen restores neither. Pelt installs its appearance-store path only during EditorWindow::open, then uses shared native hooks, whose synchronization only refreshes font inventory/controls and export effects. Therefore a clean library reopen loses the actual caller guard and the exporter can accept the formerly protected appearance path. An existing file still triggers the ordinary explicit replacement prompt; it is no longer categorically refused as host-owned. The workshop own library/preferences path checks remain active. Current tests cover path aliases/replacement rechecks and reopen persistence separately, missing their composition.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Preserve embedding policy/resource configuration across authored-library reload, or keep it in an owner that reload cannot replace. Add the actual protect/reopen/export composition case; broad state replacement should not erase host authority.

findings.title: Shared workshop bindings replace the graph with a dirty leaf on every frame
findings.status: source-verified actual frame-to-registry-to-paint chain; native/GPU performance not measured
findings.evidence: The native frame hook invokes PreviewBindings::register every frame. Unlike its retained reader and stylesheet producers, register always leaves.insert(GRAPH_LEAF_KEY, Box::new(state.graph_leaf())). That creates a new GraphCanvas whose constructor sets dirty=true, replacing the prior leaf; render_into consequently repaints a visible graph even if state/size are unchanged. Its epoch and dependent retained-fragment work are invalidated on every such pass. The source tests verify shared geometry, colors and retained producer identity, not graph clean-frame reuse. This does not imply the wrapper continuously schedules redraws, nor quantify frame time/GPU cost. It is a concrete defeated cache gate in the maintained shared host binding.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Retain the graph leaf and update it through invalidating setters only when its graph/theme/emphasis inputs change. Coordinate with Q325 public-style dirtiness; blindly mutating those fields would create a different stale-paint defect.

findings.title: The eviction policy cycle skips the promised seven-day rung for smaller custom values
findings.status: verified unchanged cycled method on matching enum fixture; full recall/kernel feature and product UI not executed
findings.evidence: The public method documents that an arbitrary KeepDays(n) advances to the next curated rung above n, with rungs 7,30,90,forever. Its first branch is d<30=>KeepDays(30), so every 0..6 value jumps to 30 instead of 7. The exact unchanged method reproduces this while ordinary rungs and KeepSessions fallback behave as documented. The fixture enum preserves all variants but omits serde derives; this is pure policy-method execution, not an actual persisted host setting or eviction pass. A live non-rung UI consumer was not established.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Add the below-seven branch or correct the advertised arbitrary-value policy. Preserve the user-owned retention policy; this finding does not authorize changing defaults.

findings.title: Remote-context discovery skips nested contexts inside inline context definitions
findings.status: verified exact scanner functions over retained serde_json; full JSON-LD expansion/acquisition pipeline not executed
findings.evidence: referenced_context_urls says it finds string references in any top-level or nested @context. collect_context_urls deliberately skips recursing into an @context value; collect_context_strings handles strings/arrays but ignores objects. Consequently a term definition containing its own @context URL is omitted, both inside a single inline context object and inside a context array. Exact original helpers return [] for the first and only the outer URL for the second. Positive controls retain top-level/@graph references and ignore ordinary IRI fields. A host using this scanner to prepare an offline cache can miss a required context, but no in-tree live acquisition consumer or actual remote/parser failure was established.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Traverse scoped context definitions and supported context import references without treating ordinary term IRIs as fetch requests. Keep network acquisition bounded and host-owned; parser callbacks should continue refusing missing cache entries.

findings.title: Held Surface assertion metadata omits parallel buckets that direct RDF facts include
findings.status: verified current source and kernel multigraph API contracts; full RDF runtime not executed
findings.evidence: node_direct_quads traverses every surface_outgoing_relation_buckets payload. node_metadata_quads instead traverses out_neighbors and resolves each target with find_edge_key, explicitly documented by the kernel to select the first directed edge. With two parallel held Surface buckets, both fact predicates are exported but only the first bucket gets reifiers, statement IDs, attribution, lifecycle and basis metadata. Repeated target neighbors repeat the same first metadata and dataset dedup conceals that repetition. dataset_quad_iter has no later Surface metadata repair; JSON-LD, file serializers and borrowed/materialized SPARQL share it. The existing parallel-bucket test checks fact direction/scopes only. Existing round-trip and query parity checks compare projections through this same owner and cannot detect pre-projection omission. Ordinary Resource statements use the separate per-resource-edge path and are not accused by this finding.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Use the same all-outgoing-buckets traversal for held metadata as direct facts and assert every known parallel handle/provenance against the source graph. This is a bounded local fix; full RDF dependencies are not present in the retained supplier set.

findings.title: Scrying translates every mouse button press and release as a left click
findings.status: verified unchanged current mapping and producer call chain; live system-WebView input not executed
findings.evidence: map_mouse passes only ev.kind to mouse_kind_to_scrying, which unconditionally maps Pressed/Released to LeftButtonDown/LeftButtonUp. The changed button only sets virtual-key flags. Right, Middle, Back and Forward therefore reach the producer with left-button event kinds even though their flag is set. ScryingProducer forwards that mapped event and returns the backend Result. The original test covers Left only; pointer-events input is a different path. The adapter nevertheless labels mouse support Supported. This source finding does not claim a headed right-click replay or reproduce concrete backend behavior.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Map the changed button together with phase, including the backend X-button selector, and exercise non-left pairs through the adapter. Confirm wheel axes separately; do not broaden into a full input redesign.

findings.title: Welding advertises typed page zoom that the public Weld adapter refuses
findings.status: verified current capability projection and inherited trait default; full Welding/CEF feature not executed
findings.evidence: Welding 0.15 map_capabilities unconditionally sets document.page_zoom to Supported. WeldSurface and WeldProducer expose no set_page_zoom forwarding, so the public WebSurface inherits Inker's explicit Unsupported return. WeldingSurface::apply_settings can set legacy zoom, but the typed trait contract explicitly distinguishes that from set_page_zoom and its state/bounds result. This is a false capability claim rather than an Ok result on a refused operation. Scrying's neighboring capability projection already makes this distinction.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Either wire typed zoom and its bounds/result through WeldSurface/WeldProducer/Welding, or narrow the capability until that path exists. This is bounded and should not become an unrelated CEF feature expansion.

findings.title: The public BM25 zero-limit query panics whenever it finds a match
findings.status: reproduced through fresh public Bm25Index over exact retained suppliers
findings.evidence: search allocates/ranks hits and, when hits.len()>limit, partitions at limit-1. A matching query with limit=0 underflows/panics, while the missing-term zero-limit control returns empty and a limit-one positive control succeeds. Both higher-level DocumentIndex and TrailIndex clamp their own limits to one, so they hide the core API bug rather than reproducing this crash in their normal route. No current direct product caller passing zero was established.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Return an empty core result for zero or validate the limit at this public API. Preserve higher-level policy separately.

findings.title: A custom-stemmed trail projection reopens as current with different search results
findings.status: reproduced using fresh TrailIndex persistent rebuild and open on disposable fixtures
findings.evidence: IndexConfig permits a stemming function and persistence together. write always stamps SearchIndexSpec::current, which names the default tokenizer; Projection stores scoring config and raw documents but no custom tokenizer identity. open accepts that sidecar and rebuilds postings with Tokenizer::new. A document titled running under a trim-ing stemmer answers runn before close, but open succeeds and returns no runn hit afterward (running still matches). This contradicts both the source promise that stemmed indices are reminted instead of reopened and the one-build-path claim that reopening cannot rank differently. The Genet segmentation profile is also exported but absent from the sidecar; no cross-version profile test was run.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Refuse persistent custom hooks without a stable profile, or retain an explicit named tokenizer profile and require its resolver on open. Do not silently invent a serialization identity for an arbitrary function pointer.

findings.title: Persistent trail rebuilding recursively removes all contents of an unverified caller path
findings.status: reproduced only with marker-identified disposable fixtures under the approved target; no user data or live store touched
findings.evidence: TrailIndex::write calls remove_dir_all on the complete supplied path before recreating two cache files. It checks neither owned cache markers nor whether unrelated files exist. A disposable unrelated marker disappears after a successful public rebuild; the transient rebuild control preserves the same kind of marker. The private method does describe replacing whatever was there, so the behavior is not undocumented there, but the public cache API and example --index override provide no path-ownership boundary. Pointing the override at another directory can delete its removable contents; no live Fjall deletion or actual source-tree overwrite was executed. Errors after removal can also leave the old cache unavailable, which is source evidence rather than a fault-injection receipt.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Confine replacement to the cache files this implementation owns and stage/replace them, or require an owned directory marker before whole-directory removal. Keep any larger cache transaction redesign documented if it would prolong the audit.

findings.title: BM25 silently wraps the 257th field into field zero
findings.status: reproduced through fresh public Bm25Index; normal three-field adapters are outside the failing shape
findings.evidence: new accepts any weights.len(), while add_document casts every enumerated field index to u8 without admission checks. With 257 fields, the sole alpha token in field index256 is stored/scored under field0, so weight256=1 and all other weights=0 yields no hit. The equivalent single-field control yields one. Length/accounting are indexed through the same truncated field, not only the posting tag. This contradicts the generic weights.len()-fields surface; no in-tree consumer with more than three fields was established.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Use a wide field index internally or refuse unsupported field counts explicitly before adding documents. Do not present silently truncated storage as an arbitrary-field scorer.

findings.title: BERT drops the tokenizer attention mask before attention and sentence pooling
findings.status: verified complete current tokenizer/provider/model/attention source; no real or synthetic BERT numerical run
findings.evidence: BertTokenizer uses BatchLongest right padding and returns real-token/pad attention_mask. forward_sentence_batch consumes input_ids and never passes the mask. BertSelfAttention softmax processes every position and mean_pool averages every position. A short sentence batched with a longer one therefore admits pad embeddings to attention and pooling, despite the sentence-transformers compatibility claim. Both sync and async provider paths share this forward helper. Reference fixtures embed each sentence alone, so they cannot exercise the mixed-length batch case. Shape/finiteness tests do not establish padding invariance.

repair_triage.disposition: document substantial model-boundary repair; active audit remains read-only
repair_triage.reason: Thread one mask through model/encoder/layers/attention and masked pooling, then compare the same sentence alone and in mixed-length batches against a numerical reference. Preserve this as a larger high-effect issue rather than spending an hour rebuilding model/GPU infrastructure during full-source reading.

findings.title: The batched index accelerator loses the CPU index key tie-break
findings.status: verified exact source ordering contracts; Burn/CPU-GPU execution not performed
findings.evidence: VectorIndex::nearest orders equal scores by K and explicitly promises corpus-determined top-k. nearest_over_index and affinity_pairs_over_index collect the HashMap in arbitrary order, while cosine_top_k stable-sorts only scores and maps retained positions back to those arbitrary keys. They do not even require K:Ord. Equal nonzero vectors or zero-score rows can therefore choose different keys/pairs from the CPU route, contrary to drop-in pair equivalence. The source parity fixture intentionally avoids head ties and cannot prove this boundary. No actual GPU mismatch receipt is claimed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Give the keyed accelerator the same stable corpus/key ordering or share a deterministic ranking policy. Preserve the row-position API semantics separately.

findings.title: Batched cosine uses a different near-zero policy from the CPU vector index
findings.status: verified formulas in current source; no Burn tensor execution
findings.evidence: CPU cosine returns zero whenever either vector norm is <=f32::EPSILON. Batched normalization instead divides by norm+1e-12. For finite one-component vectors [1e-8], CPU yields exactly0 while the batched formula normalizes them close to1 and its dot product is close to1. Thus the source claim that degenerate handling matches VectorIndex is false beyond the exact-zero fixture. These are admitted nonzero vectors of valid dimension; ordinary normalized embedding inputs do not establish this edge case.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Share an explicit degenerate-vector threshold and behavior across dense/sparse/Burn paths, with a finite near-zero parity case. Keep the invariant distinct from empirical GPU tolerances.

findings.title: SemanticSearch accepts a prebuilt index with the wrong metric and its reads disagree
findings.status: reproduced on freshly compiled unchanged portable core for both dense and sparse stores
findings.evidence: with_index/with_sparse_index check dimensions only. nearest/search use the supplied index metric; metric() and scores() use the provider metric. A cosine provider paired with a valid two-dimensional Euclidean index is accepted, reports Cosine, ranks [1,1] above [10,0] for query[1,0], while scores() assigns the latter the higher cosine. Dense and sparse fixtures reproduce the same contradiction with valid constructor inputs. Existing matching-dimension tests also happen to match metrics.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Check metric agreement during reconstruction or make the authoritative metric an explicit caller decision applied consistently. Matching dimension alone cannot certify vector-space identity.

findings.title: Vector deserialization bypasses the invariants enforced by public constructors
findings.status: reproduced fresh serde boundary and actual vector APIs; no live Eidetic store/network corruption run
findings.evidence: Derived Deserialize constructs SparseVector and VectorIndex private storage directly. Valid JSON with dimensions2 and sparse entry index7 deserializes successfully, then to_dense panics; from_pairs rejects the same entry. A dense index declared dimension2 with a stored one-element vector deserializes and nearest accepts a two-element query, zip-truncating to a plausible score1, while insert rejects that vector. The typed persistence loaders delegate to load_typed and add no vector invariant check. Content hashes/schema identity alone do not establish sorted/in-range/coalesced entries or per-entry dimension.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Validate or reconstruct admitted vectors/index entries when decoding. Keep generic representation validation explicit; do not treat an intact hash as proof of internal mathematical invariants.

findings.title: The vector rank comparator is not total when accepted scores include NaN
findings.status: fresh exact rank_order comparator cycle plus public NaN insertion; no sort panic or nondeterministic product run claimed
