findings.evidence: insert admits non-finite vector components, and rank_order handles unordered scores by key while retaining score order for finite pairs. Exact comparator tuples a=(key1,score1),b=(key2,NaN),c=(key3,score2) give a<b,b<c,c<a. This violates the claimed total order and the sort/partition comparator requirement. The fixture calls the original crate-private helper and separately proves a NaN vector is accepted publicly. It does not claim a particular standard-library sorting outcome.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Choose and enforce a finite-score admission rule or a genuine total floating-point order, including scores produced by overflow. Use the same rule in accelerators.

findings.title: Affinity can create links with zero requested neighbours and exceed its per-row top-k
findings.status: reproduced fresh portable affinity; matching accelerator recipe identified by source only
findings.evidence: Affinity asks nearest(top_k+1), assumes self is in that result, filters self but never takes top_k afterward. Two equal cosine vectors at keys0/1 with top_k0 still create one link because both queries return key0. With dot-product vectors1,2,3 and top_k1, the lowest-magnitude vector selects two other entries since self is outside the head; the final pair set includes all3pairs. The docs allow the index metric, including dot product, and promise per-entry top-k. Batched affinity repeats the same self-in-head assumption; it was not executed here.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Exclude self and enforce the requested neighbor count after filtering; define zero as empty or refuse it explicitly. Use checked/saturating arithmetic for the extra candidate rather than leaving usize::MAX as a separate panic edge.

findings.title: BERT accepts an activation name but executes GELU regardless of it
findings.status: verified config/load/assembly/math source; no non-GELU checkpoint executed
findings.evidence: BertConfig deserializes hidden_act as an arbitrary String. Artifact and in-memory constructors deserialize it and validate only expected weight dtype/shape. BertIntermediate never reads that field and always applies gelu. A structurally valid checkpoint declaring another activation is neither refused nor executed with its requested math. Supported presets use GELU; their shape tests cannot establish the generic HF-layout loader contract. Public mutable config can also reach panic-based shape checks, which remains a separate admission follow-up.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Validate the supported activation explicitly at config admission, or implement a bounded activation dispatch. Refusal is preferable to silently returning vectors under different math.

findings.title: Accepted tiny positive sampling temperatures turn tied maxima into a fixed last-token choice
findings.status: reproduced exact unchanged sampler on finite tied logits, two top-p settings and128seeds; no model execution
findings.evidence: prepare_generation admits finite positive1e-40. Sampler forms f32 reciprocal infinity and zero-times-infinity NaN for each equal maximum. With logits[3,3], every one of128seeds returns token1, both with no top-p and top-p0.9; temperature0.01 controls choose both tokens. Equal logits should retain equal probability at any positive temperature. The first hypothesis that a unique maximum[2,3] would lose was disproved and is retained in the v1 failure receipt; this finding is only the verified tie bias.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Avoid an overflowing reciprocal, for example divide the centered logit by the positive temperature, and keep a non-finite distribution policy explicit. This is a bounded mathematical fix candidate, not a model/GPU repair.

findings.title: Expected-token rank reports first place for a NaN expected logit
findings.status: reproduced exact helper with finite control and non-finite rows; tally caller verified by complete source
findings.evidence: expected_token_rank counts logits strictly greater than logits[expected_id]. If that expected value is NaN, every comparison is false and rank is1, including an all-NaN row. ranking_tally calls the helper on next_token_logits without a finiteness check and increments passed for every positive cutoff. Both trainer forcing receipts use this same tally, so shared evaluation authority can certify invalid numerical output. Finite input weights are admitted carefully, but that does not validate output arithmetic. No real model overflow, trainer run or published invalid EvalReport was executed here.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Refuse non-finite rows before evaluation and validate expected_id bounds. An invalid model evaluation must not be scored as a successful rank.

findings.title: Streaming detokenization emits an incomplete Unicode replacement then permanently loses the completed text
findings.status: reproduced exact StreamObserver and decode method with real retained tokenizers0.20.4 ByteFallback+Fuse; no model/Burn execution
findings.evidence: Real tokenizer decoding byte tokens C3,A9 gives replacement character for the first token, é after the second and éx after an ASCII third token. StreamObserver immediately emits the replacement because emitted is empty. Every later decode fails starts_with(emitted), and finish also refuses to flush it, returning Ok with text replacement only while token_ids still decode to éx. A stop sequence é is also missed after the prefix mismatch. ASCII and cross-token ASCII stop controls pass. The comment promising that held mid-byte text arrives later is false for this admitted tokenizer. Existing real-tokenizer test compares generate and streaming, which use the same observer, on an ASCII Paris prompt. Checkpointed generation independently replaces final text with full decode at completion, so this receipt does not claim identical final corruption on that path.

repair_triage.disposition: document streaming owner repair and cross-route parity as a high-effect issue
repair_triage.reason: Track stable decoder output before callback delivery, handle incomplete byte sequences explicitly and share stop/stream completion policy with checkpoint generation. Include split Unicode and stop cases; no hour-long model build is needed for this reproduction.

findings.title: Controlled cancellation can return text that its callback never received
findings.status: reproduced public API over two unchanged source modules; actor outcome handling verified by source
findings.evidence: The default generate_streaming_controlled suppresses on_token when cancelled becomes true, returning Break to generate_streaming. The underlying provider correctly includes the current fragment because Break means it was delivered, so controlled returns it as successful text anyway. Cancel on the first fragment yields alpha with zero callback deliveries. Cancel on the second yields alpha beta while callbacks contain only alpha. This violates the trait text-concatenation contract at the portable API boundary. The actor separately chooses Cancelled and discards the Ok result, so this is not evidence that the actor announces Finished after cancellation. SessionProvider also inherits this default rather than forwarding controlled calls into a decoder-specific implementation.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Make the controlled wrapper return the fragments actually forwarded or use explicit cancellation outcome semantics. Preserve ordinary callback Break including its current fragment.

findings.title: Frozen realization routes discard retained per-instance readable detail
findings.status: reproduced through current complete production library public APIs with accesskit enabled; documented, not repaired
findings.evidence: A validated SceneSnapshot supplies distinct detail strings through freeze_snapshot_with_details. Flat rows and HTML preserve the ordinary instance detail, while the AccessKit tree retains its name but drops that detail from labels and descriptions. A folded member still holds its supplied detail in FrozenFold.members, but rows, HTML disclosure/alternate table and AccessKit all omit it while retaining the member name. The separately written output recipes therefore do not deliver the same readable facts.
findings.scope: Three public API cases compile the complete current graphshell-client library over seven hash-bound retained suppliers. Data returned by rows, HTML and UxTree only; no DOM execution, OS screen reader, Tokio pump, renderer, fresh Cargo dependency graph or original library unit suite.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only audit goal
repair_triage.reason: Share readable instance lowering or explicitly define supported fact parity across HTML, rows and AccessKit. Carry visible detail into accessible descriptions and folded disclosure content; cover ordinary and folded details together. Do not infer full platform accessibility acceptance from name-only reachability tests.

findings.title: Encrypted edit splits its promised authoring key snapshot and discards a not-inserted result
findings.status: source-confirmed key snapshot split and ignored insertion outcome; rotation-race execution not yet reproduced
findings.evidence: GroupKeys::current documents one snapshot per authoring turn. EncryptedReplica::edit takes keys before awaiting load, builds and seals against that Arc, then calls self.accept. accept_into takes keys.current again and may park an operation naming an unheld epoch, returning Ok(false). edit applies ? only to the Result, discards the bool, and returns Ok(operation), despite documenting that it signs and stores the edit. A key-handle replacement between the snapshots can therefore choose different sealing and admission owners. Its public edit closure can itself capture and replace a GroupKeys clone, giving a bounded deterministic reproduction seam without a timing race. Existing tests rotate between completed edits.
findings.scope: Complete current encrypted.rs and keys.rs reviewed. The two snapshots, false-return path and ignored bool are directly source-verified. No fresh Commons compilation, callback-rotation fixture, live lane or observed user data loss in this pass.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only full-source audit; retain public API reproduction as next Commons diagnostic
repair_triage.reason: Use the same captured keyring through sealing and local admission, and preserve an explicit inserted/parked/refused outcome. Reproduce by replacing the shared handle inside the edit closure, with an unchanged-handle successful insertion control. Check lifecycle and host rotation policy before broadening the fix across chat and joined lanes.

followup_evidence.detail: Whole Commons source review complete. Public callback key-replacement cases and full-library runner are prepared but not executed: bounded retained-supplier selection could not prove the chosen Gemot/Insigne fingerprint family coherent. No fresh dependency build was substituted.

findings.title: Concurrent Commons parking exceeds its record and byte bounds
findings.status: reproduced unchanged current private Parking module over exact retained suppliers and real MemoryBackend
findings.evidence: Two valid signed operations from different authors both read an empty parking slot list before either writes. Each park call returns true and commits its own unchanged atomic batch. With max_records1, final status is parked2 and evicted0. With max_bytes equal to the larger individual encoded operation, both individually fit but the final byte sum exceeds that bound. Sequential arrivals under max_records1 leave parked1 and evicted1. Slot/occupancy reads are outside the write batch, so atomic apply does not make the read/modify/write decision atomic. The scheduling wrapper changes only the order of list completion and delegates actual MemoryBackend storage/write batches.
findings.scope: Three deterministic private-module cases, CPU and in-memory storage. No whole Commons, live LogSync, joined host, physical carrier, durable disk or observed large-memory pressure. Record encodings legitimately have different lengths; corrected byte fixture uses max(individual lengths) and their actual sum.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only source audit
repair_triage.reason: Serialize occupancy/slot conflict, eviction counter and insertion through one backend-owned transaction across every writer for the same parking prefix. Backend::transact is the existing read-plus-write owner; preserve typed refusal when unavailable. A lock only on one Parking clone would miss independently constructed owners over the same backend. Cover count, bytes and same-slot concurrent outcomes before broadening acceptance claims.

findings.title: Standalone capsule page publishes delayed navigation after grant revocation or completed Stop
findings.status: reproduced unchanged complete page and shared Runtime in Node VM with explicit boundary doubles
findings.evidence: apply checks the current navigate grant before calling openAddress. That host continuation awaits storage, pack verification and body fetch, but its final check only compares an open token. Revoking the grant and completing Stop do not advance that token. A deferred valid body then sets current state, reader text, last_opened and success notice in both cases. Stop actually calls the unchanged shared Runtime.close and terminates the Worker double; the host fetch continuation is already outside its pending-call map.
findings.scope: Fresh Node VM execution of unchanged complete standalone browser.mjs and shared runtime.mjs. DOM, honest Worker replies, absent-only IndexedDB, network and cryptographic verification are explicit doubles. This tests host continuation and publication after grant revocation or completed Stop, not actual Chromium/Wasm, signature authenticity, real IDB, live transport or the separately implemented Graphshell host.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only source audit
repair_triage.reason: Bind host navigation to the applet instance and current grants through the final publication boundary; invalidate outstanding requests on Stop, replacement and revocation. Keep the existing new-open token check. Reuse the maintained Graphshell host lifetime contract rather than making shared worker cancellation stand in for host continuation cancellation. Delayed-body controls should exercise the standalone page too.

findings.title: Current-revision constitution admission makes competing eligible amendments diverge across replicas
findings.status: reproduced four unchanged current production modules over ten exact retained suppliers
findings.evidence: A valid founder genesis configures two distinct electors and threshold one. Each signs a different replacement rule set naming that same genesis revision, using an independent sequence-zero log. Both operations verify. The pure fold over the complete corpus returns the same deterministic law in either iteration order. Two real ConstitutionStore/MemoryBackend replicas instead accept opposite first amendments, reject each other's amendment as StaleRevision before retention, and keep different rules/revisions. Repeated cross-delivery is still refused. This is not a same-signer log fork. Sequential founder amendments and an amendment retried after its initially missing genesis both pass as controls.

findings.evidence: Actual resolve_match returns the same DuckDuckGo URL for SearchQuery values explicitly tagged Bing, Google or DuckDuckGo, because the match discards provider and calls the separate NavTarget::Search hardcoded resolver. findings.scope: Three complete unchanged modules nav/omnibar/suggest compiled together over two exact retained kernel/url suppliers. Their original module tests plus two audit cases exercise pure CPU classification and resolution. This is not the complete Chrome crate/unit suite, a fresh Cargo graph, a browser or live host/provider request. The suggestion helper explicitly produces DuckDuckGo/default-sigil rows today; the cases establish that its public shared match input ignores other provider tags and that custom classification settings cannot reach this suggestion API. The local suggestions producer intentionally emits only DuckDuckGo today. This is the public shared-match resolver accepting and silently overriding another provider tag, not an observed live host changing a configured search engine or sending a query.

repair_triage.disposition: documented under active read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Resolve using the advertised provider or return an explicit unsupported result for values this host cannot handle. Keep the default choice at configuration/construction and share URL generation, rather than encoding a second implicit provider inside resolution.

findings.title: Refused native-drop file exports truncate an existing destination before validating the drop limits
findings.status: reproduced two public plaintext file-export variants over freshly compiled complete current owner
findings.evidence: A real signed operation is inserted through the actual processor/MemoryBackend. Both export_plain_topic_file and export_selected_plain_topic_file open an existing audit-owned sentinel file, then return a configured max_protected_bytes0 limit refusal. Each destination is empty afterward. A successful default-limits control round-trips the signed stored operation with matching semantic drop ID and leaves the source store at one operation.
findings.scope: Complete unchanged current Stickleback library and public consumer freshly compiled over17exact retained fingerprint-matched suppliers. Two CPU/MemoryBackend/file cases use one genuinely signed operation admitted by the actual processor. The two refusal fixtures and successful control are new audit-owned files, never user exports; their final bytes are retained. Protected-export variant is source-reviewed but not executed. No full original suite, fresh Cargo graph, live carriage, RF, real user-file loss or domain authorization bypass. Hashing/compiling all30files does not claim all30have been source-read. File export does not explicitly promise atomic replacement, but this observed failure destroys a prior destination before producing a valid replacement. This is not an ignored error or demonstrated corruption of a user export.

repair_triage.disposition: bounded file-publication repair candidate documented under active read-only audit
repair_triage.reason: Validate before touching the destination where possible, write/flush a new artifact and publish only after successful completion under an explicit replacement policy. Preserve the old destination on refusal or write failure. Coordinate portable replace/durability semantics; do not delete existing evidence to make an export succeed.

findings.title: A failed group-session save followed by same-session retry settles an update that was never persisted
findings.status: reproduced through public lane/session APIs over freshly compiled complete current owner
findings.evidence: Real identities and genuine signed lane operations establish two group members. Applying an update advances the receiver, then an injected persistence callback returns Err. Retrying with that same live session returns success, classifies the update superseded and never calls its new save callback. Reopening the old saved session against the same lane skips the settled update and cannot decrypt the new epoch. Successful-first-save and reload-before-retry controls each save once, survive reopen and decrypt.
findings.scope: Fresh whole unchanged Stickleback owner over17exact retained suppliers; real identities, signed operation processing, MemoryBackend and real group encryption. Three public-API cases: successful first save, failed save followed by same-live-session retry, and failed save followed by reload-before-retry. Secret snapshots stay in memory and are neither printed nor retained. Injected callback refusal, not real disk failure or host-level data loss; no original suite or live network. Compile source hashes do not grant source read credit.

repair_triage.disposition: bounded persistence-ordering repair candidate; active audit remains read-only
repair_triage.reason: A settled marker must not outlive the session transition it certifies. Make failure rollback/reload obligations explicit, or require persistence before settling transitions already applied in memory. The documented same-session retry currently loses this obligation; preserve both restart controls.

findings.title: Separate single and batch retention implementations disagree when pruning also erases a prefix payload
findings.status: reproduced through public processor and native-drop APIs over freshly compiled complete current owner
findings.evidence: A neutral policy explicitly authorizes a sequence2 checkpoint to prune two predecessors and erase the first payload. The single-operation path reports pruned_entries2/erased_payloads1 and leaves one operation pointer, but its log still contains the first signed header without a body plus the checkpoint. Prefix deletion is followed by a Put recreating that old log key. The native-drop batch applies the identical three signed operations under the same effects policy and leaves only the checkpoint, because its overlay retains the preceding deletion decision.
findings.scope: Fresh whole unchanged Stickleback owner over17exact retained suppliers. Real signed three-operation corpus, real OperationProcessor/MemoryBackend, same policy in single-operation and native-drop batch paths. Single-operation prune+erase recreates a removed prefix header without its pointer; batch control leaves only the checkpoint. Neutral policy explicitly authorizes effects; no governance/destruction policy chosen, no actual user data or live network, original tests0. Counts describe exact observed paths, not every retention combination. Compile hashes do not grant read credit.

repair_triage.disposition: bounded duplicate effect-planning repair candidate; no destruction policy chosen
repair_triage.reason: Use a shared effect planner or otherwise make prefix deletion dominate payload stripping in both paths. Verify log keys, operation pointers and reported removal counts together for overlapping effects. This is a mechanics discrepancy under an explicitly supplied policy, not a ruling on what a domain may erase.

findings.title: The independent architecture logit-error subcheck silently discards NaN mismatches
findings.status: reproduced exact comparison expression in a fresh CPU graph; no whole architecture model execution
findings.evidence: The exact iter/zip/absolute-error/f32::max expression reports0for [NaN,2] versus [1,2], and also for an all-NaN actual row. Finite exact-match control gives0and finite mismatch[9,2] gives8and fails tolerance. f32::max ignores a NaN operand, so its 0seed suppresses every non-finite mismatch. Later token-ID assertions are separate and were not claimed to pass for a model producing these rows.
findings.scope: Projected unchanged expression only; full independent reference fixture/model/Burn/GPU unexecuted. Related Q348 covers the separate expected-token rank evaluator; this is a new reference-comparison acceptance check with the same missing output-validity boundary.

repair_triage.disposition: bounded numerical acceptance repair candidate

findings.title: Reloaded staged update authenticity is replaced by a digest stored beside the mutable artifact
findings.status: reproduced unchanged production StagedUpdate load/take_verified methods over real filesystem and BLAKE3
findings.evidence: An intact audit-owned staged payload/record pair reloads and passes. Changing only the artifact is refused. Changing its digest in neighbouring staged.json as well makes take_verified return the substituted unsigned bytes. The record retains no publisher key, signature or signed-manifest commitment. install_staged only invokes this check before passing bytes to install; that native handoff was source reviewed and was not executed.
findings.scope: Requires write access to both stage files. Scoped unchanged methods included before cfg(test) over an audit Update facade whose installer panics and was never called. Initial directory fixture was synthetic rather than a genuine signed download. No remote ingress exploit, privilege escalation, actual installer or user file was exercised. The observed failure directly contradicts the module assurance about another process reaching the staged file across restart.

repair_triage.disposition: document high-effect restart trust migration; broader than a one-hour audit repair
repair_triage.reason: Re-establish publisher authorization using caller-trusted key policy and retained signed evidence at apply time. An editable record cannot be its own trust root. Bind target, version, format and artifact identity together, define old-stage migration and restart durability, and preserve the single-file tamper control. Do not silently choose a new publisher trust policy.

findings.title: Windows MSI update handoff exits successfully even when neither launcher starts
findings.status: source-confirmed Windows failure path; no native installer process execution
findings.evidence: If starting PowerShell fails, WiX/MSI handoff attempts msiexec directly but discards that spawn Result. The branch then unconditionally calls process::exit(0). Thus the caller terminates successfully even when the fallback also failed before starting any installer. A successful launcher spawn also does not prove installer completion; this finding is the narrower both-launches-fail branch.
findings.scope: Full platform source read. No installer, PowerShell replacement, failed real update or process exit experiment ran. NSIS uses a different panic-on-spawn-failure branch and is not claimed to share this exact false0 path.

Reload preserves that mismatch; Forward restores agreement. HistoryEntry retains engine ID/request but no route and traverse_to does not restore route. Existing engine-history positive test checks engine/address but omits route equality.
findings.status: reproduced current public CPU API behavior; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Actual unchanged engine-free Pelt core and contract suppliers. Test-supplied session factories, positive/negative controls and caught panic. No real engine, browser, desktop, hardware input or physical AT execution.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Keep history engine and its route/provenance together, or reconstruct an honest recorded-engine route on successful traversal. Do not reroute history through current policy blindly. Workspace metadata consumes this route for labels/diagnostics. Reproduction is linear-history engine loading with supplied factories; host-history graph navigation is a separate owner and no headed wrong label was measured.

findings.title: Placement Session Cancel is discarded while nonzero pointer gestures retain capture
findings.evidence: Actual pool admits pointer37 and49 in one focused placement. input(placement,SessionInput::Cancel) lowers to pointer0 terminal, is rejected for lack of pointer0 capture, delivers nothing and leaves both nonzero captures. Direct controller Cancel delivers, while input_at(window,Focus(false)) correctly cancels both through existing helpers. Controller explicitly treats Session Cancel as global within its session.
findings.status: reproduced current public CPU API behavior; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Actual unchanged engine-free Pelt core and contract suppliers. Test-supplied session factories, positive/negative controls and caught panic. No real engine, browser, desktop, hardware input or physical AT execution.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Define and consistently implement placement-level Session Cancel scope across pool/content/controller, using retained receiver envelopes for admitted gestures. Keep explicit per-pointer and window-wide cancellation distinct; this audit does not choose an all-window policy. Current direct/window helpers are real mitigations. No physical host trigger or loss of a real user gesture was measured.

findings.title: Single-document viewer reports success after native window or renderer startup failure
findings.evidence: resumed logs create_window and SurfaceHost::boot failures and exits without retaining an error. run_headed_with checks only receipt_failure and then returns Ok(outcome). Exact extracted bodies with deterministic platform doubles return Ok, created_window=false, redraws=0 and no product receipt for both failures even when a named article receipt was requested. Injected semantic-failure control returns Err; successful-startup control has a window. The caller prints successful viewer status on Ok. These startup/caller/outcome bodies are byte-equivalent to origin/main.
findings.status: documented, not repaired; reproduced exact extracted executable bodies
findings.scope: Six source-extracted CPU cases with deterministic OS/event-loop/renderer doubles, not a complete desktop build or observed native startup failure.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Retain a startup/application error and return it before the outcome, matching the existing platform-smoke error precedence. A requested product receipt also needs a final completion check. Treat intentional headless no-window behavior separately.

findings.title: Basic NetRender smoke returns Ok for blank and wrong-color readback
findings.evidence: The smoke submits a full red scene but only counts any nonzero RGBA pixel and always returns Ok. The actual complete function body with a deterministic readback double returns Ok painted_pixels=0 for all-zero pixels and Ok painted_pixels=4096 for all-white pixels. The CLI logs either outcome and does not reject zero or assert red. The nearby WebGL smoke already rejects wrong expected sample colors; receipt_capture also refuses blank capture. The smoke source is unchanged at origin/main.
findings.status: documented, not repaired; reproduced exact extracted executable bodies
findings.scope: CPU function-body/readback-double proof. No claim that a real current renderer produced blank or white, and no GPU or display run.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Require nonblank output and meaningful expected red-pixel/region assertions before returning success; keep readback/presentation/backend qualification separate.

findings.title: Windows presentation smoke redraws the configured extent after a native resize
findings.evidence: The Resized handler ignores the new size and requests redraw; every subsequent Scene is constructed from config.width/config.height. The adjacent comment claims current backing-pixel resolution. macOS and Wayland smoke paths actually read window.inner_size on every redraw. The Windows outcome likewise reports configured dimensions. Source is unchanged at origin/main.
findings.status: documented, not repaired; source-confirmed
findings.scope: Source-confirmed extent selection disagreement. No native window resize, GPU swapchain consequence or visual symptom was exercised.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Read current physical client size for rendering and report achieved dimensions, with an explicit zero-size/minimized policy. Retain fixed-size smoke semantics only if the API and comments name them honestly.

findings.title: Concurrent Pelt receipt drivers share success and can skip one requested proof
findings.evidence: Configuration rejects named-plus-legacy and acceptance-plus-cancellation, but admits interaction+capability and interaction+tearout. In the actual render guard prefix, a ready capability proof sets receipt_complete before the interaction branch, so interaction never runs. An interaction completion likewise skips the later requested tearout. The output flags all enabled legacy drivers using that same bool, and tearout finalization trusts it. Source-extracted tests execute the unchanged admission/guard bodies with deterministic driver doubles: both mixed shapes admit and skip the second proof; pending-capability and refused-combination controls behave distinctly. Guard and validation bodies remain unchanged at origin/main.
findings.status: documented, not repaired; reproduced exact source-extracted executable bodies
findings.scope: Four source-extracted CPU cases with deterministic receipt-driver/event-loop doubles, not actual native capability/interaction/tearout execution.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Reject every unsupported multi-driver combination before windowing, or give each admitted driver its own completion and finalization state. Do not infer one proof from a shared aggregate bool.

findings.title: Both Pelt child-tree lowerings discard the supplied accessibility description
findings.evidence: The current neutral DocumentA11yNode carries description separately from name/value. Both append_document_child and the copied primary-window loop copy name and value but never description. Exact complete helper/primary-lowering bodies over real current Inker neutral nodes and AccessKit0.24.1 drop a supplied supplemental description while preserving label, role, value and SetValue support. A direct AccessKit description control retains the text. The helper claims sharing across primary and tearouts, but primary has an independent copy. This file is unchanged at origin/main.
findings.status: documented, not repaired; reproduced exact source-extracted executable bodies
findings.scope: Three source-extracted CPU cases with actual neutral and AccessKit types and deterministic shell/namespace fixtures. No full desktop compilation, original desktop suite, real DOM or physical AT run.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Carry neutral description into the AccessKit node through one lowering implementation used by primary and secondary trees, with both consumers covered. This is lost supplemental text, not a missing control name or a claim of physical screen-reader acceptance.

findings.title: Primary host chrome drags survive window focus loss outside the pool cancellation boundary
findings.evidence: Primary Focused(false) updates accessibility and forwards Focus(false) to the workspace, but leaves WorkspaceApp.gesture unchanged. Divider and tab drags live only in that host field; pointer_move processes them before content input. If the terminal mouse release is not delivered while focus is away, a later cursor move continues divider mutation or marks the old tab drag moved, and pointer_up can commit its old drop. The only gesture take is pointer_up_inner; there is no focus-loss retirement. Core pool focus cancellation already clears admitted document captures, which does not retire this separate chrome gesture. The focus handler is unchanged at origin/main.
findings.status: documented, not repaired; source-confirmed
findings.scope: Source-confirmed state-machine gap under a missing terminal-release condition. No OS focus/mouse sequence, physical drag or observed layout/drop symptom was reproduced.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Retire host-owned Divider/Tab/Content gesture state on focus loss alongside the existing core focus notification; keep receiver cancellation in the core. Cover focus-loss/missing-release/return-move rather than assuming a document capture test exercises chrome lifetime.

findings.title: Workspace semantic success disables capture recovery and its deadline before a receipt exists
findings.evidence: A named semantic assertion sets receipt_complete before capture acquisition. If host.acquire then returns None, both workspace timeout branches ignore completed semantics and the recovery-redraw branch requires !receipt_complete. After at least one prior presentation, the separate startup predicate also refuses to schedule a retry. Exact complete timeout method, failed-acquire statement and startup predicate reproduce no deadline, no error and no requested redraw for semantically complete Appearance and Mixed fixtures. Pending-semantics controls get either retry or expired error; first-presentation retry control also works. All failure bodies remain unchanged at freshly fetched origin/main.
findings.status: reproduced exact source-extracted CPU recovery behavior; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Five source-extracted CPU cases with deterministic unavailable-acquire, native-statistics, event-loop and tearout-timeout doubles. No whole desktop/original-suite build, observed native hang, real GPU failure or physical input/AT run. A later external event can wake the window; the defect is that the bounded receipt no longer owns recovery or a deadline.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Separate semantic completion from captured/presented artifact completion. Retain a receipt deadline and recovery wake until the named outcome exists or a typed terminal error is returned; do not change the legitimate first-presentation-only startup predicate into a global poll loop.

findings.title: Early Pelt smoke dispatch silently bypasses another requested receipt and its validation
findings.evidence: All arguments are collected before smoke dispatch, but successful smoke handlers return before workspace required-artifact/feature validation or named receipt execution. With an available successful smoke runner, article+artifact+netrender or appearance+artifact+netrender completes only the smoke; mixed+netrender can bypass even the missing artifact/Smolweb requirements. Two requested smoke modes run only the first. Nine child-process probes execute the exact parser/early-dispatch prefix and helpers with deterministic capability/smoke doubles: these cases exit0 without the PNG or owner dispatch, while the earlier product-artifact validation correctly exits2 and the no-smoke control reaches later dispatch. Source is unchanged at origin/main.
findings.status: reproduced exact source-extracted CLI behavior; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Source-extracted CLI prefix executed in real child processes with host/engine-capability/smoke doubles. No actual desktop binary, smoke/GPU, named fixture execution or real application artifact was produced.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Reject incompatible requested run modes before invoking any handler, or explicitly aggregate each requested outcome. Keep a successful selected smoke distinct from completing a named artifact receipt. This finding is conditional on the selected smoke being available and succeeding; a missing-feature/error smoke still exits nonzero.

findings.title: Workspace JS selection silently maps invalid backend values to Boa
findings.evidence: The CLI retains --js as a string. The single-document scripted path calls ScriptedEngine::parse and rejects invalid values; that actual supplier parser is case-insensitive. The workspace branch compares only js_engine == nova and selects the Boa registry ID for everything else. The exact branch probe returns genet.scripted for misspelled-backend, matching boa, while nova control returns genet.scripted.nova. Source also shows valid case variants such as Nova take the Boa branch despite being accepted as Vano/Nova by the single-document parser; this case variant was source-traced, not separately executed. Registered engine construction binds those IDs to Boa and the Vano compatibility backend. The CLI file is unchanged upstream.
findings.status: reproduced exact source-extracted CLI behavior; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Three source-extracted branch-selection child processes, with verified engine-ID constants and declared feature cfgs; no Boa/Vano runtime or complete scripted workspace was built or executed. The remaining six probes cover Q415 dispatch controls.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Parse the backend once through the existing declared parser and use that typed choice plus the same feature-availability check in both host paths. Reject an unknown requested backend rather than selecting an apparently successful fallback.

findings.title: First-owner counter reservations can successfully reuse a spent counter under concurrent calls
findings.evidence: reserve_next_counter reads last_used, computes next, then writes/syncs/renames a fixed sibling temporary file without serializing callers. Its never-reoffered claim and test cover only sequential calls. An unchanged-body probe schedules two actual filesystem reads of last_used=0, lets A write/sync/rename and return1, then lets B continue with its already-read snapshot. B also writes/syncs/renames and returns1; disk remains1. Both successful callers can offer the same controller counter. Shared temporary-file collision is not needed for this failure.
findings.status: reproduced exact source-extracted host behavior; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: One extracted-body concurrency test with real filesystem/serde/sync/rename. A filesystem wrapper delays only return from actual reads to select a valid interleaving; it does not replace disk results or edit the reservation body. No board, radio, actual CLI process race or power-cut durability test.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Serialize the read/advance/durable commit across processes for each controller scope, or use an existing atomic reservation owner. Keep the lock over the complete operation, not only rename. Test concurrent reservation and interruption separately. Existing malformed-record and overflow checks remain real controls; board replay refusal prevents duplicate execution but cannot make both controller requests succeed.

findings.title: Host-side station stop and successful revoke cannot promptly interrupt an in-flight event wait
findings.evidence: next_event owns the station Tokio mutex while awaiting the radio under the previously accepted grant window. stop closes the lease and aborts the watchdog, then waits for that same mutex; revoke likewise closes after successful authority revocation and waits. Neither signals the pending operation. Exact next_event/stop/revoke bodies with an hour-long accepted window and pending fake radio show both stop and successful revoke exceeding a10ms virtual timeout while the lease is already closed and the event task still owns the station. Cancelling that event task lets stop finish. Idle-stop control completes. The comment that host stop is immediate is therefore stronger than this cancellation implementation.
findings.status: reproduced exact source-extracted host behavior; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Two exact-method CPU cancellation cases and one idle-stop control, with actual Tokio mutex/time/timeout and paused virtual time. Radio, lease/authority success, clock and watchdog are deterministic doubles. No actual Postilion station, Djinn revoke, serial task or physical RF cessation was executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Give the station runtime one cancellation owner that wakes in-flight operations when the local lease closes, then drops the radio without waiting for the old grant window. Cover sends, event waits and queueing, plus revocation errors, under the same boundary. This is a host-lifetime fix; remote delivery and board receipt remain separate.

findings.title: Cross-repo smoke falsely certifies registry and non-HTTPS Git dependencies as local
findings.evidence: Assert-Local promises that the edited sibling resolves to a local path. Its only remote-source test is a rendered first Cargo tree line containing (https://. A registry package line and an ssh:// Git line pass and print local. Four executions of the exact AST-extracted PowerShell function with Cargo tree doubles reproduce those false positives and retain controls for HTTPS refusal and local-path acceptance. No comparison to the requested sibling path exists.
findings.status: reproduced source-owner classifier/export behavior or confirmed missing helper; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Four exact-function PowerShell cases with deterministic Cargo output and an existing harmless working directory. No actual cargo graph/build or remote repository mutation.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Inspect Cargo metadata source and resolved manifest_path, require source=null and the expected local checkout owner. Do not use display formatting or absence of one scheme as a source authority. Modern immutable Git consumption may be intentional; update lane policy before requiring local patches everywhere.

findings.title: Firefox metadata matching drops valid unclaimed visits outside its four-position search window
findings.evidence: visit_view_times promises nearest unclaimed same-place visit within tolerance, but examines only pivot-2 through pivot+1. With visits1000..1004ms and five metadata rows at1002ms, tolerance10ms, it matches four and drops the fifth while visit5 at1004ms remains unclaimed and within tolerance. The production function runs unchanged against in-memory SQLite. Two ordinary matches and an out-of-tolerance refusal control also pass. Existing original export test exercises parent identity and microseconds, not metadata matching.
findings.status: reproduced source-owner classifier/export behavior or confirmed missing helper; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Three direct current-function calls with synthetic in-memory SQLite only. No browser profile, actual Firefox history schema/version compatibility or Rust ingestion run.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Search outward through the tolerance interval for an unclaimed candidate, preserving an explicit deterministic tie rule. Avoid rebuilding every timestamp array for each metadata row. This fixes the stated one-to-one heuristic; it does not turn heuristic matching into exact Firefox visit provenance.

findings.title: Wayland and X11 receipt wrappers call an absent helper after host extraction
findings.evidence: Both wrappers resolve remote-receipt.ps1 beside themselves under Mere/scripts, where it does not exist. That helper is present in the sibling Genet checkout. Both also default the remote repository and Repo identity to Genet while naming Cambium host/example/scenario paths now in Mere. Current Genet manifest explicitly records Pelt/Tabard/Cambium extraction; Mere manifest owns the host. These wrappers cannot launch their named checked-in helper as written. No actual SSH or native run was attempted.
findings.status: reproduced source-owner classifier/export behavior or confirmed missing helper; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Complete wrapper source read plus read-only current filesystem/helper membership and targeted current Mere/Genet manifest evidence. This is a missing-path/source-owner finding, not an executed platform failure.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Choose one maintained runner owner and explicit source repository, then bind wrapper/helper/package/scenario/commit/executable provenance consistently. Avoid copying another runner implementation as an extraction workaround. Add a read-only dependency/preflight check before remote process setup.

findings.title: Dramatis package qualifier accepts a successful process that executes zero named tamper tests
findings.evidence: The signed-feed command selects --ignored --exact real_signed_package_and_tamper_controls, but run checks only process exit0. It never requires the named test or one passing test in the log. Exact AST-extracted run evaluated with a subprocess double emitting running0tests/0passed/1filteredout returns normally and records exit0; a nonzero-exit control raises. The full main later declares signed manifest/artifact/publisher/staging tamper gates in its receipt. A renamed/filtered/missing ignored test can therefore remove those checks while preserving the process success path.
findings.status: reproduced exact AST-extracted qualifier behavior with explicit doubles; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: One exact Python helper case plus a refusal control with deterministic subprocess/log double. No actual zero-test Cargo invocation, installer, signer, complete package pipeline or generated published receipt was run. This is the demonstrated qualifier admission weakness, not a claim current retained packages executed zero tests.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Require the exact intended test to execute and pass, ideally through structured test result or an explicit named receipt. Bind that result to the compiled binary/source instead of treating cargo exit as tamper-test completion. Keep package signing/extraction success separate from test coverage.

additional_verification.detail: Unchanged resident stages wrapper accepts a real rustc --exact run with zero named tests: exit0 and native.host.json exit_code0. Explicit nvidia-smi stub, no GPU/model execution. Same exit-status-only evidence defect recurs in this wrapper; no change to original Dramatis receipt scope.

findings.title: Dramatis consent negative control can overwrite a concurrent production edit while restoring source
findings.evidence: consent_control reads production keeper/review.rs, writes an environment-gated denial bypass into the same primary source path, executes builds/tests, then unconditionally writes the saved bytes in finally. It does not require a clean isolated checkout or compare current bytes with the mutant before restore. Exact AST-extracted function with an entirely in-memory source double injects a concurrent owner edit during the negative-test call; finally overwrites it, and the byte-exact restoration assertion still passes. The no-concurrent-edit control restores as intended. Shared target builds can also retain mutant artifacts until explicit restored builds succeed.
findings.status: reproduced exact AST-extracted qualifier behavior with explicit doubles; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Two exact-function cases with in-memory source and build/test doubles only. No actual product source, binary, custody bypass, native dialog, real vault or concurrent user work changed. The risk is directly present in the full driver source; the driver itself was not executed.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Run this mutation control in an isolated permitted checkout only when needed for a real source collision, or supply a test-local substitution that never rewrites shipping source. If restoring a mutable file, compare ownership/current bytes before overwriting and preserve conflicting edits. A restored source hash alone cannot prove concurrent work was preserved or every shared binary was rebuilt.

findings.title: Retained pointwise convolution flattening ignores gaps between batches
findings.evidence: The actual is_spatial_contiguous predicate accepts shape[2,1,2,1], strides[4,2,1,1]. Enumerating the original view yields offsets[0,1,4,5]; the reshape_input flattening metadata yields[0,1,2,3]. The predicate checks channel/spatial contiguity without verifying batch stride, yet the reshape merges batch and spatial axes. Forward pointwise, data-gradient and weight-gradient paths use it. True contiguous and spatial/channel gap controls distinguish the missing batch condition.
findings.status: reproduced retained-source CPU arithmetic/control flow; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Four CPU tests use the unchanged layout predicate and independently enumerated source/flattened addresses. No device-aligned real slice construction, convolution values, CubeCL lowering or GPU execution. The tiny view is an arithmetic counterexample; actual slice code can materialize unaligned byte offsets. Root selects registry burn-cubecl0.22.0, not this retained0.22.0-pre.4 copy.

repair_triage.disposition: documented retired-copy reactivation hazard in read-only audit
repair_triage.reason: Require the merged batch axis to be contiguous too, or materialize the view through the shared layout/reshape authority. Add aligned sliced-batch tensor tests before any reactivation.

findings.title: Retained direct transpose-convolution range excludes a valid unit-kernel origin
findings.evidence: The exact stride/dilation/padding integer range block yields empty rows(0,0) and columns(0,0) for a1x1 kernel, stride3, dilation1, padding0, output origin0 and2x2 input. Input(0,0)*weight(0,0) should contribute at output(0,0). The kernel-size*dilation-stride term produces the wrong lower bound for this valid shape. Unit-stride unit/three-kernel controls include the origin.
findings.status: reproduced retained-source CPU arithmetic/control flow; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Three CPU cases compile the exact extracted2D range block with scalar args/input/clamp doubles. No shader compilation or convolution value run.3D source has related arithmetic but different unsigned operations; this executed result is not generalized to3D. Retained/root-unselected copy only.

repair_triage.disposition: documented retired-copy reactivation hazard in read-only audit
repair_triage.reason: Derive inverse bounds from the transposed-convolution equation and use a shared tested bounds helper rather than separately maintained2D/3D arithmetic. Check dilation, padding, stride wider than kernel and boundaries before reactivation.

findings.title: Retained zero-inner-dimension matmul returns nonempty output without zeroing
findings.evidence: matmul_autotune treats any zero input dimension as proof output is zero-sized. For[2,0]@[0,3], output has six elements and each empty dot product is0. The exact initialization/early-return prefix returns a supplied six-element17-filled output unchanged without dispatch. With out=None, the prefix returns its allocator output without initialization; source init_matmul_output calls empty_device_dtype, which calls client.empty_tensor rather than fill. M0/N0 controls truly have empty outputs; nonzero operands reach the dispatch marker.
findings.status: reproduced retained-source CPU arithmetic/control flow; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Five CPU tests compile the exact early-return prefix with metadata/tensor/allocator doubles. Supplied-output behavior is concrete; allocator sentinel shows absent initialization in this prefix, not observed uninitialized device memory. No backend/GPU execution or registry-backend failure. Retained/root-unselected copy only.

repair_triage.disposition: documented retired-copy reactivation hazard in read-only audit
repair_triage.reason: Distinguish empty output dimensions from empty reduction K. Explicitly zero the nonempty output for K0, including supplied output, through the normal fill authority. Keep shape validation and empty identities shared between tuning and non-tuning paths.

findings.title: Selected Burn remote server-survival test accepts failed read/value assertions as success
findings.evidence: The test opens a new remote client after abrupt disconnect, then expects a tensor read and asserts values[30,60] inside finishes_within. That helper catches and discards any panic and sends completion unconditionally; the outer assertion checks only completion. Exact unchanged helper returns true for a synthetic wrong-result assertion panic, just as for an empty successful body. A blocked-body control returns false and is then explicitly released. A connection/read/value failure can therefore leave this server-survival test green.
findings.status: reproduced unchanged selected-patch helper/registry behavior with explicit IR/process-state doubles; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Three CPU helper cases execute the unchanged std-thread helper. No remote server, disconnection, real failed tensor result or full Cargo integration test executed. This proves test admission weakness, not that the current server actually fails after disconnect.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Keep panic-tolerant completion only for tests whose exact contract is failure surfacing without a hang. For server-survival/correctness, return the worker Result or panic payload and propagate it after the timeout; retain timeout refusal separately. Lease-close no-hang tests intentionally accept error/panic and need different helpers or explicit outcomes.

findings.title: Selected Burn remote shares process-local transfer counters across unrelated server sessions
findings.evidence: Each independently linked client process starts its static LocalTransferId counter at0. One SessionManager shares a LocalCommService across all its sessions, keyed only by LocalTransferId. expose unconditionally inserts and overwrites an existing id; take removes by that id without source/client/target session validation. Two module-local copies of the unchanged counter simulate independent process state and both issue0. Full unchanged LocalCommService on actual Tokio receives payload111 from source session100, then222 from source200 under0; take for the first id returns222 and empties the map. Distinct-id and source-purge controls preserve the correct payloads. Worker wire handlers pass the id directly with no namespace translation.
findings.status: reproduced unchanged selected-patch helper/registry behavior with explicit IR/process-state doubles; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Three CPU rendezvous cases compile full unchanged LocalCommService and exact counter functions against existing actual Tokio. Tensor payload is an i32 backend double, SessionId a u64 double, and two module-local statics model separate processes. No real multi-process/server/transport/credential/GPU tensor run. The demonstrated overwrite/wrong payload can cause a second target to wait with no entry; an actual close/reclaim hang and cross-credential deployment disclosure are source-level effects to qualify separately.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Give same-host transfer identity a shared scope agreed by source and target sessions, or use a server-issued/random capability bound to the intended participants. Reject duplicate exposure rather than replacing a live payload. Validate the taker and make missing/cancelled source terminal so a target cannot indefinitely prevent owner reclaim. This changes a cross-session/wire ownership contract; document before choosing the protocol migration.

findings.title: Selected runtime allocation window ignores a pinned client stream and skips reset on unwind
findings.evidence: Most client operations resolve self.stream_id(), which honors set_stream. allocation_window instead takes StreamId::current() and submits the mode transition there. The exact function with immediate device/server/stream doubles changes stream1 while a client pinned to2 continues observing Auto for its allocation stream. The ordinary unpinned control routes Persistent and resets Auto. If the caller callback unwinds, the exact function never submits its closing Auto transition; the double retains Dedicated and records only one transition. The public safe wrappers promise to bracket the task in a mode and then restore it.
findings.status: reproduced unchanged selected-runtime control flow with exact source and stated doubles; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Three CPU cases compile the unchanged allocation_window function with explicit immediate Device/Server and StreamId doubles. They establish routing and missing reset commands, not an actual GPU allocation, leak, FIFO runner execution or backend nested-mode semantics.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Resolve the same client stream as allocation calls and use a scope guard to balance the transition on unwind. Define nested/previous-mode restoration explicitly rather than silently promising it while always posting Auto. Keep backend state lifetime on its actor; no production change in this audit.

findings.title: Selected runtime RealRun guard can move across threads and corrupt both threads dry-run state
findings.evidence: RealRun contains only unit state and is implicitly Send; new increments the creating thread TLS depth and Drop decrements the dropping thread with saturating_sub. Full unchanged dry_run source compiled with std atomics allows std::thread::spawn to move it. After foreign drop the origin still has depth1 and executes during an active DryRun. A second case gives the destination its own live RealRun, then drops the foreign guard there: destination depth becomes0 and skips launches despite its own guard still alive. Four original nesting/default/dry-run control tests pass.
findings.status: reproduced unchanged selected-runtime control flow with exact source and stated doubles; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Two additional real std-thread cases plus four unchanged dry_run tests. Only serial_test test attributes were removed; the test runner serializes execution. No fake TLS, CubeCL lowering, autotune/backend/GPU run or actual shipped cache contamination. Probe manually balances leaked test state afterward to isolate cases.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Make a TLS-owning guard unable to cross thread boundaries and ensure all tuners/exclusive callbacks construct it on the launch-issuing thread. Add compile-fail or trait assertions for transferability and retain original nesting tests. Do not constrain the global DryRun guard for this TLS-specific issue.

findings.title: Launch observations dropped in documented taken order lose an active observer then resurrect an ended observer
findings.evidence: Documentation says guards dropped in the order they were taken leave the process as found. The exact replacement/restore implementation actually needs strict reverse order. Install A then B, drop A first: its previous=None clears B while B scope is active, so B receives no launch. Drop B next: its saved A is restored even though A scope ended; after both guards have dropped, A receives another launch and is_observing remains true. The reverse-order control restores A while alive and clears it when finished.
findings.status: reproduced unchanged selected-runtime control flow with exact source and stated doubles; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Two CPU cases compile unchanged guard/new/drop/is_observing/notify_launch code with a minimal observer trait and std RwLock adapter. No actual kernel/profile, concurrent install race, logging backend or GPU was run. Sequential documented-order failure and reverse-order control are the executed claims; the adapter does not prove every cubecl_environment lock behavior.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Either explicitly enforce strict nesting and correct the contract, or track live observation registrations so independently overlapping lifetimes cannot restore ended observers. A process-wide observer needs a deliberate overlap owner. Atomically couple the observing fast flag to slot changes under the same ownership decision. Keep source-only concurrent flag/callback timing concerns separate from this sequential witness.

findings.title: Shared roofline helpers admit invalid peaks despite their documented refusal policy
findings.evidence: time_at_peak documents None for negative rate, but checks only is_normal. A negative normal peak(-4) with amount8 reaches Duration::from_secs_f64(-2) and panics. A tiny positive normal finite peak1e-100 also panics because the derived duration is unrepresentable. The scoring path has a different validity rule: score_resources produces fraction-2 for a negative peak and0 for an infinite peak; binding_achieved only checks fraction.is_finite and selects both, though its docs say those peaks are skipped. Zero-peak scoring control is refused. Eight unchanged original roofline tests pass but include neither negative nor duration-overflow rate cases.
findings.status: reproduced selected-runtime numeric/encoding behavior with exact source and stated doubles; documented, not repaired

Demonstrates public numeric helper panic/invalid binding admission, not ordinary measured hardware producing a negative rate.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Centralize validity and representable-duration conversion for resource bounds; reject nonpositive/nonfinite peaks and handle an unrepresentable duration without panic. Make scoring expose invalid model entries consistently so binding selection cannot name them. Keep over-100-percent valid scores visible as documented. AutotuneBound already rejects negative thresholds, but delegates the peak check to this flawed shared helper.

findings.title: Throughput ranking narrows iteration count before normalizing duration
findings.evidence: rank accepts usize iteration counts and min_iterations, then divides fastest Duration by iterations as u32. On a64-bit host a floor of2^32 with a20ms sample reaches a zero divisor and panics. Separately retarget can grow a1000-iteration1ns observation to20,000,000,000 iterations, beyond warmup ceilings; a deterministic20s sample then normalizes through wrapped2,820,130,816 and reports7ns rather than1ns per iteration. Ordinary1000ns/iteration and zero-minimum controls behave as intended.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Keep iteration normalization in a representation that can name the requested count and bound retargeting consistently with the probe/callback contract. Reject or safely normalize counts outside a backend-supported loop range; do not truncate silently. Preserve the minimum-pass constraint while preventing division by zero or reporting a different per-iteration duration.

findings.title: Autotune candidate-list checksum loses name boundaries and candidate count
findings.evidence: compute_checksum concatenates candidate names into one String before StableHasher. Exact unchanged accumulation prefix gives the identical preimage abc for[ab,c] and[a,bc], as well as for the one-candidate list[abc]. Both names and list arity can change without changing its claimed invalidation key. Distinct concatenation control differs. Equal input necessarily gives the same deterministic hasher output; this is an encoding collision before hashing, not a probabilistic hash collision.
findings.status: reproduced selected-runtime numeric/encoding behavior with exact source and stated doubles; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Three CPU cases compile exact accumulation prefix with minimal name-bearing candidate/set structs and inspect the String preimage. Remaining TuneCache/Tuner code is explicitly unread at this checkpoint.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Hash the structured ordered name sequence, including boundaries/count, rather than its concatenation. Require names/identities to cover configurable candidate semantics. Trace cache-load/index admission before deciding migration/version invalidation; a source checksum by itself cannot establish a winner still names the same operation.

findings.title: Autotune calls a pre-execution refusal an executed fallback and settles its index
findings.evidence: Client::exclusive explicitly says its error means nothing ran. run_batch maps that error to Unknown for every candidate. run_plan treats Unknown as executed-but-unmeasured and, after all batches fail, picks the first such index. process_request inserts that decision into in-memory cache as Match and returns Hit; settled then exposes it as a settled winner before any real candidate execution. The exact-body probe refuses exclusive acquisition, proves drive was entered zero times, and observes Hit/settled index0. All-NotMeasured instead panics; a measured-score control selects its actual result index. LocalTuner then attempts the selected operation and expects success, but that execution occurs after cache insertion and does not provide evidence for the earlier executed claim.
findings.status: reproduced scoped CPU behavior with exact source and stated doubles; documented, not repaired
findings.scope: Three CPU cases compile exact run_batch/run_plan/process_request and full tune_cache.rs under non-persistence cfg, using an explicitly refusing client and shape-equivalent surrounding types. No real contention, kernel, GPU, browser, persistent Store or full runtime build. Source confirms disk insertion is suppressed for unmeasured decisions; no disk defect asserted.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit
repair_triage.reason: Keep exclusive-admission failure separate from executed-but-untimed output. If an unmeasured fallback is necessary, preserve its evidence state and admit/retry candidates explicitly instead of describing a never-run index as settled fastest. Keep the existing prohibition on persisting unmeasured guesses. Converge adaptive and fixed all-failed behavior under explicit failure categories rather than broad Unknown.

findings.title: Retained Vulkan backend reads 16-bit features to advertise 8-bit storage

Exact predicates report eight-bit storage true for sixteen-only capabilities and false for eight-only capabilities; both-present/both-absent controls behave normally.

findings.title: Retained WGSL helper discovery skips switch cases and default bodies
findings.evidence: Compiler lowers Switch scopes recursively and Instruction display emits their helper calls, but register_extensions descends only through If/IfElse/Loop/RangeLoop and ignores Switch. findings.title: Retained WGSL f64 NaN and Infinity helpers swap exponent and absolute-value masks
findings.evidence: The f64 tuple gives inf_bits=0x7fffffffffffffff and abs_mask=0x7ff0000000000000. Generated helpers therefore compare exponent-only bits against an all-non-sign-bits threshold. Exact selector and emitted text confirm f64::INFINITY and f64::NAN both classify as neither infinity nor NaN; the f32 control classifies both correctly. The mask also discards the fraction that distinguishes NaN from infinity.

findings.title: Retained Vec4 indexed assignment emits no WGSL statement terminator

The outer Instruction::IndexAssign arm returns the helper directly, adding no terminator.

findings.title: Retained write-only flush reports success without submitting queued writes
findings.evidence: write_to_buffer increments pending_write_count, not tasks_count. flush returns flush_errors immediately when tasks_count==0, regardless of pending writes. Thus its source path has no admission of queued write-only work before declaring submitted work done.

findings.title: Matmul benchmark column layouts can exceed allocation or alias logical elements
findings.evidence: Benchmark prepare generates the requested logical row-major shape then swaps only its last two strides for column layout. A2x3 allocation has strides[3,1], changed to[1,3] while keeping shape2x3; its maximum addressed extent becomes8 elements from a6-element allocation. A3x2 view produces aliasing between[2,0] and[0,1]. Both lhs/rhs arms are affected; square/row controls pass. The benchmark catalogue contains rectangular shapes with all four layout combinations. Correctness seeding uses shared builder.layout instead, so successful correctness is evidence for a different physical layout than this timed preparation.

findings.title: Matmul CPU reference indexes every operand using output rank and panics on valid rank broadcast
findings.evidence: matmul_cpu_reference allocates lhs_index/rhs_index at output rank and fills batch axes from the left, then passes them to HostData.get_f64. A rank2 lhs[1,2] and rank3 rhs[2,2,1] producing[2,1,1] cause exact cached HostData.strided_index to index lhs strides[2] and panic. Expected dot products are23 and33. Same-rank ordinary and singleton-broadcast controls return those values correctly. Problem constructors support different ranks, but the claimed CPU ground truth has not migrated with that shape contract.
findings.status: documented, not repaired; scoped CPU witness where named, otherwise source/primary-contract finding

findings.title: Matmul batch-layout payload combines output-rank divisors with shorter operand-rank strides
findings.evidence: The host builder takes batch_shape from problem.out_batches and batch_strides only from handle.shape/strides before the last two axes. It zeroes existing singleton strides but does not left-pad missing axes. An unbatched rank2 operand against one output batch axis yields one divisor and no strides; a one-batch-axis operand against two output axes yields two divisors and one stride. Layout to_source_pos iterates every divisor and indexes the corresponding reversed stride. The exact host payload mismatch is reproduced; a scalar CPU interpretation of the layout body bounds-panics for both cases. Four same-rank/unbatched controls map offsets as expected. This is the kernel-layout side of the shape migration already exposed in CPU reference Q446.
findings.status: documented, not repaired; exact host payload witness and explicitly interpreted layout-body witness
findings.scope: Six CPU cases compile exact BatchLayoutLaunch::from_handle with shape-equivalent binding/problem/generated-launch DTO. to_source_pos is interpreted as CPU Rust after removing one #[unroll] attribute; Sequence/reversed/FastDivmod are explicit scalar doubles. A macro/compiler may reject mismatched sequences earlier; the precise device failure mode is unproved.

repair_triage.disposition: documented in read-only full-source audit

Reject incompatible extra axes explicitly. Keep logical batch index and byte/element offset meanings separate across normal and quantized argument paths.

findings.title: Copied partial cyclic strict-workload checks admit a vector starting at the stage length
findings.evidence: Both partial cyclic validators compute the last unit/task vector start and reject only max_position > num_stage_elements. A start exactly at the element count is already outside the stage. For63 vectors of4 elements with32 loading units, each unit receives2 tasks; final start252 equals a252-element stage and both exact validator bodies admit it. Strict execution takes the copy/store branch unconditionally despite balanced_workload=false. The full cyclic validators use divisibility and reject the same imbalance. Balanced64-vector controls pass;62-vector further-overrun controls reject. The sync/async copies share the defect rather than one delegating to a common scheduling check.

findings.title: Specialized GEMM and vector launchers reuse one operand rank for both operands
findings.evidence: Both derive rank from RHS then index LHS m/k with it and slice both batch lists at that rank. Valid [1,32]@[2,32,64] panics indexing LHS; reverse [2,1,32]@[32,64] reads m2,k1 instead of m1,k32 and drops batch information. GEMM GPU normalization also indexes RHS with LHS rank before this block, so reverse rank can panic even earlier. Generic batch construction already uses each own rank. Specialized Strategy entries catch InvalidConfig and fall back to SimpleUnit, but do not catch these panics; reverse-rank GEMV may be rescued by that error fallback. No silent wrong device result is claimed.

These are experimental implementation/admission gaps, not production default failures.

findings.title: Atomic split-cube benchmark retains accumulated output across warmups and samples
